title: Music in a Circle
description:
Educarer arranged the musical instruments in a circle for Hogan to explore and manipulate.


Hogan was sitting inside the circle and was invited by his educarer to play the instruments. “Hogan, look around you. So many instruments, right? Which one you want to play?” Hogan looked at her and smiled  happily. He excitedly crawled towards the egg shakers and grabbed them with his both hands. He shook the shakers , left to right. “Good shaking Hogan” educarer praised him. He giggled aloud and babbled “ah ah ah” in response. He then crawled towards the tambourine and used the shaker to hit it. Upon hearing the sound, he smiled and happily banged the instruments together. “Oh! The sound is getting louder.” Educarer added. Hogan giggled aloud while exploring the instruments. 
After a while, he crawled towards the hand bell shaker and grabbed it  with his right hand while his left hand was taking the rain stick. He manipulated both instruments, shaking them back and forth. With a wide smile on his face, he repeatedly shaking the instruments merrily. “Wow! Hogan, you look so happy shaking the instruments.” Educarer told him. “How about this?” Educarer asked while prompting him the cabasa. Hogan looked at her with a big smile. He excitedly took the cabasa from her educarer and explored hitting it on the tambourine. Hogan was smiling and eagerly explored all the instruments.
interpretation:
• Hogan displays enjoyment in playing and manipulating with materials. He showed strong interest in musical instruments and explored making sounds through hitting, shaking and banging the instruments. He was seen smiling giggling and babbling while exploring the instruments.
  • During exploration, Hogan enjoyed interactions with his educarer, too. He can respond and interact well with enjoyment.

learning_goals.title: Foster interactions between adult and child
Foster enjoyment in playing with toys and materials

title: 一起玩
description: 在团体游戏时间，小朋友们围坐在一个趣味玩具盘周围，颖悦率先伸手抓住了玩具。老师微笑着鼓励道：“颖悦，你可以试着把玩具插进圆盘中。”颖悦用手把玩具稳稳地插进圆盘，动作非常认真和专注。然后她又拿起一块玩具，准备继续插入圆盘。旁边的小朋友看到颖悦的动作，纷纷好奇地伸手模仿，有的去拿玩具，有的拿起玩具尝试把玩具插进圆盘中。老师适时引导道：“我们可以轮流来插玩具，看看谁能插的最多！”听到老师的话，颖悦和小朋友高兴地继续把玩具插进圆盘。整个过程中，颖悦和小朋友们不断分享玩具，开心地互相注视和微笑。
interpretation: 在这个团体互动游戏中，颖悦展示了强烈的社交兴趣，愿意和其他小朋友一起分享玩具，表现出信任和友善。老师的鼓励和语言引导增强了孩子之间的互动性，培养了他们的团队合作意识和社交能力。颖悦在活动中不仅体验了分享的乐趣，还进一步发展了手眼协调能力和专注力。

title: String Pulling
description:
Hogan was provided with a recycled paper tube with some strings on it for him to engage in string pulling.

Hogan was cruising along the bench. Educarer called and invited him, “Hogan, look! I have something for you.” while showing him the material. Hogan looked at her  and smiled. he then quickly crawled towards her. He sat down on the floor while facing the paper tube. Educarer handed him the material and invited him to grasp and pull. “Hogan let’s pull the string this way.” Educarer modelled the action. Hogan giggled in response. He pulled the paper tube nearer to him, in between his legs, and began exploring with the materials. He was eyeing for the blue string and and slowly laid his right hand on to it. He used his radial grasp to contact its end-point and then explored pulling it out. When the string got stuck, educarer encouraged him, “You can do it Hogan. Pull it harder”. Hogan used his strength and pulled it out. He was smiling when he successfully did it. “Good pulling Hogan”, educarer praised him. He giggled and clapped his hands in response. 
He then continued doing the activity. He was looking at the white string. He extended his left arm into the tube and used his pincer grasp to pick up the string and pulled it hard quickly. “Yay! Well done Hogan! You can pull the string well.” educarer applauded. Using his right hand and with a good radial grasp, he picked the red string and pulled it harder. He continued pulling most of the strings with good eye-hand coordination.
interpretation:
• Hogan displayed good hand-eye coordination skills while engaged in string pulling. He was able to grasp and contact the string and pulled it out.
  •  He also demonstrated  good pincer and radial grasp while holding on to the strings. His small muscles are developing very well.

learning_goals.title: Foster hand-eye coordination
Foster gross and fine motor development (sitting, crawling, rolling over, standing, holding, grasping, reaching etc.)

title: Spider Web Basket
description:
Hogan was engaged in “spider web basket” activity. The basket was covered with layered of strings and filled with sensory balls for him to retrieve and manipulate.

Hogan was sitting on the floor while playing with the ring shakers. Educarer called him while prompting him the materials, “Hogan, look! I have a basket of sensory balls. Come here.” Hogan turned his head towards the direction of his educarer. He smiled and quickly crawled towards her. He sat down beside the basket and placed his hands on top of the strings. “Hogan, let’s retrieve the balls out from the basket.” Hogan looked at her and smiled while babbling “ah ah ah”. He put his right hand inside the basket and tried pulling out the sensory ball but failed. “Oh! Oh! The balls are trapped. It’s okay Hogan. You can try it again.” Educarer motivated him. Hogan kept on trying. He grabbed the ball with a strong grip and manoeuvred his hand away from the strings and pulled his hand out harder. After many attempts, he managed to retrieve the ball. “Yay! You did it! Good grabbing Hogan.” Educarer praised him. 
He continued grabbing the balls. He grabbed the orange ball and pulled it harder. He was smiling and giggling when he managed to grab the ball out. He then excitedly shook and banged the balls together. “Hogan, there are some balls left in the basket. You can try to let them out”. Hogan smiled and slid his hands into the basket. He tried to pull but failed. He then held the basket and flipped it down causing the balls to almost come out from the layered strings. He then grabbed the balls out one by one. “Wow! That’s a very good idea Hogan! You retrieved all the balls out!”
interpretation:
• Hogan is able to stay focused and demonstrate sustained involvement while exploring the materials. 
  • He engaged in trial and error while working his hands through the different layers of strings while trying to reach and retrieve the sensory balls. 
  • Pulling the toys out was abit challenging for him, but with focus and concentration and engage in problem-solving-(finding ways on his own), he managed to retrieve the trapped balls out from the basket.

learning_goals.title: Children are confident, curious involved learners
Develop focus and concentration-sustained involvement
Develop opportunities for infants to make connections between actions and outcomes

title: 穿过圆环
description: 老师拿来了两个颜色鲜艳的圆环，一个黄色，一个蓝色，并微笑着对颖悦说：“颖悦，我们来玩穿过圆环的游戏吧！你准备好了吗？”颖悦看着老师，开心地点点头，迈着小步走向黄色圆环。老师把黄色圆环举在颖悦的面前，鼓励地说：“来，抬起脚，走过圆环！”颖悦稍稍停顿了一下，低头看了看自己的脚，然后慢慢地抬起一只脚，稳稳地迈过圆环。随后，老师将蓝色圆环移动到另一侧，边说：“太棒了！试试蓝色的圆环吧！”颖悦听后，很快调整方向，小心翼翼地穿过蓝色圆环。当她成功穿过两个圆环后，老师鼓掌说道：“颖悦真棒！再来一次试试看好吗？”颖悦听到鼓励，露出了满足的笑容，再次穿过圆环，动作变得更加流畅和自信。
interpretation: 在这个活动中，颖悦表现出对挑战新事物的兴趣和探索的勇气。通过穿过不同高度的圆环，她锻炼了手脚协调性和平衡能力。在老师的引导下，颖悦也展现了对指令的理解力和积极回应的能力。整个过程中，颖悦脸上始终洋溢着自信的微笑，表现出她对运动游戏的享受和成就感。

title: 翻看书本
description: 老师拿来了一本图画书递给颖悦，颖悦立刻被书吸引住，双手拿起书本，安静地坐下后，马上翻开书本。她的目光在书页上的一幅动物图画上停留，神情专注。老师微笑着指着画中的动物说：“这是一只驴子，它会踢后腿。”颖悦听得非常认真，不时抬头看向老师。接着，她用双手翻到下一页，兴奋地用小手指着一只猴子的图画。老师继续引导：“这是一只猴子，它会挥动手臂。你看，它的手臂是这样挥动的。”说着，老师做了一个挥动手臂的动作。颖悦似懂非懂地笑了，也动了动手臂。随后，她又兴致勃勃地翻到另一页，指着一只大猩猩的图片。老师说：“这是一只大猩猩，它会用手拍自己的胸脯。”
interpretation: 在这个看书过程中，颖悦非常享受这个听故事的乐趣，她能投入、持续的注意力，通过老师讲解理解了图画中的内容和词语之间的联系，培养了颖悦的聆听能力和理解能力，发展了颖悦的知识和认知范围，增强了颖悦对词语与图片、物体之间关系的意识。

interpretation: 在这个团体互动游戏中，天恩展示了强烈的社交兴趣，愿意和其他小朋友一起分享玩具，表现出信任和友善。老师的鼓励和语言引导增强了孩子之间的互动性，培养了他们的团队合作意识和社交能力。天恩在活动中不仅体验了分享的乐趣，还进一步发展了手眼协调能力和专注力。

title: 阳光隧道
description: 老师拿来了一个蓝色的爬行隧道放在活动区，天恩看到隧道后立刻被吸引了，他先趴在隧道入口处仔细观察，用小手轻轻地触摸隧道的布料，眼神里充满了好奇和兴奋。老师微笑着鼓励天恩：“试试看，你可以爬进去哦！” 天恩听到后，用双手支撑着身体，慢慢地向隧道里爬去。天恩一边爬行，一边观察老师的反应，看到老师鼓励的笑容，他露出了自信的笑脸，继续向前爬。最后成功地从隧道的另一端爬了出来。接着，天恩又兴奋地绕到隧道入口，主动再次爬了进去。这一次，他爬得更加熟练，动作也更加协调，老师在一旁继续鼓励他：“你真棒！再爬一次看看！” 天恩听到老师的鼓励，爬行的动作更加有力，速度也有所提升，表现出满满的自信和快乐。
interpretation: 在这个活动中，天恩通过多次爬行，不仅锻炼了四肢的力量，尤其是手臂和腿部的肌肉，也提升了身体的平衡感和协调能力。在穿越隧道的过程中，天恩学会了如何克服空间上的障碍，培养了对新环境的适应力和对探索活动的勇气。整个过程中，天恩表现出快乐、自信和积极向上的态度，充分展现了他良好的身体素质和勇于探索的精神。

title: 益智玩具
description: 老师拿来了一个颜色鲜艳的积木套柱玩具，放在天恩面前。老师微笑着说：“天恩，你看，这些积木有好多颜色，我们可以把它们套在柱子上，试试看吧！”天恩先拿起一个蓝色的积木块，仔细地观察后，将它套在绿色的柱子上。老师鼓励道：“哇，你选了蓝色的积木，套得真棒！还有其他颜色的积木哦，可以试试看。”随后，天恩继续从旁边的积木中挑选，拿起一个红色的积木块，尝试套在柱子上。积木一开始没对准柱子滑落了，老师温柔地说：“没关系，慢慢来，试着调整一下方向。”天恩听后，重新调整方向，终于成功地将积木套上了柱子。老师高兴地说：“太好了！这是红色的积木，你套得真棒！”
interpretation: 在这个活动中，天恩展现出高度的专注力和耐心，不断调整积木的方向来对准柱子。他不仅练习了手眼协调能力，也培养了他对颜色的初步感知，在活动过程中，通过老师的引导话语，使天恩随着每一次的尝试和成功，都表现出自信和满足，愉快地享受着游戏带来的成就感，同时在互动中进一步认识了积木的颜色和形状。

title: 手偶游戏
description: 在游戏互动时间，老师戴上了一只玩具小鸭手偶，挥动着小鸭的翅膀，温柔地呼唤着：“雅俊，快来看，小鸭子来找你玩啦！”雅俊听到呼唤，立刻抬起头，兴奋地迅速爬到老师面前。他的目光紧紧地追随着小鸭手偶，眼中满是好奇和期待。老师轻声笑着，用手偶装作小鸭的声音对雅俊说：“嘎嘎嘎，雅俊你好呀！”接着，老师开始唱起了一首欢快的儿歌：“小鸭子，一身黄，扁扁嘴巴红脚掌。嘎嘎嘎嘎高声唱，一摇一摆下池塘。”边唱边用手偶夸张地模仿小鸭摇摆、拍翅膀的动作。雅俊看得入迷，并被小鸭的动作逗乐了，不时发出咯咯的笑声。同时还伸手去触摸小鸭子玩偶。
interpretation: 在活动中雅俊对老师的呼唤迅速回应，体现出雅俊对老师的认可和依恋关系，游戏过程中雅俊不仅体验到了游戏的乐趣，还在感官、语言和社交多个方面获得了发展，同时与老师的情感联系也得到了进一步的加强。也表现出雅俊对于手偶玩具的喜爱。

title: 穿越小山洞
description: 老师在活动区放置了一个软垫小隧道，并有五颜六色的软条作为门帘。雅俊立刻被这个色彩鲜艳的场景吸引，趴在地上观察了一会儿，露出了好奇的神情。他用小手轻轻拨动橙色的软条，感受其触感，随后抬头看向老师。老师微笑着对雅俊说：“雅俊，你想试着钻进去看看吗？”雅俊听到后，两只手用力支撑起身体，慢慢地爬向隧道的入口，拨开软条后，小心翼翼地爬了进去。他一边爬行，一边看向老师，看到老师的鼓励眼神，他露出了兴奋的笑容。爬过隧道后，老师开心地对他说：“太棒了！雅俊真勇敢！你可以再爬一次吗？”雅俊听到后，快速绕到入口，迫不及待地再次钻进小房子。这次他的动作更加熟练，爬行速度也快了许多，并开心的露出了笑脸。
interpretation: 在这个活动中，雅俊通过反复爬行，锻炼了手臂和腿部的肌肉力量，提高了全身的协调性和平衡感。整个过程中，雅俊表现出快乐、自信和积极向上的态度，充分展现了他良好的身体素质和勇于探索的精神。

title: 音乐玩具
description: 老师拿来了一个音乐玩具给雅俊，雅俊好奇地用双手触摸和按动玩具上的按钮，探索着每一个机关。雅俊按下不同的按钮时，玩具会发出不同的声音或亮起不同的灯光，这让雅俊感到新奇和兴奋，不停地按动和尝试。老师在旁边引导雅俊，告诉雅俊：“这里有一个星星，你按一下就会唱儿歌。还有这上面有一只小狗，按下去会发出‘汪汪’的叫声。” 雅俊认真地听着老师的讲解，眼神专注地观察玩具上的变化，还会用手指着按钮尝试更多的操作。
interpretation: 在这个活动过程中，雅俊展现出了专注、持续的注意力，积极地探索和操作玩具，感受不同的声音、光线和结构变化。通过老师的引导，雅俊进一步理解了按键和结果之间的联系，发展了因果认知能力，同时也锻炼了手指的小肌肉动作，提升了手眼协调能力。

title: 一月份，认识自己。（PTC)
description:
老师与他一起互动玩转圈圈活动，然后叫他爬去镜子区域，照一照镜子，看一看镜子的他。
他听懂老师的指示，手拿了一个圈圈很快的爬过去，看一看镜子的他。
老师问：'你帅吗？‘
他再看镜子的他，看了蛮久的，然后，老师帮他把圈圈带在头上面。
他一只手摸着镜子，马上转头看老师。
老师再问他：’你帅不帅？‘
他马上转头看镜子，而且用手指指着镜子的他，回应老师；“他帅！”
他不只达到自我认识的发展，更达到社会行为发展的目标，好棒!

title: 吹泡泡
description: 老师手拿着泡泡管笑着对刚刚吃完了午餐的芸西说：“我们去吹泡泡好不好？”说着，老师把手伸向了她，芸西抬头微笑着看向老师对着老师抬起了右手，于是，老师握住她的手后牵着她来到了游戏角落。老师邀请芸西坐在老师对面后，把泡泡棒举在她的嘴前用鼓励的话语对她说：“我们要开始吹泡泡了，芸西，吹！用嘴巴吹气，泡泡就会出来。”依旧面带微笑的她马上抿住嘴对着泡泡棒吹了一口气，随着这口气泡泡棒上连接鼓起了三个泡泡飞了出去，在老师的表现声中她含笑低了一下头，马上抬起双手臂连拍了三次手。之后，在整个3-4分钟的活动期间，她有好几次的把气吹去上方把额头的头发吹的飞扬起来的情况下，也大概5-6次向前吹气吹出了泡泡。
interpretation: 芸西在游戏过程中能持续参与游戏，并且表现出了自豪、开心、享受和轻松，她享受了活动。她知道自己的名字及老师话语的意思，在语句提示下基本掌握了只有吹气才会有泡泡出来的因果关系。

title: 新年红
description: 老师邀请恩熙来到了游戏区面对面的坐了下来后，把一盘红色的活动材料放在她的面前。老师首先把一根红色的毛线递向她，说到：“恩熙，红红火火的新年要到了！摸一摸红色软软的毛线！”双手扶在腿上坐立着恩熙先抬头看了看老师手中的线，约3-4秒钟后她抬起右手张开手指拿过了线，她随即低下头转睛看向了右手拿着的线，在看的同时她微微动了动五指捏了捏线，就这样反复抓捏了约5-6秒钟后她松开了抓握着线的手指，眼睛看向了面前的其它材料。之后，老师先后递给了她网兜苹果和红包灯笼，她都接了过去并抓捏和看了它们。
interpretation: 恩熙享受了活动，并与活动材料进行了互动，比如：她先后抓捏了毛线、苹果和灯笼，通过活动促进她对红色活动材料的喜欢。

title: 一月第二周：探索软布卡上的动物 （Update )
description:
老师拿出三片颜色亮丽的软布卡片，卡片上分别有大象、狗和猫的图片，放在筠心面前。筠心对这些鲜艳的软布卡片很感兴趣，伸出小手去抓弄卡片，把它们弄乱。老师微笑着整理卡片，并逐一介绍动物的名称：“这是大象，大象会‘噢噢’叫！这是小狗，小狗会‘汪汪’叫！这是小猫，小猫会‘喵喵’叫！”
荺心专注地看着软布卡片，认真地听老师说话。虽然筠心只有六个月大，但当老师问：“猫猫在哪里？”筠心似乎听懂了，伸手去拉出猫的软布卡片。老师立刻给予鼓励：“哇！你找到猫猫了！真棒！”并继续引导筠心探索其他软布卡片，通过语言互动和动作鼓励，帮助筠心发展对词语与图片、物体之间关系的意识，能指认图片和物体。

title: Threading!
description:
Jenna was invited to thread using straws and pipe cleaners. She inserted a pink straw into the brown pipe cleaner. She began by holding the pink straw with her right hand and the brown pipe cleaner with her left hand. She coordinated her eyes and hands to bring the straw to the tip of the pipe cleaner. 

Then, Jenna coordinated her left hand to push the straw while her right hand held onto the pipe cleaner. As she do so, she slowly adjusted her wrist to accommodate the moving straw. When she successfully threaded, she gave a smile! Afterwards, she repeated it with the green straw.
interpretation: Jenna coordinated her eyes and hands to fit the straw into the pipe cleaner. Additionally, she persisted until she successfully threaded the straws into the pipe cleaner.

title: 美丽的烟花
description:
描述：
       为了渲染节日的气氛，我们要做美术活动——烟花。教师准备若干张黑色的卡纸，黄色和红色的颜料，若干根剪好的吸管，然后教师向幼儿介绍活动流程，请幼儿自由操作。
       歆淯坐在桌子前，她拿起吸管蘸取颜料，然后将颜料拓印在黑色的卡纸上，教师问道：“歆淯，吸管上是什么颜色呀？”歆淯回答：“颜色”。教师纠正歆淯是黄色，歆淯复述“黄色”。歆淯又用吸管蘸取红色的颜料，将红色的颜料拓印在黑色的卡纸上，过了一会儿，黑色卡纸已经拓印满了，歆淯指着卡纸说道：“我做好了。（用英语），” 教师回应歆淯说道：“你做完了呀！你的烟花做的很好看哦。”歆淯看着教师笑了。
interpretation:
诠释：

歆淯在活动过程中，能够坚持完成活动，将黑色的卡纸涂满颜色；她也能复述教师说的话，；也能够独立完成美术活动作品。特别棒！

title: "Can you watch our concert?"
description:
Livia was playing at the music corner with Keian. She was hitting on the drum and singing the song "Jingle Bell" together with Keian. She went over to the other side of the classroom and invited the teacher over to the music corner and said "Ms. Fang Min! You want to watch our concert? We are very good you know." 

Ms. Fang Min agreed and sat down by the side and watched them performed. Livia took the drumsticks out and hit the drums in a steady beat and sang to "Jingle Bell" loudly with Keian.
interpretation: Livia was able to recognise elements of music through singing and playing of percussion instruments. She was also able to hit the drums steadily to the beat.

title: My Favourite Activity
description:
Children shared about the various activity they can do together as a family - playing games, going to the beach and etc. Elizabeth shared that she enjoys playing with her younger sister when she goes to the playground. 

Elizabeth started her drawing by drawing the slide. She used shapes and lines to represent the slide, swing set and see-saw. She also used various circles and triangles to represent herself and Lauren as well. Elizabeth also used different colours to colour her playground. 

"I like to play in the playground with my meimei."
interpretation: Elizabeth was able to use elements of art to represent ideas - various shapes for the equipment at the playground and using lines as ladders. She was also able to observe her surrounding well and expressed them out in lines and shapes.

title: 一月第三周：转一转 （Update）
description:
老师将蝴蝶形状的吸盘旋转玩具吸附在镜子上，轻轻转动，鲜艳的色彩和旋转的动作立刻吸引了筠心的目光。他专注地盯着那只“飞舞”的蝴蝶，过了一会儿，才慢慢伸出小手，轻轻触摸玩具.
随后，老师将玩具吸附在软垫上，让筠心更方便触摸。看到玩具在地上旋转，小手尝试去抓住它。当手掌碰到玩具时，筠心停下片刻，露出了好奇而满足的小表情，随后发出了一声清脆的笑声、充满了探索的乐趣.

title: Black and white high contrast flashcard
description: To get Hanzal’s attention, the educator first spoke to him, and he responded with a smile. Then, the educator placed a black-and-white high-contrast flashcard in front of him for him to reach. The flashcard also made a crispy sound, which Hanzal could hear as he grabbed and folded it. While he was exploring and interacting with the flashcard, the educator continued to talk to him, describing the images on the card. Throughout this, Hanzal was engaged in observing, exploring, and listening to both the educator's voice and the crispy sound from the flashcard.
interpretation: Through the activities, Hanzal demonstrated his ability to feel and express enjoyment, evident in his bright smile. He seemed to truly enjoy the interactions with his educator as she spoke to him, guiding him through the activities. As he explored the material, he engaged his senses of touch and hearing, responding to both the texture of the objects and the educator’s voice. Additionally, he used his locomotor skills to approach the materials, showing his growing coordination and curiosity.

title: Roll over.
description: Before turning 3 months, Hanzal showed interest in rolling over. With a little assistance and encouragement by the educarer, he was able to roll on his tummy while lying on one side. The educarer also used toys to encourage Hanzal from rolling over. The educarer will place toys next to him to get his attention and he would roll towards the side to get closer.
interpretation: In his first month of school, before turning 3 months old, Hanzal showed significant improvement in his muscle tone, allowing him to lie on his side for several minutes before rolling onto his tummy. He was also able to briefly lift his head to look at his educator and intentionally move his head to follow them within his visual field. This is an excellent milestone, and he’s right on track as he approaches 3 months.

learning_goals.title: Foster coordination of body part movements

title: Counting ducks
description: The educator placed several big and small ducks in front of Hanzal. As she counted, she lifted the ducks one by one, as Hanzal lifted his head to track them. Even when the ducks were placed to the side, Hanzal was able to shift his body and reach out for them. The educator also pointed out the two different sizes of the ducks, showing him the contrast. When the ducks were placed closer to him, he seemed to prefer reaching out and grabbing the smaller ones.
interpretation: This activity demonstrated that Hanzal is able to follow movement from side to side, adjusting his body direction based on where the ducks are placed. He showed circular reactions, using more advanced motor skills, such as reaching out toward the ducks. Hanzal also explored the toys by applying existing schemas, like grasping the ducks. He seemed to enjoy the experience, actively looking at and listening to his educator while tracking the movement of the ducks.

title: 萧义泽入园更新
description:
亲爱的义泽爸爸妈妈：

您们好！

首先，感谢你们对我们幼儿学步班全体教师的信任和支持。义泽宝贝加入我们的幼儿学步班已经有两多星期了的时间了，看到他逐渐的开始适应新的环境及教师同伴等，我们由衷为他感到开心！

义泽早上来学校时是哭着进来的，这是很正常的幼儿入园与父母分离时的表现，不用太过担心。当进入课室后，他有时会哭一小会儿，在教师的陪伴和安慰下他会很快停止哭泣。义泽偶尔会表现出有些许不安，他喜欢拿着自己的小书包。义泽与班级教师已经建立起良好的信任依恋关系，当听到其他同伴哭泣时，他会主动走到教师面前要抱抱。我们将继续关注义泽的情绪变化，及时给予安慰和支持，帮助他更好地应对周围环境的变化。随着对幼儿园环境和课室环境逐渐熟悉起来，义泽现在大多数时间已经能够较为独立的主动去探索周围的玩具和设施。义泽与班级其他同伴的关系还在建立中，有时他会拿着小书包一个人静静观察同伴，有时他也会走到同伴身边看同伴在玩些什么，然后在教师的下一起参与活动。在教师开展大组活动时，义泽能主动参与活动，他尤其喜欢和大家一起进行音乐律动活动和听教师讲故事绘本。义泽也开始逐渐熟悉幼儿园的每日流程。当教师解释接下来要做什么后，他会在教师的引导下和同伴一起去做，例如：自己拿水壶喝水，自己拿书包去厕所等。非常棒！

义泽很喜欢去游乐场探索，他已经会尝试和同伴一起玩不同的体育器材了。他尤其喜欢玩球和洞洞板游戏，偶尔也会尝试坐在三轮车上走一小会儿。

吃饭和午睡方面，义泽都表现得很好。他可以自己拿着汤匙吃饭，有时还会跟教师要第二碗。义泽也很喜欢吃水果。吃完饭后，他可以在教师的引导下自己去把餐具放到篮子里，非常棒呢！午睡方面，义泽喝完牛奶在教师的陪伴下会很快安稳入睡。他一般会睡一个半小时到两个小时左右。醒来后，他基本不会哭闹，会观察教师和同伴在做什么，然后主动走到教师身边寻求陪伴。

这里是义泽最近在学校时的日常生活及活动照片，展示着他在适应新环境、与小朋友互动以及学习新技能等方面都取得了显著的进步。期待接下来的日子里，义泽能更加适应学校生活，并喜欢我们的学校生活。宝贝加油！！！

最后，再次感谢您对我们工作的支持与配合。如果您有任何疑问或建议，请随时与我们联系。让我们携手合作，共同为义泽的健康成长创造良好的条件！

祝好！

幼儿学步班全体教师

首先，感谢你们对我们幼儿学步班全体教师的信任和支持。献正宝贝加入我们的幼儿学步班已经有两多星期了的时间了，看到他逐渐的开始适应新的环境及教师同伴等，我们由衷为他感到开心！

献正在早上入园时已经很少哭闹，表现出较好的适应能力。他会在班级教师的陪伴下吃少量的早餐。进入课室后，他情绪也很稳定，在教师的陪伴下会主动到兴趣的区角进行探索，表现出强烈的好奇心。当班级有其他幼儿哭闹时，献正会被同伴的情绪影响，有时会表现出不安。献正与班级教师已经建立了良好的信任依恋关系，当他感到不安时，会寻求教师抱抱他。在教师的安抚下他会逐渐恢复安全感继续去探索角落游戏或继续参与大组活动。我们将继续关注献正的情绪变化，及时给予安慰和支持，帮助他更好地应对周围环境的变化。当教师组织大组活动时，献正也开始慢慢融入，会和教师一起将自己的小照片粘贴到出席班上。献正比较喜欢音乐律动和讲故事绘本的活动。当进行美工活动，如：玩橡皮泥和玩颜料时，献正开始不愿意触碰，需要教师耐心引导和鼓励后他才会慢慢尝试。献正与班级同伴的关系正在建立中，他会观察班级其他同伴在玩些什么，偶尔也会主动过去一起参与活动。我们将引导献正与其他小朋友进行更多的互动，帮助他学会分享和合作。

饮食方面：献正的饮食习惯正在逐步改善。有时候需要教师喂食，但大部分时间他可以自己拿着小勺子吃饭。他最喜欢吃的水果是香蕉，对其他水果兴趣不大。我们会继续鼓励献正尝试不同的食物，增加他对多样食物的兴趣。

午睡方面：献正的午睡情况非常好，能在喝完奶后在教师的陪伴下独立入睡。他午睡时长一般是一个半小时到两个小时左右。起床后献正也不会哭闹，他会静静地坐在自己的小床上观察教师和同伴们在做什么。在教师的引导下，他开始慢慢学习把自己的睡觉包放回柜子里。非常棒！

献正非常喜欢去游乐场玩，特别是玩球类游戏和洞洞板游戏。在教师的引导和协助下，他有时也会坐在三轮车上行走，展现出较强的运动兴趣。最值得惊喜的是献正现在不仅在室内可以牵着教师的手走路，连户外活动时他也愿意配合牵着教师的手自己走，还尝试和同伴一起牵着甜甜圈牵引绳走。非常棒！我们会继续鼓励他锻炼自己走路。
总的来说，李献正在幼儿园的表现非常令人满意。这里是献正最近在学校时的日常生活及活动照片，我们会持续关注他的成长和发展，希望他能在这里获得更多的乐趣和学习机会。最后，再次感谢您对我们工作的支持与配合。如果您有任何问题或建议，欢迎随时与我们联系。

祝好，

幼儿学步班全体教师

title: Safe and Sound
description:
Pretending to be a squirrel, Ava had to run to the trees (hula hoops) to hide from the hunter. As the woodcutter chopped off the trees, her friends had fewer trees to run to. One of her friends approached her and asked if he could join her. With the teacher's guidance, Ava nodded and gestured for him to join her in the hula hoop.

Afterwards, Ava spotted another friend who did not have any trees to hide in. She called out to her, "Come!" Her friend entered the hula hoop and thanked her. With that, the teacher announced that they were all safe from the hunter and everyone cheered!
interpretation: Ava fostered empathy and a sense of sharing by inviting friends who do not have a safe place to hide with her. She recognized that fostering a positive relationship with others begins with pro-social behaviours. Hence, she communicated using approriate social skills to ask them to join her. Additionally, Ava fostered a sense of belonging, recognizing there are others other than herself.

When the song played, Emma began to sing along with her friends, "small, small, small, and big, big, big," making the circle small and big. She looked at her friends and laughed.

When it came to making the circle up and down, Emma took the lead to sit down and looked out for friends who did not know what to do. She spotted Emmanuel and said, "Emmanuel, down, down, down! Sit down!" Emmanuel followed. As the song came to an end, Emma smilingly waved at her friends and said, "Hello!"

title: Pegging
description: Ava was invited to peg onto the laundry rack. She picked up a blue peg and held it with her right hand. Using her right thumb and right index finger to press it open, she coordinated her eyes and hand to bring the peg to the laundry rack. As she do so, she slowly adjusted her right wrist in the orientation of the rack. Then, Ava released her thumb and index finger, successfully pegging onto the laundry rack. Afterwards, she repeated it with the pink peg.
interpretation: Ava coordinated her eyes and hands to peg onto the laundry rack. She displayed strength in her fingers to peg. Additionally, she persisted until she successfully completed the task.

title: Threading
description:
Maeve was invited to thread using straws and pipe cleaners. She inserted a pink straw into the brown pipe cleaner. She began by holding the pink straw with her right hand and the brown pipe cleaner with her left hand. She coordinated her eyes and hands to bring the straw to the tip of the pipe cleaner. 

Then, Maeve coordinated her left hand to push the straw while her right hand held onto the pipe cleaner. As she do so, she slowly adjusted her wrist to accommodate the moving straw. When she successfully threaded, she gave a smile! Afterwards, she repeated it with another pink straw.
interpretation: Maeve coordinated her eyes and hands to fit the straw into the pipe cleaner. Additionally, she persisted until she successfully threaded the straws into the pipe cleaner.

title: Matching Cutlery Set
description:
While exploring the dramatic space, Maeve was encouraged to match the cutlery on the placemat. Maeve looked at the placemat and picked up a yellow spoon. The teacher asked, "Where are you matching it to?" Maeve looked at the placemat, and said, "Here!" 

Next, Maeve picked up the orange knife and matched it. Later, she looked at the placemat and said, "I need bowl." The teacher asked, "What colour will the bowl be?" Maeve looked at the cutlery, chose the blue bowl, and said, "blue!"  Subsequently, she was able to match the cutlery on other placemats independently.
interpretation: Maeve displayed sustained involvement in the task and was able to persist until she finished matching the cutlery on the placemat. She distinguished the differences between the cutlery and colours, and matched them accordingly. While doing so, she understood and comprehended the teacher's spoken language and questions.

title: Avery at School!
description: These are a few photos of Avery adjusting to and exploring a new environment—school. On her first week, she was exploring the routines at school, trying to follow her friends and teacher. She cries often and seeks attention from her parents and grandma. On the second week, she started playing with her friends in the kitchen and would stop crying from time to time. She also ate the school food and sat on the chair together with her friends. She joined classes with her friends and explored other areas at school, such as the playground and the space at level two. On the third week, she was able to recognize some of her friends names and would play with them at times. She would call her teacher's name when she needed help. She likes hugs and holding hands.
interpretation: Avery was able to slowly adjust to the school routine, though most of the time, she cried. She somehow managed to calm down when the teacher would hold her hand or hug her. She was also able to play alongside friends during playground time and would help to clean up a few toys in class. She enjoys a small group and would often play with a smaller circle of friends.

title: Walking Walking
description: Declan was invited by his teacher to walk around the classroom and was encouraged to collect a toy phone from the floor. Initially, Declan walked with assistance from his teacher, who gradually eased off by letting go of his arm without him realizing. Over time, Declan made a few steps on his own and independently walked to collect the toy phone before sitting on the mat. Later, Declan pointed to the storybooks, and the teacher encouraged him to walk over and pick one up. With support, Declan walked again, and once more, the teacher slowly released his arm. Declan continued to walk independently, successfully making his way to the library space.
interpretation: From this observation, it is clear that Declan is taking small steps towards walking independently, following the challenge set by his teacher. However, he seems hesitant, likely due to a fear of falling. With continued encouragement and support, he will build confidence and be able to overcome his fear. Well done, Declan—keep up the great effort!

title: 定廷入园情况更新
description:
亲爱的定廷家长：
你们好！
定廷来到我们的班级已经两个星期了。在这两个星期当中很欣慰看到定廷在逐步适应学校的生活。
在她进入课室的时候，虽然带着对父母不舍的情绪，但是她缓和情绪的时间越来越短。她在教师的安慰下会很快加入小组活动，或者自己去角落探索。 

定廷现在开始熟悉常规活动，会听老师的指令，老师说喝水的时间到了，她会拿着水壶坐在垫子上和同伴一起喝水。她的独立性很强，在午休的时候，她会主动去拿睡袋自己铺床垫，然后抱着抱枕躺下去，老师拍几下便很快入睡。看得出来她在学校的睡眠越来越安稳了。睡醒之后也不会嚷着找父母，她会做一些安静的操作游戏。她能够在一边专注很久玩游戏直到同伴起床。我相信再过一段时间，她的睡眠时间也会更迟久更安稳。

她在学校的胃口很棒，特别是下午茶点的时候，她会一直跟老师要牛奶。她喜欢吃包子,馒头还有面包，会一直跟老师说还要。 虽然在午休的时候她不要喝奶，但是在下午茶的时候，她会喝很多的牛奶。

她现在能够叫出班里面一些小朋友的名字了，会和同伴一起玩，也开始分享手里面的玩具给同伴。她很喜欢帮助别人，会主动帮老师送水壶给同伴，也会把同伴的水壶放到他们的柜子里面，还会帮老师放同伴的睡袋在柜子里面。
interpretation:
老师相信再过一两周这样的时间，她能够完全的融入到学校的生活当中，也请家长继续配合我们，给她更多的信心，相信她会一天比一天更棒！

title: Let's create bubbles.
description: Educarer places a plastic container filled with bubbles and water infront of Elijah and demonstrates by gently scooping up a handful of bubbles with her hand. As soon as Elijah sees this, he eagerly follows suit, placing both of his hands into the bubble-filled pool and starts scooping up the bubbles. In the process, he accidentally splashes some water onto his face, but instead of being upset or discomfort, he begins splashing the water everywhere, having an absolute blast.
interpretation:
Through cause and effect, Elijah explores how his actions create reactions, and he delights in the results of splashing the bubble water. This activity helps him maintain interest and curiosity for several minutes before bath time. By accidentally splashing the pool of bubbles, Elijah begins to understand how different actions can affect one another—when he splashes, water splashes out instead of just the bubbles.

Elijah also demonstrates problem-solving skills, using sensorimotor schemas, such as quickly moving his hand to create more bubbles with the guidance of his Educarer. This not only helps him grasp the concept of cause and effect but also strengthens his awareness of how his actions influence the environment around him.

Through this bubble exploration, Elijah learns how to create more bubbles by interacting with objects in new and inventive ways, understanding what actions will make the bubbles appear. He shows keen observation, staying focused when his Educarer demonstrates, and follows simple instructions with ease.

title: 印象最深刻的画面
description:
新学期的第一周，孩子们学习了绘本《奥莉薇》。故事的主人公是一只小猪，它擅长很多事情，但是最擅长的事情就是把人累昏，甚至常常把自己也累昏。它会涂妈妈的口红、穿上妈妈的高跟鞋照镜子，还会吓唬弟弟。要是出门，它还会把所有的衣服都拿出来穿一遍。晴天时，它会去海边，它会把自己晒成一条大热狗；而下雨天，她则会去参观美术馆。她喜欢直接走到德加的《芭蕾排练》面前，幻想自己将来有一天也能够在大大的舞台表演。不过，也有一幅画它怎么也看不懂。回家，它就在墙上画了起来。

title: 摇铃摇起来
description:
老师在和祥宏互动时，拿出一个摇铃在祥宏面前摇晃，祥宏看到后就伸左手过来抓住摇铃，老师放开摇铃，祥宏用左手抓握摇铃放在眼前看，然后又伸出右手拿过摇铃，之后双手一起抓握还有意或无意的摇晃，摇铃发出铃铃的声音，听到老师的表扬和鼓励，祥宏还会同时和老师对视露出笑容，祥宏玩的很开心。
 活动中体现祥宏的手眼协调在持续发展，也可把物体左手右手交换，达到五个月幼儿发展里程碑。恭喜祥宏，我们会继续加油！

learning_goals.title: 通过提供适宜的玩具和材料，培养婴幼儿对玩具和材料的喜爱
发展手眼协调能力，如：能用五指抓物品
通过精心的环境创设，发展视觉能力，如：会注视悬挂在床上的玩具并将手伸向玩具；在婴幼儿面前将物品全部盖起或藏起来时，能寻找物品

title: 小小设计师
description:
教师邀请幼儿回忆奥莉薇的不同穿着，然后出示图片，邀请幼儿观察和讨论奥莉薇的不同装扮，哪一件是自己最喜欢的。教师和幼儿一起讨论大家平时的衣服和装扮，鼓励幼儿用语言描述出来，并请他们说说自己觉得哪种款式的服装最漂亮。     
       教师为幼儿提供图画纸、铅笔、剪刀、胶水以及不同质地的材料。教师鼓励幼儿发挥想象力，自由选择他们喜欢的材料和工具进行创作。教师请幼儿在图画纸上画出自己的脸，然后剪贴布料为自己设计衣服，以展示自己最漂亮的模样。（实现了来创造领域的“运用观察和想象力创作平面和立体的艺术作品”以及来动吧领域的“能利用小肌肉技能使用小设备”学习成果）。

title: 手工奥莉薇
description:
教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。
媖绮拿到粘土后，她问教师：“这个是什么颜色？”教师告诉她是‘肤色’或者‘肉色’。她听后复述到：“肉色。”她又问：“老师，这个怎么放到鸡蛋上？”教师邀请她先把粘土揉成一个球，她一边揉，一边问：“这样对吗？”教师点点头，然后为她演示，将圆形的粘土在桌子上摊开，并告诉她就像和做印度煎饼一样。她笑着说：“我在做印度煎饼。”然后她用双手把粘土压扁，然后将粘土的边缘往外推。待她将推好的粘土贴到塑料鸡蛋上后，教师递给她一个报纸卷。她问道：“这个是什么。”教师将实先做好的奥莉薇模型举起来给她看，请她猜测用途。她观察了一下模型，说：“我知道了，是鼻子，对吗？”教师点点头示意她对了。
interpretation: 媖绮能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等，发挥自己的想象力制作属于自己的奥莉薇。

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（听）- 听指令：能完全理解3个口头指示并完成任务。
语言学习成果（说）- 交谈：能够积极主动地用华语表达，态度自然。

恺骏将粘土揉成一团，然后在桌上展开。他先用双手手掌将粘土压扁，然后向外推开。他一边推一边笑着说：“看，我在做Roti Prata。”他将压好的粘土贴到透明鸡蛋上。然后用手指按压和推挤不平整的地方。教师将一个报纸卷递给他，请他猜测用来做什么。他想了想，说：“嗯，是Nose。”教师问他Nose华文是什么，他说道：“是鼻子。”教师点头示意他猜对了。教师邀请他像刚刚一样制作一个小的印度卷饼将报纸卷包起来。他制作好后，将包好的报纸卷粘贴到塑料鸡蛋偏上的地方。他将鼻子装好后，用在教师的引导下将手做好贴在奥莉薇身上。他告诉教师：“我要黑色的眼睛。”说完，他拿取来一些黑色粘土，然后揉成两个小球粘贴到奥莉薇脸上。
interpretation: 恺骏能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: 我喜欢...
description: 在学习绘本《 奥莉薇》 的过程中， 肇祯对于故事很感兴趣， 她仔细地阅读绘本故事， 并且尝试和我沟通。通过沟通， 我请她说说他最喜欢的故事的情节， 肇祯想了想， 告诉我说：“ 我喜欢奥莉薇在美术馆的这幅画， 因为我也喜欢去美术馆。” 。 听了他的答案之后， 我便问他：“ 如果请你用绘画的方式表达出来， 你会怎样画呢？” 他看了看我， 想了想， 说到：“ 我会画奥莉薇和她的妈妈， 还有她的弟弟一起在美术馆， 这边有几幅画。”
interpretation: 通过肇祯的回答，可以看出肇祯的回复具有逻辑性， 说明他能够准确地理解老师问句的含义， 也能够使用清晰明确有逻辑的语句来表达自己的想法。 通过他和老师的对话， 也能够看出， 他能够自信流利地使用华语来和别人沟通。

家乐接过教师手里的粘土，教师告诉他粘土是肉色，也是肤色。他复述道：“肤色。”然后他开始揉搓粘土，他将粘土揉成球后放置到桌上用手按压。之后，他问道：“How to do，你可以帮我吗？”教师为他示范如何将压扁的粘土向四周展开。他看后，用手慢慢的推挤粘土，他一边推，一边问：“是这样吗？”教师点点头并鼓励他很棒。他将粘土摊成一个‘大饼’后，将粘土放置到塑料鸡蛋上制作奥莉薇的身体。他指着鸡蛋上空白的地方问教师：“这个怎么做？”教师请他按压粘土，并将多余的粘土推挤到空白处。他一边看教师的示范，一边跟着做。待他将奥莉薇的身体制作完成后，教师递给他一个报纸卷。他问教师：“这个是做什么？”教师拿起制作好的奥莉薇模型请他猜测，他看了看，说：“我知道了，是nose。”教师问他nose的华文是什么。他说：“是鼻子。”在教师的引导下，他用同样的方式包裹好了报纸卷，制作了奥莉薇的鼻子。
interpretation: 家乐能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: 手工奥莉薇
description:
教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。
思婷告诉教师：“我想要做奥莉薇。”教师将肉的粘土递给她，她说：“我知道这个，是肉色。”教师点点头示意她对了，然后告诉她将粘土摊成一个‘大饼’的方法。她听后，将粘土放到桌上揉搓成球，然后按压粘土，并沿着粘土的边缘将中间的粘土往四周推挤。之后，她将粘土饼覆盖到透明鸡蛋上制作奥莉薇的身体。她指着鸡蛋上的空白处，问道：“这里怎么做？”教师邀请她推挤鸡蛋上粘土厚重的地方，直到将空白填满。她听后点点头，开始制作起来。她用同样的方式制作了奥莉薇的鼻子，再制作了奥莉薇的四肢。她告诉教师我想要粉色的鼻子，教师告诉她是鼻孔。她复述道：“我想要粉色的鼻孔。"教师邀请她将一小块粉色粘土分成两半，揉成小球贴到奥莉薇的鼻子上。接着，她有用粉色粘土制作了艾莉薇的衣服。她说道：“我想放花在头上。”她拿起一些红色粘土问教师：“怎么做花呢？”教师引导她将粘土揉成一个小的圆形，然后折叠圆形的边缘，再在中心放一个小的黄色做为花的花蕊。她拿来一点绿色，说：“这个是叶子。”说完，她将绿色粘到花的根部。
interpretation: 思婷能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: 颜色排序
description:
教师带领幼儿观察一些不同风格的绘画作品，鼓励他们细心观察。通过讨论，引导他们注意颜色的不同层次。例如，画面中有些部分使用了明亮的色调，而其他部分则使用了较深的颜色。从而引出颜色深浅的概念。教师出示色块，请幼儿观察这些颜色，带领他们从深到浅或从浅到深排列这些色块。之后，教师请幼儿创作色彩排序画，鼓励幼儿使用水彩颜料，按照从深到浅或者从浅到深的顺序选择颜料盘里的颜色，绘制出自己喜欢的图形进行排序。最后，教师邀请幼儿选择一种排序方式，将6张深浅不一的色卡按照选择的方式进行排序。
嘉乐问道：“Is it from dark to light?"教师告诉他dark是深，light是浅。他复述道：“Dark深，light浅，从深到浅。”教师邀请他从水彩颜料盘里选择5个颜色，进行深浅排序。他指着色彩盘里的蓝色看向教师，教师告诉他可以，但是下一个颜色要比这个颜色更浅。他蘸取一些蓝色，他一边画一边说：“Rabbit。”教师问他华文是什么。他说：“兔子。”教师夸他真棒。他笑着有蘸取了一些红色画到蓝色的前面。教师问他红色深还是蓝色深，他抿着嘴笑着不回答。教师告诉他是蓝色深，所以红色应该在蓝色的后面。他点点头，继续选颜色。等他完成绘制后，教师出示两个白板，介绍上面写的排序要求。嘉乐指着从浅到深说：“这个。”教师告诉他是从浅到深，他复述道：“从浅到深。”他拿起卡片看了看，教师告诉他白色是浅色。他将白色放在最前面，接着是黄色、绿色、粉红色。教师提醒他仔细观察绿色和粉红色哪个更浅，他看了看，将绿色和粉红色的位置调换了一下。
interpretation: 嘉乐通过观察绘画作品学习颜色的变化，学会了区分颜色的深浅。在教师的引导下，通过动手实践，选取色彩盘里的颜色和色卡按照要求排序，加深了对颜色深浅的理解，逐渐培养了对艺术作品色彩运用的感知力。

title: "Scooping and Pouring of Caps into Muffin Tray"
description:
Jovelle is sitting on the floor, with the materials displayed in front of her. When the educarer demonstrated to her by scooping the food pouch caps from the bowl and poured it to the muffin tray, she tentatively observed the educarer actions.

When it was her turn to do the activity, she held the spoon with her right hand and scooped two of the food pouch caps, while moving her hand towards the muffin tray, she poured out the food pouch caps and it dropped to the floor. She responded by saying “Oh, oh” when she saw the food pouch caps on the floor. She picked it up and placed it into the muffin tray. When the educarer reminded her to use the spoon, she smiled at the educarer and continued to scoop again.

This time, she scooped one food pouch cap and slowly lowered her spoon and poured it into the muffin tray. Next, she scooped the food pouch caps again and moved her spoon to the empty muffin tray slots. She continued to scoop and pour the rest of the food pouch caps from the bowl to the muffin tray. When she had none, she showed with her hands “No more”. When the educarer asked her, “Would you like to do the activity again?”, she nodded her head and said “Hmm” softly.
interpretation: Jovelle was able to get herself involved in scooping and pouring activity. She was able to use her spoon to scoop the food pouch caps from the bowl and transferred them to the muffin tray. As she went scooping and pouring, she showed persistence in pouring the food pouch caps into the muffin tray slots. At first attempt, the food pouch caps scattered to the floor and she picked them up and placed them in the muffin tray. She continued to scoop and transfer the food pouch caps and showed the willingness to try again. She also communicates “no more” with a hand gesture and a nod as a communication skill.

learning_goals.title: Develop focus and concentration-sustained involvement

title: "Pom poms on Christmas Tree"
description:
Jovelle is sitting on the floor with a tray of colourful pom poms and a picture of a Christmas tree that has velcro dots attached. She picked one of the colourful pom poms and held it in her hands. She manipulated the pom pom, turning it over and squeezing gently with her fingers. She then placed back into the tray and picked another pom pom from the tray and repeated the same actions.

When the educarer prompted her to place it on the velcro dot of the Christmas tree, she moved her hands and carefully placed it down. She then picked another pom pom from the tray and placed it on a velcro dot. When the pom pom moved away from the velcro dot, she placed it back again on the velcro dot and pressed it gently. She continued to pick another pom pom and place the pom poms on the velcro dots. She smiled looking at the pom poms on the Christmas tree and when the pom pom shifted slightly, and didn't stay attached to the velcro dots, she adjusted it with her hand. She continued this process, filling several velcro dots on the Christmas tree with pom poms.
interpretation: Jovelle showed sustained concentration and persistence while working on the pom poms on the velcro dots of a Christmas tree. She displayed curiosity when the pom poms moved and placed back on the velcro dots. She demonstrated fine motor skills, eye-hand coordination and response to the educarer’s prompt indicated she is able to understand and follow simple instructions.

learning_goals.title: Develop physical well-being and physical competencies

title: "Exploring with Fruits and Vegetables"
description:
Jovelle sat in front of the educarer with a tray of velcro fruits and vegetables. The educarer held up each item individually, clearly naming it. “This is an apple”, “This a carrot”, “This is an orange”. As she watched the educarer attentively, making eye contact, she reached out for the apple from the educarer. She examined it closely by turning it over in her hands, feeling the texture and bringing it close to her face to smell it. 

When the educarer continued, “This is a corn”, she reached out for the corn and mimicked eating it, bringing the corn to her mouth and making chewing motions. She repeated her actions with the rest of the fruits and vegetables. She used her facial expressions to pretend eating actions suggested enjoyment. She continued to explore the fruits and vegetables for another few minutes.
interpretation: Jovelle showed positive interactions as she made eye contact with the teacher, suggesting engagement in the interaction and responsiveness to the educarer’s lead. She also gets herself involved in demonstrating receptive language skills by attending to the educarer’s naming of fruits and vegetables. The pretend eating suggests an understanding of mimicking, making facial expressions which demonstrate imitation skills as part of her learning.

learning_goals.title: Foster interactions between adult and child

title: Puppet Play- Hop Little Bunny
description:
Rebekah is engaged in a hand puppet play through a song “Hop Little Bunny, Hop Hop Hop”. Educarer provided her with a bunny ear headdress and a hand puppet.

Rebekah was sitting on the floor in front of her educarer. Educarer prompted her the bunny hand puppet and said “Rebekah, look! I have a bunny, “bounce! Bounce! Bounce!” while manipulating the puppet by bouncing it on the floor. Rebekah giggled gaily and babbled “ehh ehh” in response. Educarer asked her, “Can you say “Hi” to Bunny?” Rebekah smiled and looked at the puppet. She then touched the bunny and said “hi” while waving her hand. “Rebekah can you give me your hand?” educarer asked. Upon hearing, Rebekah extended her right hand towards her educarer. Educarer held her hand and let the bunny puppet hopped on her arm while singing “Hop little Bunny, hop hop hop.” Rebekah giggled happily while feeling ticklish. Educarer started singing the song. She modelled the actions towards her. When she sang the phrase “See the bunnies sleeping, till it’s nearly noon”, Rebekah imitated her actions. She put her hand on her face and pretended to sleep. “Well done Rebekah. You can follow the actions.” Educarer praised her. Rebekah looked at her smiled.

After playing with the puppet, educarer put the headdress on her head and told her, “Rebekah, let’s dance.” Rebekah excitedly stood up and babbled “ahh ahh ahh”. When educarer sang the song, Rebekah bounced her body up and down merrily. She was smiling and giggling while stomping and bouncing around the classroom. She also swayed her hips and clapped her hands. “Wow! Good dancing Rebekah.” Educarer applauded her.
interpretation:
• Rebekah displayed good interactions towards her educarer during puppet play. She was able to respond with enjoyment to her educarer through smiling, giggling, babbling and hand gestures. She can also imitate her educarer’s actions.
  • She expressed her enjoyment in playing with puppets. She also shown strong interests in music and movement.

children.fullname: Lau Tze Min Rebekah Grace (Liu Zhi Min)

Foster enjoyment in playing with toys and materials

title: Poking Sticks
description:
Rebekah was given tongue depressors and a recycled box with small slits for her to engage in poking to enhance her hand-eye coordination skill.

Educarer invited Rebekah to sit on the floor while showing her the materials. “Rebekah, look what I have. I have some sticks and box for you to explore poking. Let’s sit down here” educarer told her. Rebekah excitedly ran towards her and sat down in front of her. “Look, I pick the stick with my pincer grasp and poke it here.” Educarer described the actions while showing her the process. Rebekah smiled and quickly picked the tongue depressor with her palmar grasp. She aimed it into the slit and tried to poke it in. After adjusting and repositioning, she managed to poke the stick into the box. “Yay! Good poking Rebekah.” Educarer praised her. Rebekah smiled at her and clapped her hands in response. 

She continued doing the activity. With good palmar grasp, she grabbed the stick tightly with her right hand and poked it into the slit. She then pushed it down all the way to the bottom of the box. “Wow! You did it well Rebekah.” educarer applauded her. With a smile in her face, she quickly grabbed the stick on the floor and aimed it into the slit. She maneuvered her hand when the tongue depressor didn’t go through. When the stick went in to the slit, she pushed it down with her palm.  Rebekah poked all the tongue depressors into the box with good coordination and control.
interpretation:
• Rebekah’s fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination are developing very well. She displayed good palmar grasp while manipulating the materials. She demonstrated good hand-eye coordination while aiming the slit and poke the sticks into the box. 
  • While poking the sticks, she displayed good control and coordination while readjusting and repositioning her hand/material.

title: Painting with Nature
description:
Rebekah is engaged in art exploration using natural materials.

Educarer provided Rebekah with paints (red, yellow and blue), twigs, feathers and stones. Before exploration, educarer showed her the materials and named them. “Rebekah, look! These are the paints, yellow, red and blue.” while pointing on to the colours. Rebekah looked at her and babbled “bu” referring to blue. “Yes, you are right. It’s blue.” Rebekah smiled in response. She then pointed on the twigs while babbling “ah ah ah”. “Oh you want the twigs?” educarer asked. Rebekah smiled while extending her right arm towards the twigs. Educarer handed it to her. “Rebekah, let’s paint the stones this way.” Educarer told her while modelling the action.

Rebekah looked at her and started imitating the process. She held the twigs in both of her hands and dipped them into the paints. She explored twirling and swirling the twigs over the paints. “Rebekah, you are mixing the paints” educarer explained. Rebekah smiled at her. Educarer pointed on the stones and said “Rebekah, you brush the twigs here.” Rebekah carried the twigs towards the stones and randomly brushed them with the paints. “Oh, look at those beautiful marks!” educarer exclaimed. Rebekah repeated the process. She looked so focus while dipping the twigs on to the paints and brushed them on the stones without educarer’s assistance. “Good painting Rebekah” educarer praised her. She continued being engaged in the activity. She was smiling while brushing the twigs on to the stones. She also took the feathers and explored painting using the material.
interpretation:
• Rebekah was focused and was able to demonstrate sustained involvement while engaged in art exploration. She displayed curiosity and independence while exploring the materials. She looked so engrossed while engaged in the process.
  • She displayed interest in art through exploring with paints, colours, brushing/painting and making marks using natural materials.

title: 颜色排序
description:
教师带领幼儿观察一些不同风格的绘画作品，鼓励他们细心观察。通过讨论，引导他们注意颜色的不同层次。例如，画面中有些部分使用了明亮的色调，而其他部分则使用了较深的颜色。从而引出颜色深浅的概念。教师出示色块，请幼儿观察这些颜色，带领他们从深到浅或从浅到深排列这些色块。之后，教师请幼儿创作色彩排序画，鼓励幼儿使用水彩颜料，按照从深到浅或者从浅到深的顺序选择颜料盘里的颜色，绘制出自己喜欢的图形进行排序。最后，教师邀请幼儿选择一种排序方式，将6张深浅不一的色卡按照选择的方式进行排序。
慈恩告诉教师：“我要画星星。”说完，她蘸取了一些粉红色颜料在白纸上画出一颗粉色的星星。她说：“我要从浅到深，这个是很浅的粉红色。”说完，她看了看颜料，说：“我要橙色。”她又在纸上画出一颗橙色的星星。待她画完后，她说：“谢老师，你看。我画好了，从浅到深。”教师出示两块分别写有从深到浅和从浅到深的白板，问她想要进行哪个排列顺序。她看了看，指着其中一块白板说道：“我要这个，从深到浅。”说完，她观察了一下卡片。然后拿出黑色卡片放在最前面，她一边放，一边说：“黑色，蓝色，绿色，粉色，黄色，白色。我好了。”
interpretation: 慈恩通过观察绘画作品学习颜色的变化，学会了区分颜色的深浅。还通过动手实践，选取色彩盘里的颜色和色卡按照要求排序，加深了对颜色深浅的理解，逐渐培养了对艺术作品色彩运用的感知力。

title: 我的博物馆
description: 在学习绘本故事《奥莉薇》 的过程中， 孩子们对有奥莉薇去的博物馆很感兴趣。 宇翔对于博物馆很好奇， 我们一起收集了一些关于博物馆的信息。 当我问他：“ 如果你有一个博物馆， 会是什么博物馆呢？” 他认真的想了想， 告诉我说：" 我要有一个家的博物馆。” 于是我接着问， “那这个家的博物馆里都有什么呢？你能画出来给我看吗？” 宇翔听了很开心， 他迅速地拿出一张纸， 开始画了起来。 画完之后他主动在其他小朋友们面前做了分享与说话， 他告诉朋友们：“ 这是房子博物馆。 这是一个个的家。 我画房子， 因为人人都爱自己的家。 这个博物馆会在2026年1月2日开， 它是在日本。 ”
interpretation: 通过宇翔制作的海报， 可以看出他能够将自己的想象通过绘画的方式表现出来， 是创作能力的体现。 同时， 他能够使用简单的华语以小段话的方式表达出来， 说明他具有良好的沟通与表达能力， 能够自信地使用华语。

title: "Dried Leaves Exploration"
description:
Matthias eyes fixated on the leaves scattering to the floor and he picked them up with his hands. He checked the dried leaves and started moving his hands up and down. He slowly wriggled his fingers on the dried leaves to check its texture and continued to manipulate with his hands. He then held onto the twig and started grabbing the dried leaf with another hand. He slowly plucked out one of the dried leaves from the twig and dropped it to the floor. He continued to pluck one more leaf and dropped to the floor. 

Again, he plucked out the leaf again and this time, he had more leaves scattered to the floor. He picked them up and gathered them in his hands and dropped them to the floor. When the educarer picked up a bunch of leaves, he looked at the educarer’s hands and watched as the dried leaves flew down and scattered to the floor and some landed on his head! He picked the leaves from the floor and placed them back into the tray and continued to explore the leaves for another few minutes.
interpretation: Matthias displayed curiosity as he explored the dried leaves with his hands by manipulating and checking the texture of the dried leaves. He also wriggled with his fingers to check the texture of the dried leaves to experiment with the leaves through sensory experience and showed sustained concentration. When he watched the educarer pick a bunch of dried leaves and flew down, scattered to the floor and on his head, he saw the action and experience with cause and effect.

learning_goals.title: Children are confident, curious involved learners

title: "Pulling and Pushing of Straws"
description:
Matthias sat in front of the educarer and watched the educarer demonstrate the activity to him. “Let’s grab the straw and pull it out from the box. Then you put the straw on the tray like this”. As he observed the educarer carefully, “Now, it’s your turn Matthias”, he grabbed the straw with his right hand and slowly pulled it out from the box. “Place the straw on the tray here”, as he slowly moved his hand towards the tray and released it on the tray. “Let’s pull another straw”, as soon as he heard the educarer’s voice, he moved his hand to the straws and grabbed one of them and placed the straw on the tray. He continued to grab the rest of the straws from the box and placed them on the tray. “Yay, you did it!

The educarer asked, "How about we push the straw through the hole like this?”  Matthias watched the educarer attentively pushing the straw through the hole, he picked one of the straws from the tray and moved the straw to the hole. While making attempts to push the straw through the hole, he maneuvered his hand and pushed the straw in. He grabbed another straw from the tray and repeated his actions. This time, he pushed and pulled the straw with a little more force and successfully pushed it through the hole. He also used his alternate hands to remove two straws at the same time to explore. When he tried to push back the two straws through the hole with both hands, it didn’t go in easily. He kept trying to maneuver with both hands and when he was unable to do it, he showed the two straws to the educarer to ask for help and continue trying to push the straws through the holes again.
interpretation: Matthias is capable of following instructions and imitating the educarer’s actions such as observing the educarer demonstrating the activity and pulling out the straws from the box to the tray. He continues to repeat the action of grabbing and placing straws, demonstrating a growing confidence and engagement with the task. He maneuvered his hands to push and pull the straws which shows good grasping skills, eye-hand coordination and hands control movements. When he encountered a challenge with two straws, he seeked help from the educarer and continued to make effort in the exploration.

learning_goals.title: Foster hand-eye coordination

title: "Pom Poms Pouring"
description:
Matthias sat on the floor with a tray and cups of pom poms in front of him. He picked one of the pom pom from the cup and explored it with his fingers. He squeezed the pom pom with his pincer grip and placed it back into the cup. “Come, let me hold your hand and hold the cup like this”, as the educarer guided his hand to pour out the pom poms into the empty cup. He watched the pom poms drop into the cup and he used his hand to touch the pom poms. When the educarer guided his hand again, “Let’s pour it like this”, he saw the pom poms dropped into the cup again and some scattered to the tray and the floor. He picked the pom poms from the tray and placed them back into the cup. He also searched for the scattered pom poms and picked them up from the floor and placed them back into the cup.

When it was his turn, “Come Matthias, it’s your turn to pour the pom poms”, he held the cup filled with pom poms and started shaking the cup. Some of the pom poms flew out from the cup and scattered to the floor. He saw the pom poms moving and rolling away and continued to pour out the remaining pom poms in the cup. He easily poured out the pom poms into the empty cup. Then, he checked the cup that he was holding and showed it to the educarer. “This cup is empty. No more pom poms”, as he showed “no more” with his hands. When the educarer pointed at the other cup filled with pom poms, “see, you poured into the cup”, he picked with his hands and smiled at the educarer.
interpretation: Matthias displayed confidence and curiosity as he explored the pom poms pouring activity. With educarer’s guidance, he was able to experience pouring motion and see visual results such as an empty cup when he checked the cup after pouring the pom poms out. As he explored and experimented the activity, he demonstrated a desire to explore different ways to explore the pom poms such as observing pom poms movement and rolling when he shakes the cup. He was also able to use the “no more” gesture and smiled at the educarer to be pleased with his accomplishment and to communicate to the educarer.

description:

教师将白纸递给家乐，他用笔刷蘸取了一些黑色颜料在纸上画出一个黑色圆圈，他一边画，一边说：“我要画pokemon的，这是一个pokemon ball。”教师告诉他ball的华文是球。他说道：“我画的球，我要画一个eevee。”说完，他蘸取了一些紫色在白纸上画了一个轮廓。教师告他紫色太浅了，之后很难找到更浅的颜色。他问道：“How？”教师请他看看调色盘里的紫色，请他看看自己的笔刷。他看后说：“太多水了。”教师点点头，请他再蘸取一些紫色填充到图案中。他填好后，又使用了橙色、黄色。他指着白色说：“这个看不见。”教师告诉他白色已经沾染到其他颜色并请他试试看。他蘸取了白色，在纸上画下一个图案。他说：“可以。”教师问他选择的哪种排列顺序，他说：“From light to dark."教师告诉他是从浅到深，他复述了：“从浅到深。”教师指正他从浅到深第一个颜色应该是白色。他指着作品说：“From 这边。”

title: 捞皮筋
description:
描述：
       教师和幼儿坐在桌子前，教师向幼儿介绍“捞皮筋活动”要用到的物品有皮筋，筷子，碗。然后向幼儿讲解并演示如何捞皮筋。
       晟德用他的右手拿起一根筷子，将筷子伸进水里面，用筷子将皮筋挑起来，然后将筷子上的皮筋放在盘子里，他看着教师笑着说：“张老师，你看。”教师回应晟德：“晟德你很棒哦，你能够将水里面的皮筋挑起来。”晟德继续将筷子伸进水里面，然后用筷子将皮筋挑出来放在盘子上。晟德完成活动后，教师对晟德竖起大拇指。
interpretation:
诠释：

      在活动过程中，晟德能够用筷子将水里面的皮筋挑出来，并将筷子上的皮筋放在盘子上，展现出晟德的抓握能力，手眼协调能力和手部肌肉的精细动作。晟德在活动中也能用简单的语言与教师进行沟通。

title: 奥莉薇
description: 在学习绘本《 奥莉薇》 的过程中， 暄恩对于故事很感兴趣，她仔细地阅读绘本故事， 并且尝试和我沟通。通过沟通， 我请她说说他最喜欢的故事的情节，暄恩仔细地想了想， 告诉我说：“ 我喜欢奥莉薇在堆沙堡的这幅画，她堆了高高的沙堡， 因为我也喜欢和爸爸妈妈还有弟弟一起堆沙堡。” 。 听了她的答案之后， 我便问她：“ 如果请你用绘画的方式表达出来， 你会怎样画呢？” 她看了看我， 想了想， 说到：“ 我会画奥莉薇和她的妈妈， 还有她的弟弟一起在沙滩上， 这边有高高的沙堡。”
interpretation: 通过暄恩的回答，可以看出暄恩的回复具有逻辑性， 说明她能够准确地理解老师问句的含义， 也能够使用清晰明确有逻辑的语句来表达自己的想法。 通过她和老师的对话， 也能够看出， 她能够自信流利地使用华语来和别人沟通。

title: 自由发掘新乐器
description:
瑞泽在课室里自由探索，发现玩具柜子里面有一摞朔料碗，瑞泽拿起整套的碗放在地板上，然后用两只手把摞在一起的碗分开再摞回去，在反复几次后瑞泽拿起两个碗用碗底相互敲击，敲出铛铛铛的声音，瑞泽听到声音露出笑容，之后开始有节奏的敲击时快时慢，身体也跟着节奏扭动。

title: 记忆翻牌游戏
description:
教师提供“高兴、伤心、生气、害怕”的字卡，引导幼儿复习情绪词语并模仿相应的表情。接着教师和幼儿一起玩记忆翻牌游戏，规则是：幼儿依次排列字卡并记忆各个字卡位置10秒，再翻面，最后找到一样的字卡并说出名称或者模仿对应表情。鼓励幼儿通过游戏认读所学词汇，培养认字的兴趣，对于未找到匹配卡片的幼儿，鼓励其坚持尝试，完成任务。

在情绪字卡复习活动中，当老师拿出字卡“伤心”时，天瑞马上就回答：“伤心”。在记忆翻牌游戏中，天瑞一直看着放好的的字卡，当计时结束，天瑞马上举手说：“I know（我知道），“ 他找到了伤心字卡，并说：”伤心“。在接下来的游戏中，他重复进行游戏， 尽管有时未能找到正确的牌，但他表现出坚持尝试的态度，最终成功完成任务。
interpretation: 天瑞能够认读字卡：伤心、生气和害怕，他也能辨别并做出不同的的情绪表情。他能够用华语表达自己看到的字卡。他多次重复的玩游戏，表示他的专注力和坚持不懈的态度。

title: 我的博物馆
description: 在学习绘本故事《奥莉薇》 的过程中， 孩子们对有奥莉薇去的博物馆很感兴趣。 谦睿对于博物馆很好奇， 我们一起收集了一些关于博物馆的信息。 当我问他：“ 如果你有一个博物馆， 会是什么博物馆呢？” 他认真的想了想， 告诉我说：" 我要有一个汽车的博物馆， 然后这个旁边是很多的家” 于是我接着问， “那这个博物馆里都有什么呢？你能画出来给我看吗？” 谦睿听了很开心， 他迅速地拿出一张纸， 开始画了起来。 画完之后他主动在其他小朋友们面前做了分享与说话， 他告诉朋友们：“ 这是汽车博物馆。 这是一个个的家。 我画了很多的家， 因为人人都爱家， 从家出去这边就是汽车。 这个博物馆会在2025年4月5日开， 它是在我的家开。 ”
interpretation: 通过谦睿制作的海报， 可以看出他能够将自己的想象通过绘画的方式表现出来， 是创作能力的体现。 同时， 他能够使用简单的华语以小段话的方式表达出来， 说明他具有良好的沟通与表达能力， 能够自信地使用华语。

title: Brown Bear, Brown Bear
description: Kaen was sitting with his friends in the library space when he picked up the book Brown Bear, Brown Bear by Eric Carle. He began flipping through the pages while singing the song that goes along with the book. He identified each character and finished singing before turning to the next page. When the teacher prompted him, Kaen continued singing and responded to questions like, “What is that?” as he described the pictures. In the following video, he successfully named the animals and their colours, saying things like, “a green frog,” “a blue horse,” and “a yellow duck.”
interpretation: Kaen’s actions show his developing language and cognitive skills. He is actively engaging with the book Brown Bear, Brown Bear by Eric Carle, demonstrating his ability to remember and recognise different animals and their colours. When Kaen sings the song, it shows his ability to describe and label objects, indicating his expanding vocabulary. "White Dog, white dog what do you see? I see a black sheep looking at me."

title: Match and Celebrate Pairs
description: During a numeracy pairing activity, the teacher provided a variety of items for the children to find and match things that are of a pair and would work well together. Thaddeus picked up a dustpan before reaching over for a cleaning brush. When asked to described how would the items be used together, Thaddeus then made a sweeping motion with the brush before moving it closer to the dustpan. The teacher then added a piece of paper acting as rubbish for Thaddeus to demonstrate using the items once more. Thaddeus then dramatized his actions again by showing how he swept up the piece of paper into the dustpan.
interpretation: The action of selecting a brush after picking up a dustpan reflected Thaddeus' ability to demonstrate a logical understanding that these two items are functionally related and typically used together. By making a sweeping motion and using the dustpan, Thaddeus also physically demonstrated the items' relationship through actions. He showed a good understanding of how the two objects work as a set, reinforcing the concept of pairing through practical application. Through his dramatization of sweeping up 'rubbish', Thaddeus additionally symbolically represented the purpose of the paired objects he had chosen. This is an important early numeracy skill, as it reflects making connections between objects and their functions.

learning_goals.title: Pair related objects (e.g: a cup to a saucer, a fork to a spoon)

title: Matching and Celebrate Pairs
description: During a numeracy pairing activity, the teacher provided a variety of items for the children to find and match things that are of a pair and would work well together. Diyansh first picked out a sharpener before reaching for a colour pencil next. When asked to describe his items and how they worked together, Diyansh could correctly name the items before explaining, "You use the sharpener to sharpen the colour pencil." Diyansh then went on to fit the pencil into the hole of the sharpener before making a twisting motion with the colour pencil to demonstrate how it would be sharpened.
interpretation: Diyansh demonstrated a good understanding of object relationships by selecting a sharpener and then correctly choosing a colour pencil — two items that naturally pair together. Diyansh's verbal explanation reflects his understanding of how the colour pencil and sharpener work together. By physically fitting the pencil into the sharpener and mimicking the twisting motion, Diyansh translated his verbal understanding into a hands-on demonstration. This shows he not only understands the conceptual relationship but also knows how to use the objects together in practice. Diyansh’s explanation and demonstration illustrates his awareness of cause and effect — understanding that using the sharpener on the pencil produces a specific outcome (a sharpened tip). This logical reasoning is an important part of early numeracy development.

learning_goals.title: Pair related objects (e.g: a cup to a saucer, a fork to a spoon)

title: Match and Celebrate Pairs
description: During a pairing activity, the teacher provided a variety of items for the class to find and match things that would work well together. Elly first reached for the plate and then a fork. When asked how would she used both items together, Elly started to bring the fork from the plate towards her mouth. She then said, "I can eat spaghetti like this." The teacher then replied, "Oh you use the fork to eat the spaghetti from the plate?" Elly nodded in response and spoke, "Yes" before twirling her fork and bringing it to her mouth to dramatize the action of eat spaghetti with a fork.
interpretation: By selecting a plate and then a fork, Elly demonstrated an understanding of functional object pairs. She recognized that these two items are commonly used together, showing her ability to match objects that have a practical relationship. Elly didn’t just name the objects — she acted out their use. By bringing the fork from the plate to her mouth and later twirling it, she physically demonstrated how the fork and plate work together during mealtime. This hands-on demonstration reinforced her good conceptual understanding of the pairing. Elly's association of the plate and fork with eating spaghetti, also reflects her ability to connect the objects to a real-life context. Through this activity, Elly shows her strong development of understanding relationships between objects, which is a foundational concept in early numeracy development.

title: 奥莉薇故事续编
description: 教师带领幼儿复习绘本《奥莉薇》，并将《奥莉薇》最后一页的情节作为起点，想象奥莉薇醒来后的一系列活动。通过自己的理解和想象来创编奥莉薇醒来后的行为。教师通过提问或给出一些示范来引导幼儿思考，例如：奥莉薇喜欢什么，她醒来后会做自己喜欢的事情吗？教师为幼儿提供材料，邀请幼儿通过绘画和仿写的方式将自己的故事分享出来。
interpretation:
媖绮想象并绘制了奥莉薇一家去探望新出生的宝宝威廉，因为在故事开始前，作者提到也献给还没赶上绘本问世前出生的威廉。可能是感受到了奥莉薇的淘气个性，媖绮的作品中出现了猪宝宝在家的墙上绘画，妈妈回家后很生气的场景。

她的作品色彩丰富且包含了多个场景，体现了她对故事的理解和想象力。画面清晰，能够通过表情、动作和场景表达人物关系和情节发展。

title: Work Sample - My Traffic Light Craft
description: As part of our exploration on the theme of "Transportation," Jayley engaged in creating her own traffic light craft using red, yellow, and green paint. With a paintbrush in hand, she eagerly transformed a plain paper plate into a bright, colorful signal. She began by carefully dotting her brush and marvelling at the imprints left behind. She soon explored working with different strokes and movements, gradually covering her paper plate with paint. Curious about the texture, she gently touched the paint with her fingers before continuing her masterpiece. When she was done, Jayley beamed with pride, excitedly smiling and pointing to her artwork. Through this activity, she explored colour recognition, creativity, and sensory experiences while having fun with art.

title: Toy Hunt
description:
The word "matching" was introduced to the children, and examples were given to help them understand the concept. A box with different toys was presented to the children, and they were invited to find the toy that matched the one they chose. Aydin chose the green bottle and began looking for its match. Aydin walked around the class, searching for the other green bottle in each corner. When Aydin couldn't find the bottle, I asked him if he needed help from his friends. Aydin replied, "No," and continued searching. Aydin was having a hard time finding the bottle, so I gave him a hint, saying, “Is it in the box?” referring to the wooden box. Aydin looked for the wooden box, and when he found it, he looked inside. With a smile, Aydin looked at me and said, “I found it!” I asked Aydin if the bottles matched or were the same, and he replied, “Yes.”

Aydin successfully matched two identical green bottles, demonstrating his ability to recognise and match identical objects showing an understanding of the concept of matching. Aydin effectively communicated his thoughts and feelings throughout the activity. He expressed his excitement and achievement by smiling and saying, “I found it!” Additionally, Aydin demonstrated persistence and independence by continuing to search for the matching bottle, even when he faced difficulty. His clear verbal communication and actions showed his ability to express his ideas and feelings effectively with others.

learning_goals.title: Match identical objects or pictures.

title: Toy Hunt
description:
The word "matching" was introduced to the children, and examples were given to help them understand the concept. A box with different toys was presented to the children, and they were invited to find the toy that matched the one they chose. Kyan chose the pink tube and began looking for its match. He walked around the class, focused on finding the other pink tube. I asked him, "What is the colour of your toy?" and Kyan replied, "Pink." I told Kyan to look for a pink toy to encourage him, and even his friends cheered for him, saying, "You can do it!" Kyan smiled and eagerly continued looking for the pink tube. He walked near the cubby, looked up, and found the other pink tube. Kyan said, "I found it." I asked Kyan if they matched, and he put the two pink tubes together, saying, "Yes."

Kyan successfully matched two pink tubes, demonstrating his ability to recognise and match identical objects. Kyan experienced feelings of focus and determination as he worked to find the matching toy. Additionally, the encouragement from his peers, as they cheered him on with phrases like "You can do it!" helped foster a sense of support and positive social interaction.

learning_goals.title: Match identical objects or pictures.

title: Self-Portrait
description:
The children were invited to create self-portraits by making marks and using playdough to add details. Kyan began drawing his portrait, and while adding details, he shared his thoughts, saying, "I drew two eyes," and "This is my mouth." While pasting the playdough, Kyan counted the strands he was making as the hair for his portrait. I shared with Kyan how much I liked how he formed the hair for his portrait, then I asked him if he liked it. Kyan responded with a "yes."

Kyan demonstrated confidence in creating and sharing his self-portrait. He was comfortable expressing his thoughts and explaining his process. By drawing and adding details to his portrait, Kyan showed an understanding of his own identity, evident in his recognition of the different features that make up his image.

learning_goals.title: Know the similarities and differences between living things, non-living things, places and events.

title: Numicon Size Tower
description:
The Numicon toys were given to the children, and they were invited to create their own towers by placing and lining them up on the floor. Kyan chose some Numicon pieces and began arranging them on the floor. Once Kyan was done, I invited him to share about his tower. Kyan said, "My tower is very high," while showing it to me. I asked him what we could do in the tower, and he shared, "I can eat inside." After hearing his friend mention a swimming pool in their tower, Kyan also shared that there was a swimming pool in his tower. After our conversation, Kyan continued playing with his friends.

Kyan displayed focus and enthusiasm while making his own tower using the Numicon toys. He confidently shared his thoughts and ideas about the tower and used his imagination to suggest activities we could do in his tower.

learning_goals.title: Use expanded vocabulary and language for a variety of purposes.

title: Funny Nature Hair
description:
The children visited Pasir Ris Park, and as part of their activity, they were invited to create art using dried leaves and twigs to represent the hair on their portraits. Kyan collected leaves with his peers and happily handed me the leaf he had gathered. He then began placing the leaves on his portrait. Li Kee lao shi gave Kyan a leaf and asked if he would like to add it to his portrait. Kyan accepted the leaf and pasted it onto his artwork. Once Kyan was finished, I asked him which natural items he had used for the hair on his portrait. Kyan responded by sharing that he had used twigs and leaves while pointing to them. At the end, I asked Kyan if he liked his funny hair portrait. Kyan smiled and said, "Funny."

Kyan showed happiness and focus as he worked on his nature-inspired hair portrait, demonstrating strong social-emotional competence by engaging positively with his peers and adults, expressing his creativity, and showing pride in his work.

learning_goals.title: Talk about their own artworks (e.g: what the artwork is about and the lines, colours and shapes used).

title: Obstacle
description:
The obstacle course was set up, and the children were invited to explore it. Eldrin, full of excitement, climbed onto the first arch. When he reached the second arch, he paused and began thinking about how he would get down. While trying to balance himself, Eldrin attempted to climb down while facing forward, but he struggled with the descent. I asked if he needed help and offered my hand for him to hold. Eldrin took my hand and carefully descended the arch. Afterward, Eldrin knelt down and crawled under the arch, making sure it didn't move. With careful attention and determination, Eldrin successfully completed all the obstacles and, feeling confident, asked to do another round.

Eldrin was full of confidence, displaying his strength and abilities. Throughout the activity, he managed to move with balance and control.

learning_goals.title: Move with balance and control.

title: Match and Celebrate Pair
description:
A box with different objects was presented to the children, and the concept of pairing was explained by demonstrating an example. Each child was invited to choose the item they liked, and Eldrin chose a pencil. I asked him, “What is a pencil for? How do you use it?” Eldrin mimed drawing with the pencil. I invited Eldrin to stand in front and look for his friend who was holding an item that would pair with the pencil. Eldrin said, “Paper,” and Solomon immediately stood up beside him. I asked both of them how to use the items they were holding. Solomon placed the paper on the chair, and Eldrin used the pencil to draw on it. Eldrin happily drew on the paper.

Eldrin displayed an understanding of the concept of pairing related objects. He demonstrated an enthusiastic attitude and interacted positively with his teachers and friends.

learning_goals.title: Pair related objects (e.g: a cup to a saucer, a fork to a spoon)

title: This is Me
description:
The children were introduced to journal writing, and the question to reflect on was, "Can you draw your face and tell me what makes it special?" Engracia began making marks and drawing shapes. While drawing her hair, she said, “Teacher Chari, this is my Elsa hair.” I replied, “That is nice hair.” Engracia smiled and continued drawing her face. Once she was done, I asked, “Could you share with me what you drew?” Engracia shared, “This is my hair, Elsa hair. I like Elsa.” I asked her again, “Is that what makes you special?” She answered yes. Engracia continued sharing what she drew, saying things like, “My mouth is here,” “This is my face,” and “I like my hair.”

During the activity, Engracia showed great interest and enthusiasm in drawing her face portrait using lines and shapes and sharing her thoughts. While sharing, she could communicate her thoughts and feelings about her face portrait and how much she likes Elsa.

learning_goals.title: Use letter-like shapes, symbols and letters to convey meaning.

title: Numicon Toy Matching
description:
Using the Numicon toy, the children were invited to match the pieces of Numicon to their shadow cut-out. Engracia placed the shape shadow cut-out in front of her, and I invited her to observe it. After observing, she picked up a piece of the Numicon toy and tried to match it with the shadow cut-out. Engracia was figuring out if they matched. title: Self-Portrait
description:
After looking in the mirror and discussing her facial features, Engracia was invited to create her self-portrait by making marks and using playdough to add details. Engracia took a marker and said, "I want pink," then began drawing her portrait. While drawing, she shared with me that she was drawing two eyes and pointed to her nose and lips. Engracia placed playdough on the head of her portrait to represent hair. Once she finished, I asked Engracia what she liked about her portrait, and she pointed to the hair, saying, "I like my pink hair." I shared with her that I liked her hair as well.

Engracia displayed a strong sense of identity by showing awareness of her own features, identifying and labeling parts of her face, such as her eyes, nose, and lips. She was confident in expressing herself by sharing her choices and preferences.

title: Five Senses
description:
The ‘Talking Tub’ was presented to the children, and they were invited to take one object. Solomon searched the box and quickly took the sunglasses, saying, “I have eyeglasses at home, too.” Once everyone had an object from the box, they were invited to describe it. A friend passed the scented tissue to Solomon, and I invited her to share her observation. Solomon smelled the scented tissue and asked, “What is this smell?” I answered, “That’s a mint smell. Do you like it?” Solomon smiled and said yes. When it was Solomon’s turn to share, he described the sunglasses by saying, “I wear eyeglasses when it's a sunny day.” Then, I encouraged him to look at the board and point to the body part we use the sunglasses on. He immediately pointed to the eyes and tried to place the sunglasses on the eye picture. Solomon laughed when I noticed what he had done.

Throughout the activity, Solomon observed and talked about the scented tissue and sunglasses. He also demonstrated the ability to describe the use of sunglasses, specifically their use for the eyes, and engaged in a conversation about smell. As Solomon described the sunglasses and made connections between the object and his own experiences (wearing eyeglasses on sunny days), he demonstrated self-awareness and confidence in sharing his thoughts.

title: Five Senses
description:

Solomon, who was behind Gemma, asked her, "Is it heavy?" Gemma responded by nodding her head.

Gemma observed and interacted with various non-living objects, such as the mint-scented tissue and the rock. She explored the objects presented to her through touch and smell, which required her to observe their properties (e.g., the texture of the rock, the scent of the tissue). During the activity, Gemma demonstrated her ability to recognize and express her personal preferences and emotions in a social setting. The interaction between Solomon and Gemma shows that she is able to engage in conversation and respond appropriately to her peers, demonstrating social awareness and communication skills.

description:

After describing the leaf, Jasmine and her friend were invited to group their nature items and observe which ones were small and which ones were big. Without any hesitation, Jasmine and her friend said that the round leaf was big and the spear-shaped leaf was small.

Jasmine displayed strong observation skills and social-emotional competence. She was able to articulate her thoughts and feelings about the nature item with clarity. title: Exploring Bubbles
description: The educarer placed a container filled with soap and water in front of Elijah. She then dipped her hand into the tub and moved it around to create bubbles. Afterward, she encouraged Elijah to do the same, asking him to move his hand back and forth inside the tub to form more bubbles. Once there were plenty of bubbles, Elijah scooped them up with one hand and clapped with excitement. When he clapped, he noticed the bubbles splashed all over his face and body. Delighted, he repeated the action several times. When the bubbles were gone from his hand, he continued to scoop and clap, making sure the bubbles splashed all over again. Elijah had so much fun scooping and splashing the bubbles repeatedly.
interpretation: Elijah was able to follow simple, one-step instructions, demonstrating an awareness of how his actions lead to certain outcomes and actively trying to make things happen. He shows a high level of happiness, trust, confidence, vitality, curiosity, and engages in positive interactions. During this activity, he was able to maintain interest and curiosity for several minutes. Elijah also demonstrated an understanding of cause and effect, noticing how actions impact one another. Overall, he sustained intense focus and involvement, showing concentration, energy, and persistence. Great job, Elijah!

learning_goals.title: Foster understanding of cause and effect through engagement with toys, materials and books 通过玩有回馈动作的玩具（如：按压一个会嘎嘎叫的玩具）、探索材料（如：吹泡泡）和阅读书籍等活动，初步发展婴幼儿对于因果关系的感知。

title: Peek-a-boo, Where are you?
description: The educarer began singing the "Peek-a-boo, Where are you?" song. Elijah then approached Miya, who was near the mirror, and faced her while covering his face. The educarer said, "Elijah, Peek-a-boo, where’s Miya?" Elijah removed his hand and stared directly at Miya before repeating the action. This time, the educarer asked, "Can you cover your ear? Where’s your ear?" Elijah and Miya then took turns covering their ears and other facial features, such as their head, nose, and mouth. They both observed each other closely while the educarer asked about the locations of the different facial features. Elijah seemed to guide Miya in identifying the facial features; when the educarer asked, "Where’s your head?" Elijah pointed to his own head first, while Miya watched and then imitated the same action. Well done, Elijah, for guiding Miya along!
interpretation: From this activity, we observed that Elijah’s self-conscious emotions seem to emerge in the presence of others. He clearly enjoys guiding and showing his friends that he understands what the educarer is saying. Elijah also displays a high level of happiness, trust, confidence, vitality, curiosity, and engages in positive interactions with his peers. He was able to label several emotions and actions based on the educarer's prompts, demonstrating his ability to connect his feelings with his social behaviors. By performing the correct actions and guiding his friends through the activity, Elijah showcased a strong sense of self-concept and self-esteem, as well as a developing self-identity, particularly through his identification of different facial features. He also demonstrated sustained involvement, concentration, energy, and persistence throughout the activity, interacting and engaging well with his friends.

learning_goals.title: Foster interactions between children during routines and experiences 在常规活动、互动和体验中，培养婴幼儿之间的互动。

domains.title: Psycho-social Self 心理-社会行为

title: Twist the bottle cover
description: The educarer handed Elijah a cupboard filled with different-sized bottle caps for him to explore. The educarer first demonstrated how to twist open the bottle caps using just his fingers. Afterward, the educarer ensured that the caps were not twisted too tightly, making it easier for Elijah to open them. When Elijah took over, he quickly understood the task and seemed confident in twisting open the bottle caps, regardless of their size. In just a few seconds, he was able to twist the caps open, often trying to open two at once—one in each hand. While he was usually able to open the bottle cap with his right hand, he didn’t give up when the other hand had difficulty. After having two bottle caps in his hands, Elijah even tried mixing them up, placing them in different combinations, but noticed that the sizes didn’t fit as well. Elijah continued this activity for a good 5-10 minutes.
interpretation: From this activity, we observed that Elijah is always very interested in exploring new activities. He demonstrated sustained involvement throughout the task, showing concentration, energy, and persistence by not giving up easily. Elijah was able to pick up the smallest bottle caps, displaying a well-coordinated pincer grasp as he twisted the caps open. Although he attempted to use both hands, he primarily used his right hand, indicating a preference for it. He also displayed a high level of happiness and confidence as he successfully twisted the caps open. His curiosity was evident when he mixed up the bottle caps, but in the end, he was able to match them back to their original places correctly. Keep up the curiosity, Elijah, and continue to be excited to explore new things

title: Guess Who?
description:
Maeve was invited to play a game of ‘Guess Who?’ with her friends. Standing behind the blanket, Maeve had to name the friend standing across her when the blanket was lifted up. “Are you ready?” the teacher asked. “Yes!” she squealed and beamed excitedly. “Alright, close your eyes!” Maeve closed her eyes. “And open! Who’s standing in front of you?” the teacher asked. Maeve waited for a while before saying, “Caden! Ethan!” 

Maeve indicated her interest to try again and eagerly said, “I want!” As the teacher readied her and said, “1, 2, 3! Open!” Maeve leaned in to get a good look of her friend and exclaimed, “Ethan! Hello, Ethan!” The teacher praised her stating that it was a good game.
interpretation: Maeve fostered a sense of self and others when she named her friends in the game. While playing, she showed excitement to interact with her friends by displaying pro-social behaviours such as leaning towards her friends and smiling at them. Maeve also fostered a sense of trust in her teacher as she comfortably interacted and followed her lead in the game.

description:

description:
描述：
　　教师向幼儿展示毛毛虫的图片，请幼儿观察毛毛虫，引导幼儿说出这是毛毛虫。然后向幼儿介绍做美术活动所需的材料以及活动流程。
　　轩伊走到桌子旁边，摸了摸桌子上的“毛毛虫”的头，教师问轩伊：“你想要做美术活动吗？”轩伊点了点头。然后她坐在桌子前，接过粘有“毛毛虫”的头的白纸，将其放在桌子上面，拿起笔刷蘸取绿色的颜料，将颜料涂在手上面，然后将小手上的颜料拓印在白纸上，教师指着白纸对轩伊说：“轩伊，你的小手也要拍拍这里哦。（毛毛虫的头的后面）”轩伊看着教师点了点头，然后再次将小手涂满颜料，然后用小手继续拍打白纸，当整张白纸都是绿色后，轩伊告诉老师她做完了。教师对轩伊竖起大拇指并说道：“轩伊，你的毛毛虫是胖胖的呦。”轩伊笑着说：“胖胖的。”

诠释：

description:
在问好时间，教师引导幼儿们一起学习了儿歌《找朋友》，随后教师鼓励幼儿自由分组，两人一组随着儿歌做动作和同伴来玩找朋友游戏。
      在活动中，老师询问：“哪个小朋友愿意和自己的朋友一组来交朋友啊？”含饴看了看老师，老师招招手说：“含饴是不是想玩游戏呀？快过来！”含饴听后走了过来，老师询含饴是否愿意和敏瑄一组，含饴看了看朋友，和朋友相对而坐，当老师说道：“找一个朋友碰碰拳”时，看到朋友伸出手，含饴也伸出手，和朋友碰碰拳，当听到：“找一个朋友握握手”时，他与朋友同时伸出手，握了握手，当老师说道：“现在，你和敏瑄已经是好朋友了，可以互相抱抱了！”朋友拥抱了含饴，含饴不好意思的看了看朋友，笑了。
interpretation: 在活动中，含饴能够在老师的鼓励下，积极参与找朋友的游戏，并尝试与同伴碰拳、握手、拥抱，体现出他与同伴能够建立良好的社交关系。

title: 作品分析
description:
围绕绘本《逃家小兔》幼儿们掌握了句式：如果你变成、、我就变成、、在创意美术的延申课程中，幼儿们继续围绕句式“如果你变成……，我就变成……”展开丰富的想象，设计并制作了一本独特的剪贴画小书。他们挑选多种颜色的彩纸，运用剪、贴、画等方式，将自己的奇思妙想变成具体的图画和文字。
