title: Math Mind: Shape Hunt (Integrated domain: Kidzercise)
description:
During learning application time, Jarren picked up circle and triangle shape hunt sticks and began searching for matching shapes around the classroom. Holding the circle stick, he walked to the cubby holes, placed the circle stick on the side of the cubby hold and said, "Ms Wei Ling, look! It's the same! Woah, same eh!" The teacher responded, "You found a circle, and the circles are even of the same size!" Jarren grinned and headed back to the learning centre to pick out an oval stick.

The teacher asked, "What shape did you choose this time?" Jarren replied, "Oval." The teacher suggested, "Shall we look for ovals together? Let's hop on one foot while we look for ovals in the classroom!" Jarren agreed and hopped on his right foot to different parts of the classroom to search for ovals. When he reached the birthday chart, he looked around and said, "I cannot find. Our classroom got no ovals." The teacher responded, "But I saw a few ovals here! Don't give up, try to find again. If you can't see it here, try looking up." Jarren turned around, looked up, and saw the ovals pasted on the wall. He then tiptoed, held up the oval stick, and said, "Here!" The teacher asked, "How do you know that's an oval?" Jarren replied, "A bit long here. The stick is also long." The teacher responded, "Yes! The oval is a little stretched out at the sides, right?" Jarren said, "Ya." and proceeded to pick up magnetic tiles on the floor. Using four big squares, Jarren arranged them and proudly shared, "Ms Wei Ling! See, a diamond!" The teacher responded, "Wow! How did you do that?" He replied, "I used the squares to make one. I combined."
interpretation:
Math Mind:

Jarren demonstrated his ability to match objects by shape and size when he compared the circle on his shape hunt stick to the one on the cubby hole, recognizing their similarity. He also showed an emerging understanding of shape attributes by identifying an oval and describing its distinguishing feature of being “a bit long.” When creating a diamond using magnetic tiles, Jarren applied spatial awareness and problem-solving skills by arranging four squares to form a new shape, recognizing that combining smaller shapes can create a larger geometric form. His ability to identify and describe the characteristics of different shapes reflects his growing understanding of shapes and spatial awareness.


Kidzercise (Gross Motor):

Jarren exhibited balance and control as he hopped on one foot while searching for ovals. While he hopped to different parts of the classroom, he was also adjusting his posture to maintain stability. When Jarren noticed that the oval pasted on the wall was taller than him, he coordinated his movements by tiptoeing to reach the ovals on the wall. Thus, demonstrating body control to accomplish a task. His ability to hop on one foot and tiptoe while staying focused on his activity highlights his developing coordination and gross motor skills.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

Jarren develops a positive self-concept (i.e., feels good about his own competence and characteristics)

title: Work Sample 2: Journaling
description: The children were invited to express their thoughts about what they enjoy about being three years old by drawing in their journals.
interpretation:
Yi Xuan used a regular pencil and yellow colored pencils to draw shapes like circles to express her ideas. When asked about her drawing, she pointed to a circle at the bottom right and explained, “That’s me, and the black shapes around me are the lego blocks.” She drew more shapes that resembled rectangles, similar in size to lego blocks, all around the page because, as she said, “In class, we have a lot of legos to share.”


Through gestures and short phrases like "Blue lego" or by pointing to herself, Yi Xuan showed how she communicates to interact with others. When asked about her drawing, she said, "I like that I can play with bigger lego blocks." This demonstrates her ability to identify her own likes, as she enjoys playing with legos, and expresses her personal feelings.

title: Work Sample 1: Letter Tt
description: After learning the letter "T" through Letterland, the children practiced writing both uppercase and lowercase "Tt" with a pencil, following air tracing exercises to build confidence and muscle memory.
interpretation:
Elliott initially asked for help with writing the letter "T" as he was unsure how to form it. After I demonstrated by air-tracing the letter "T" on the book, he carefully followed my movements, using his finger to trace the lines. He was then able to write both the uppercase and lowercase "T" with a pencil using a palmar grasp. 


As he attempted to draw straight lines, they were slightly curved, resulting in letter-like shapes that resembled "T"s and a copied symbol of a curved "t." This suggests that Elliott is still refining his fine motor skills and hand control. With more practice, he will likely improve his ability to draw straighter lines and form more accurate letters. After completing the task, he proudly showed me his work, saying, "Look! Teacher Crystal! Letter T big and small!"

title: Work Sample 1: Happy Valentine’s
description: The Valentine artwork is a simple yet meaningful gesture from the children to show love and appreciation to the seniors. After reading a story about love, the children were inspired to create something special for the elderly.
interpretation: Jaea created a Valentine’s Day artwork using pink paper, her favourite color, which she colored red with crayon to form a heart. She added two pom-poms for eyes and one for the nose. To represent the mouth, she used twine for a smile, inspired by her friends. After struggling with gluing the thin string, her teacher guided her to press it down using her palms. The final piece featured a heart with a pom-pom face and twine smile. She explained that it represented a self portrait of a grandma. This reflects Jaea’s developing understanding of expressing appreciation and linking it to her personal experiences.

interpretation: Raylan created a heart with a face, using coloring pencils to outline features like the hair and nose. Initially, he used glitter glue for added shine but switched to regular glue when it didn’t adhere properly. Using his left hand and a pincer grip, he carefully attached pom-poms for the eyes and dimples, along with circular paper rolls for spectacles. These choices reflected his intention to make the artwork colorful, and he explained that he wanted it to “look like a grandpa.” This demonstrates Raylan’s growing understanding of expressing appreciation and connecting it to his personal experiences.

learning_goals.title: Represent things in the environment through artwork.

She added a pom-pom for the nose and crumpled tissues, using her palmer grasp, to represent the white hair of the grandma. The final piece featured a heart with colorful houses representing "my house," "grandma’s house," and "mummy’s house," with the idea that they could all go to the green field to play together. title: Loud and Soft
description: The children were introduced to loud and soft sounds using two musical instruments. They were invited to explore which instrument played loud or soft music.
interpretation:
Jaea was introduced to two instruments, bells and a guitar, to explore loud and soft sounds. Unsure which instrument made which sound, she identified the bells as "very loud" and the guitar as "soft" after hearing them played a few times and prompts. This showed her growing ability to distinguish between different sound volumes. 


After the teacher named the instruments, Jaea tries incorporating them into her language, saying things like, "I want to play the bells".Through different hand gestures while playing the guitar, Jaea begins to understand how the speed and size of her movements influence the sound's volume—faster, larger movements create louder sounds, while slower, smaller movements produce softer ones. For example, when she uses the palm of her hand to strum across all the strings, the sound is much louder and fuller. In contrast, when she uses just her fingers for a more delicate strum, the sound is softer and more controlled. This deepened her understanding of how physical actions can control sound.

title: Math Mind: Shape Hunt (Integrated domain: Kidzercise)
description:
During learning application time, Miao En grabbed a box of shape hunt activity sticks and picked out a rectangle. Holding the rectangle stick, she walked around the class and noticed a pile of Lego blocks on the floor. Miao En ran towards the Lego blocks and picked up a yellow one. She placed it on her rectangle stick and said, "You know this is a rectangle? But...but...but this one is a smaller one." The teacher replied, "How do you know this is a rectangle?" Miao En responded, "Because here and here is long long one like this one. Then...then here and here is short. The Lego look like the bigger rectangle." The teacher repeated, "Oh, do you mean the top and bottom of the Lego block are long while the sides are short like the rectangle stick?" Miao En smiled and nodded.

Miao En proceeded to take another shape hunt stick and said, "It's a circle!" The teacher asked, "Shall we try to look for circles together? Let's try hopping around while we look for circles in the classroom." Miao En agreed and started hopping on her right foot. As she hopped around the classroom, she paused and said, "Woah! I'm falling!" She balanced herself and continued hopping until she reached the music shelf. Miao En took the drum, placed the circle stick on it and said, "I found a circle! It's the same you know! The...the...er...is the same small small one." The teacher responded, "Do you mean the size of the circle is the same? You're right, you managed to find a circle that looks just like your circle stick!" Miao En smiled and nodded.

Miao En left the music area and suggested, "I want to look for more circles. I want to jump like a frog!" She squatted, placed her arms in front like a frog and jumped around the classroom. When Miao En reached the dehumidifier, she paused and looked at the mat for a few seconds. Placing the circle stick on the mat, she shared, "Circle! This whole thing got circle! It's so big, round round one!" The teacher replied, "Yes! I like how you noticed the mat on the floor is also a circle. It's even bigger than our circle stick!" Miao En chuckled and continued jumping like a frog to other parts of the classroom.
interpretation:
Math Mind:

Miao En demonstrated her ability to match objects by both shape and size when she compared the yellow Lego block to the rectangle stick, recognizing that both shared similar attributes but differed in size. She also showed an emerging understanding of shape attributes by describing the distinguishing features of a rectangle, noting the differences between its long and short sides. When searching for circles, she was able to identify and compare objects of the same shape in different sizes, such as the drum and the large circular mat. Hence, this indicates her growing spatial awareness and ability to classify shapes based on their characteristics.


Kidzercise (Gross Motor):

Miao En exhibited balance and control in her movements while engaging in shape hunting around the classroom. As she hopped on one foot, she demonstrated coordination when she momentarily lost balance and quickly stabilized herself. She further explored movement by transitioning to frog jumps, adjusting her posture and movement to imitate a frog. Her ability to control her body while changing locomotor actions, maintaining balance, and coordinating her movements reflects her developing gross motor skills.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

Miao En develops a positive self-concept (i.e., feels good about her own competence and characteristics)

title: 《小鞋子踩一踩》
description: 在教室老师准备三个呼啦圈，以及爸爸、妈妈、宝宝鞋子照片，老师示范双脚跨进不同的呼啦圈中，踩在爸爸妈妈宝宝的鞋子上。鼓励昊霆和朋友轮流跨进不同的呼啦圈中。昊霆并拢双脚站在黄色的呼啦圈前，低头眼睛看着地下的呼啦圈。昊霆手指着呼啦圈中的图片：“Shu shu.”老师：“昊霆shoe shoe 鞋子呀，这个是谁的鞋子呢？”昊霆抬头看着老师：“爸爸.”昊霆伸出右脚向上向前跨进黄色的呼啦圈中，接着他也抬高左脚跨进黄色的呼啦圈中，昊霆双脚来回在”爸爸的鞋子“上踩，昊霆：“爸爸 爸爸shu shu .”老师：“昊霆在穿爸爸的鞋，走走走，那昊霆还要穿谁的鞋子呢？”昊霆低着头笑着看向地上的鞋子，接着重复前后脚跨进呼啦圈的动作，依次跨进剩余的全部呼啦圈中，他在不同的鞋子上来回踩。
interpretation: 昊霆在《小鞋子踩一踩》活动中能够前后脚跨进不同的呼啦圈中，同时扮演穿鞋子的动作，在鞋子上来回踩并尝试用语言介绍自己看见的物品“爸爸 爸爸shu shu.”以上的动作都展现出昊霆的粗大动作正在发展中。我们也会继续开展不同的体能活动观察昊霆的粗大动作的发展。

title: Kicking a ball
description: During Ready Steady Go Kids, the children were invited to place a ball on the cone and kick it forward into the goal post. When it was Harold’s turn, he stood on the red circle mat, gripping the teacher’s hand with a sense of security. He looked at her, his eyes filled with curiosity and a hint of hesitation. With the teacher’s encouragement, Harold took a small step forward, gaining confidence while approaching the cone. He let go of the teacher's hand and carefully kicked the ball forward with his right leg. The ball wobbled and rolled towards the goal post, landing inside. A look of joy spread across Harold's face and he bounced with excitement. The teacher lifted her hand and Harold gave her a high-five.
interpretation: Through this activity, Harold demonstrated emerging gross motor skills as he was able to kick a ball forward with minimal guidance. This activity highlighted his growing ability to coordinate his large muscles as he learns to balance, aim, and propel the ball forward. Moreover, his increasing confidence when attempting to kick the ball suggested a developing sense of body awareness and control, which are important components of gross motor development. Overall, Harold’s ability to kick the ball reflects his progress in motor development, coordination, and self-confidence, laying the foundation for continued growth in physical skills and cognitive development. Moreover, Harold also portrayed great engagement as he was able to stay focused and participate actively in the activity throughout.

title: 《好玩的面团》
description: 在操作区，老师出示面团、饼干形状模具，鼓励雨芯和朋友一起用不同形状的模型在面团上按压出来，制作形状小饼干。雨芯右手抓握拿着“方形”模具，她抬头看着老师：“kayla do.”老师：“可以啊雨芯想要印什么形状的饼干呢？”雨芯笑着说：“This 。”接着她将右手向下将方形模具放在面团上，手掌张开捏住模具向下压，接着她又用手抓握起模具，雨芯：“老师 老师look this。”老师：“雨芯的小手很厉害，可以印出一个方形饼干，你还想印什么形状吗？”雨芯从桌上抓握起圆形模具，将模具放在面团上方，拇指在下，四指并拢在上向下按压模具，将圆形印在面团上。雨芯：“老师，老师圆圆 。”老师：“老师看到了，雨芯印出了一个圆圆的饼干，太棒了！”雨芯笑着继续重复刚才的动作，用其他模具在面团上进行按压。
interpretation: 在《好玩的面团》中雨芯能够用右手抓握起模具并按压在面团上，同时她也能尝试用语言表达自己的想法和需求：”“kayla do、老师 老师look this、老师，老师圆圆 。“在整个活动过程中她能够用双手揉捏和搓面团，展现她的精细动作的技能和小手控制力正在增强，我们也会继续通过各种精细动作活动、美劳创作活动持续发展雨芯的小肌肉能力。

title: Math Mind: Shape Hunt (Integrated domain: Kidzercise)
description:
During free play time, Musa grabbed a box of shape hunt activity sticks and picked out a rectangle. Holding the rectangle stick, he walked around the classroom and noticed the class' Essential Agreement. Musa walked towards the Essential Agreement board, placed his rectangle stick on it while tiptoeing, and said, "Ms Wei Ling... That's a rectangle." The teacher responded, "How do you know that's a rectangle?" Musa replied, "Hmm... I don't know. The sides are like this." The teacher shared, "You're right, Musa! Look at the sides. The sides of the rectangle are short here, and the top and bottom are longer." Musa smiled and said, "I want to find more rectangles." The teacher suggested, "Sure! Shall we try to gallop like a horse? We can gallop and find rectangles together." Musa smiled and agreed.

Musa began galloping around the classroom with his teacher. As he noticed the Lego blocks on the floor, Musa paused, placed his rectangle stick over the blocks, and said, "That's a rectangle. The Lego is a rectangle." Musa continued galloping to the learning centre when he paused and looked at the shelves. He lifted the container with one hand, placed the rectangle stick on the activity card with the other hand, and said, "A rectangle! This one is small..."
interpretation:
Math Mind:

Musa demonstrated his ability to match objects by shape when he compared his rectangle stick to the Essential Agreement board, Lego block, and Activity Card, recognizing their shared attributes. Although he was initially unsure of how to describe a rectangle, he showed emerging shapep and spatial awareness by observing and acknowledging the shape's sides. His growing understanding of shape attributes was evident when he differentiated between a larger rectangle and a smaller one, showing an awareness of size variations within the same shape category. His ability to identify and compare rectangles in different contexts reflects his developing understanding of geometric concepts.


Kidzercise (Gross Motor):

Musa displayed balance and control as he moved through the classroom while engaging in shape hunting. He maintained stability while tiptoeing to place his rectangle stick on the Essential Agreement board and demonstrated coordination while galloping like a horse. In addition, Musa's use of both hands to lift a container while simultaneously placing the rectangle stick on the activity card showcases his coordination and ability to perform tasks requiring controlled movements.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

Musa developes a positive self-concept (i.e., feels good about his own competence and characteristics)

title: 认照片
description:
教师准备了若干幼儿们的照片，鼓励幼儿在照片中挑选出自己的照片，学习说：“这是我！”并说出其他照片上面有谁，说出同伴的名字。
      芸希坐下来看了看照片，很快就挑出来自己的照片递给老师看，老师询问她：“这是谁的照片？”芸希拍了拍自己，跟老师说：“我的照片！”随后老师指向其他的照片询问道：“那这是谁的照片？”芸希回答道：“敏瑄的！”老师继续问道：“那这张呢？”芸希点了点头，说：“是赞杰的。”接着她分别认出了淑涵和麗颖的照片，并说：“这是淑涵的！”“这是麗颖的！”
interpretation: 芸希能够在若干照片里辨认出自己的照片，并愿意与老师互动，告知老师是谁的的照片，使用华语表达说出同伴的名字，体现了她有自我意识，能够认识同伴。

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of others (saying out the names of their peers) 培养对他人的认识，如：说出同伴的名字等。
Foster sense of self-concept and identity 培养自我概念和认同感，如：能使用代词“我”。

     義腾坐下来看了看照片，很快就递给老师看自己的照片，老师询问他：“这是谁的照片？”義腾拍了拍自己，说：“我！（英文）”老师回应说：“義腾跟着老师说，我，这是我的照片！”義腾听后重复道：“我，这是我的照片。”随后老师指向其他的照片询问道：“那这是谁的照片？”義腾回答道：“赞杰（英文）的！”老师反问道：“是赞杰的吗？”義腾点了点头，说：“是赞杰的。”接着他分别认出了麗颖和淑涵的照片，并尝试说：“这是麗颖的！”“这是淑涵的！”随后他将照片贴在了墙上看着自己和朋友的照片微笑。
interpretation: 義腾能够在若干照片里辨认出自己的照片，并愿意与老师互动，告知老师是谁的的照片，说出同伴的名字，体现了他有自我意识，能够认识同伴，乐意重复老师学习华语表达。

title: Curious Works: Our Family Activity (Integrated domain: Kids Create)
description:
After collecting natural items during the outdoor walk, Audrey picked up some twigs and carefully applied white glue to them before pasting them on her paper. She arranged the twigs to form a rectangle and dipped her paintbrush in yellow paint. After painting the rectangle yellow, she continued using twigs to form a triangle above it.

Using another paintbrush, Audrey dipped it in green paint and painted the triangle. She went on to paint two more house-like structures on other parts of her paper using purple paint. The teacher asked, "I see that you're using twigs to form a rectangle and a triangle! Can you share what you made?" Audrey responded, "This one is my jie jie’s treehouse, this one is mine. Daddy is this."
interpretation:
Curious Works:

Audrey demonstrated curiosity as she explored the environment and collected natural materials like twigs back to school. She carefully examined how to use them in her artwork, thoughtfully arranging them to form recognizable shapes. By creating multiple structures and explaining their significance, Audrey showed her ability to make meaningful connections between her artwork and observations. Her engagement in using natural materials to represent real-world objects reflects her growing sense of wonder and exploration.


Kids Create:

Audrey is becoming familiar with different art media as she experimented with twigs, white glue and paint to bring her ideas to life. She showed awareness of how to use twigs to form shapes before carefully applying paint to distinguish different parts of her creation. By using yellow for the rectangle and green for the triangle, she demonstrated an understanding of colour application. Her ability to create multiple structures and experiment with paints and natural materials such as twigs highlights her growing confidence in using art materials.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

Audrey develops a positive self-concept by exhibiting a sense of autonomy and choice.

learning_goals.title: Examine new objects and environment.
Begin to become familiar with and to differentiate the application of each conventional art media.

title: 找朋友
description:
在问好时间，教师引导大家一起学习了儿歌《找朋友》，随后教师鼓励幼儿自由分组，两人一组随着儿歌做动作和同伴来玩找朋友游戏。
      在活动中，老师询问：“哪个小朋友愿意和自己的朋友一组来交朋友啊？”赞杰走了过来看向老师，说：“我！”老师询问赞杰是否愿意和峻宇一组，赞杰点了点头，和同伴相对而坐，当老师说道：“找一个朋友握握手”时，赞杰和朋友互相伸出手牵住了彼此的手，握了握手，他开心的对朋友笑，当听到：“找一个朋友拍拍手”时，他拍了拍朋友的手，当老师说道：“现在，你和峻宇已经是好朋友了，可以抱抱他了！”赞杰立马与朋友开心的拥抱。
interpretation: 在活动中，赞杰能够在老师的引导下，积极参与找朋友的游戏，并与同伴握手、拍手、拥抱，体现出他能够与同伴建立良好的社交关系。

title: 黏贴花束
description: 在制作花束的黏贴花朵过程中，老师给睿彤已经涂彩好的蛋盒花朵，蓬蓬球、彩纸叶子，鼓励睿彤进行黏贴花束活动。在老师的引导下，睿彤右手握住笔刷蘸取胶水，左手拿住蛋盒花朵，在花心刷胶水，然后放下笔刷，拇指食指捏起蓬蓬球，放到花心上，再用食指压一压，所有的花心黏好后，睿彤右手一把握住笔刷，左手压住彩纸，在彩纸上涂刷胶水，接着用右手将花朵一个一个黏在刷过胶水的位置上，最后右手拇指和食指捏起彩纸叶子，黏在彩纸上，再用手指轻轻按压。睿彤的花束完成了。老师问：“这是谁的花束好漂亮？”睿彤看看老师说：“彤彤的。”
interpretation: 从黏贴花朵的过程中，睿彤能够右手握笔刷涂花心胶水，并用拇指食指捏取蓬蓬球黏到花心处；能够左手扶住纸张，右手抓握笔刷进行涂刷胶水，拿取花朵黏贴到纸上；捏取彩纸叶子并黏到彩纸上，独立完成一系列的动作，最后完成作品，展现出睿彤精细动作有进一步发展；手眼协调能力也在进一步的发展中，逐渐能够完成一些较复杂的精细动作。

title: Read and Sequence
description:
During the Lit Attack activity, the children engaged in reading a passage with decodable words and worked collaboratively to interpret its meaning. Abhigyan actively participated in the group reading process. After a friend read the first sentence, he continued with the next, saying, "The… pet hen… got wet... Okay, it's your turn now." He followed along and took turns reading with his peers.

While sequencing the pictures, Abhigyan identified the number 10 picture card and said, "I think this is the last one," before placing it in the final box. As the group continued reading, he picked up another picture and handed it to a peer, saying, "This one. Here you go, Leanne!"

When the group had one last image left, Abhigyan observed, "This one is number 5. It is the last one. Because they went home and went to bed. We need to move this one." The group adjusted their sequence accordingly, moving the earlier image that had been placed in box number 5 and replacing it with the image of the bed. The children were also observed rereading the passage and checking it against the sequence of pictures below.
interpretation:
Abhigyan was actively engaged in decoding and reading during the Lit Attack activity. He demonstrated strong teamwork by participating in group discussions and supporting his peers. He showed kindness and cooperation by handing them picture cards and helping to arrange them in the correct sequence.


Abhigyan’s thoughtful observation about the last image showed his developing comprehension skills. He was observed reasoning to understand the flow of the passage. When rereading the passage, Abhigyan continued to self-correct when he notices that the picture does not seem to match the sentence. These reflects his developing understanding of how stories are structured and his confidence in making meaning from text.

title: 奥莉薇故事续编
description: 教师带领幼儿复习绘本《奥莉薇》，并将《奥莉薇》最后一页的情节作为起点，想象奥莉薇醒来后的一系列活动。通过自己的理解和想象来创编奥莉薇醒来后的行为。教师通过提问或给出一些示范来引导幼儿思考，例如：奥莉薇喜欢什么，她醒来后会做自己喜欢的事情吗？教师为幼儿提供材料，邀请幼儿通过绘画和仿写的方式将自己的故事分享出来。
interpretation: 嘉乐绘制的是“奥莉薇起床了，它要去找妈妈。”画中奥莉薇面带微笑，身体似乎在往前迈步，而妈妈则在房间外等待，表现出她在等待或者回应奥莉薇。这幅画充满了童趣，展现了嘉乐对绘本内容的理解和再创作能力。从奥莉薇的形象，色彩和人物动态来看，嘉乐通过绘画表达了对奥莉薇起床后去找妈妈的温馨场景，同时也反映了他对妈妈的期待和依恋。这不仅是对绘本内容的再现，也是嘉乐表达情感的一种方式。

语言学习成果（写）- 笔画与笔顺：主动地仿写短句。

interpretation: 从走拱凳桥活动中，睿彤能够自己独立站到拱凳桥上，并能慢慢走过拱凳桥，蹲下身体，左右脚先后走下拱凳，平稳站到到地面上，展现出睿彤四肢力量和身体平衡协调能力有进一步的增强与提高。

description: 在游乐场上，轩宇在球池里玩耍，这时他来到球池边，准备爬出球池，老师问：“轩宇要出来吗？”轩宇点点头，老师说：“让老师看看轩宇怎样爬出球池。”他双手抓住球池边沿，身体趴在球池沿上，接着右脚搭在球池沿上，身体用力骑在球池沿，随后左脚跟着跨出球池，双手扶住池沿，双脚落到地面，轩宇稳稳地站在地面上。然后笑眯眯地看看老师，老师称赞：“轩宇真棒！能够这么快速爬出球池。”

title: 小小设计师
description: 教师邀请幼儿回忆奥莉薇的不同穿着，然后出示图片，邀请幼儿观察和讨论奥莉薇的不同装扮，哪一件是自己最喜欢的。教师和幼儿一起讨论大家平时的衣服和装扮，鼓励幼儿用语言描述出来，并请他们说说自己觉得哪种款式的服装最漂亮。教师为幼儿提供图画纸、铅笔、剪刀、胶水以及不同质地的材料。教师鼓励幼儿发挥想象力，自由选择他们喜欢的材料和工具进行创作。教师请幼儿在图画纸上画出自己的脸，然后剪贴布料为自己设计衣服，以展示自己最漂亮的模样。
interpretation:
Abhigyan的作品主体是一个正面的自画像，由简单的线条进行勾勒。头部比例较大，眼睛涂黑，用于表现浓眉大眼的形象，耳朵也有清晰的轮廓，说明他注意到了五官的完整性。他的作品融合了绘画和拼贴，体现了他在视觉艺术方面的探索能力。他的衣领上有三个白色的纽扣，说明他观察到了服装的细节，并通过拼贴增强立体感。

从拼贴的材质选择到绘画的细节处理，都可以看出他对服装设计的兴趣和观察力。

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（写）- 笔画与笔顺：主动地仿写短句。

title: 奥莉薇故事续编
description: 教师带领幼儿复习绘本《奥莉薇》，并将《奥莉薇》最后一页的情节作为起点，想象奥莉薇醒来后的一系列活动。通过自己的理解和想象来创编奥莉薇醒来后的行为。教师通过提问或给出一些示范来引导幼儿思考，例如：奥莉薇喜欢什么，她醒来后会做自己喜欢的事情吗？教师为幼儿提供材料，邀请幼儿通过绘画和仿写的方式将自己的故事分享出来。
interpretation:
浩恩的作品画面使用了丰富的颜色，如红色、紫色、蓝色和黄色等，展现了他对世界的鲜明感知和自由表达能力。画面由几个不同的部分组成，分别代表了奥莉薇起床后的几个活动。他绘制了奥莉薇起床后打开门，去游乐场玩耍的场景。

作品展示了浩恩对绘本内容的理解和再创造能力，他不仅复述了奥莉薇的故事，还根据自己的想象力进行了故事续编。颜色和形状的搭配富有童趣，表达方式具有独特的个人风格。

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（说）- 仿编故事：在理解故事的基础上，根据故事书提供的线索展开想象，并能独自仿编故事。

慈恩照搬了绘本中“去美术馆”的去情节，还结合了自己的理解，加入了“乱七八糟”的画这一生动的描述，展现了她对故事理解以及将自己的行为投射到创作中。

新学期的第一周，孩子们学习了绘本《奥莉薇》。故事的主人公是一只小猪，它擅长很多事情，但是最擅长的事情就是把人累昏，甚至常常把自己也累昏。它会涂妈妈的口红、穿上妈妈的高跟鞋照镜子，还会吓唬弟弟。要是出门，它还会把所有的衣服都拿出来穿一遍。晴天时，它会去海边，它会把自己晒成一条大热狗；而下雨天，她则会去参观美术馆。她喜欢直接走到德加的《芭蕾排练》面前，幻想自己将来有一天也能够在大大的舞台表演。不过，也有一幅画它怎么也看不懂。回家，它就在墙上画了起来。孩子们从这只可爱的小猪身上找到了许多的共鸣，他们分享自己也会做和奥莉薇一样的事情。教师邀请他们回顾奥莉薇给他们

title: 我的身体部位
description:
描述：
       教师和幼儿坐在地板上，教师播放儿歌“身体歌”，通过儿歌帮助幼儿复习身体各部位的名称。复习身体各部位的名称后，请幼儿来到镜子面前，观察自己。 
       歆淯坐在镜子前对着镜子在做鬼脸。然后教师向歆淯提问：“歆淯，请问你的鼻子在哪里呀？”歆淯边看着镜子里的自己边指了指自己的鼻子说道：“鼻子”，教师接着提问：“歆淯，请问你的嘴巴在哪里呀？”歆淯看着镜子张开了嘴巴看出啊呜的声音，然后用手指指了下自己的嘴巴说：“嘴巴”。教师对歆淯竖起了大拇指。教师继续问道：“歆淯，请问你的屁股在哪里呀？”歆淯看着镜子摸了一下自己的肚子，教师告诉歆淯说：“歆淯这里是肚子哦，屁股在这里。”歆淯对教师点了点头，又看向镜子拍了拍自己的屁股。
interpretation:
诠释：

      歆淯在活动过程中能够持续的参与活动，并在活动中表现出快乐；通过和教师的谈话，歆淯能够指出自己的身体部位名称并说出来。

learning_goals.title: Foster sustained involvement and persistence in chosen activities 通过幼儿所选择的活动，培养持续参与和坚持性。
Foster language and expression through conversations, songs, stories and rhymes 通过谈话、歌曲、故事和儿歌，促进幼儿的理解和用短句表达能力的发展。

新学期的第一周，孩子们学习了绘本《奥莉薇》。故事的主人公是一只小猪，它擅长很多事情，但是最擅长的事情就是把人累昏，甚至常常把自己也累昏。它会涂妈妈的口红、穿上妈妈的高跟鞋照镜子，还会吓唬弟弟。要是出门，它还会把所有的衣服都拿出来穿一遍。晴天时，它会去海边，它会把自己晒成一条大热狗；而下雨天，她则会去参观美术馆。她喜欢直接走到德加的《芭蕾排练》面前，幻想自己将来有一天也能够在大大的舞台表演。不过，也有一幅画它怎么也看不懂。回家，它就在墙上画了起来。孩子们从这只可爱的小猪身上找到了许多的共鸣，他们分享自己也会做和奥莉薇一样的事情。教师邀请他们回顾奥莉薇给他们
留下了哪些印象，并鼓励他们用一句话来形容奥莉薇，例如：奥莉薇很可爱；奥莉薇喜欢画画；奥莉薇最爱玩堆沙堡……然后将自己印象最深刻的一件事情用绘画和仿写的形式记录到白纸上。

title: 小小设计师
description: 教师邀请幼儿回忆奥莉薇的不同穿着，然后出示图片，邀请幼儿观察和讨论奥莉薇的不同装扮，哪一件是自己最喜欢的。教师和幼儿一起讨论大家平时的衣服和装扮，鼓励幼儿用语言描述出来，并请他们说说自己觉得哪种款式的服装最漂亮。教师为幼儿提供图画纸、铅笔、剪刀、胶水以及不同质地的材料。教师鼓励幼儿发挥想象力，自由选择他们喜欢的材料和工具进行创作。教师请幼儿在图画纸上画出自己的脸，然后剪贴布料为自己设计衣服，以展示自己最漂亮的模样。

title: 手工奥莉薇
description:
教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。媖绮拿到粘土后，她问教师：“这个是什么颜色？”教师告诉她是‘肤色’或者‘肉色’。她听后
复述到：“肉色。”她又问：“老师，这个怎么放到鸡蛋上？”教师邀请她先把粘土揉成一个球，她一边揉，一边问：“这样对吗？”教师点点头，然后为她演示，将圆形的粘土在桌子上摊开，并告诉她就像和做印度煎饼一样。她笑着说：“我在做印度煎饼。”然后她用双手把粘土压扁，然后将粘土的边缘往外推。待她将推好的粘土贴到塑料鸡蛋上后，教师递给她一个报纸卷。她问道：“这个是什么。”教师将实先做好的奥莉薇模型举起来给她看，请她猜测用途。她观察了一下模型，说：“我知道了，是鼻子，对吗？”教师点点头示意她对了。
interpretation: 媖绮能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等，发挥自己的想象力制作属于自己的奥莉薇。

恺骏将粘土揉成一团，然后在桌上展开。他先用双手手掌将粘土压扁，然后向外推开。他一边推一边笑着说：“看，我在做RotiPrata。”他将压好的粘土贴到透明鸡蛋上。然后用手指按压和推挤不平整的地方。教师将一个报纸卷递给他，请他猜测用来做什么。他想了想说：“嗯，是Nose。”教师问他Nose华文是什么，他说道：“是鼻子。”教师点头示意他猜对了。教师邀请他像刚刚一样制作一个小的印度卷饼将报纸卷包起来。他制作好后，将包好的报纸卷粘贴到塑料鸡蛋偏上的地方。他将鼻子装好后，用在教师的引导下将手做好贴在奥莉薇身上。他告诉教师：“我要黑色的眼睛。”说完，他拿取来一些黑色粘土，然后揉成两个小球粘贴到奥莉薇脸上。
interpretation: 恺骏能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

Abhigyan跟着教师的指示，将粘土放在桌上用手揉搓成一个香肠。他一边揉搓，一边说：“看老师，我的香肠。”教师笑着点头并告诉他做的很好。他将揉成条的粘土分成两段，分别贴到了奥莉薇身体的两侧。他说道：“老师，看奥莉薇的手。”教师问他想为奥莉薇做什么样的衣服，他看了看桌子上的粘土，说：“我想要Orange。”教师告诉他是橙色，他大声复述道：“橙色。”他拿取一些橙色粘土，在桌上揉搓，推平后贴到奥莉薇身上。他说：“老师，你看。我做了衣服。”教师问他还想添加什么。他说：“我还要皇冠。”说完，他拿起一些黄色粘土，搓成
长条，贴到奥莉薇头上，然后又揉了一些黄色短条。他将黄色小条添加到长条上。他说：“我做好了！”
interpretation: Abhigyan能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。
子彬跟着教师的步骤，将粘土在桌上推成一个大的‘煎饼'，然后将‘煎饼’覆盖到透明蛋壳上制作奥莉薇的身体。他指着蛋壳上空白的部分问教师：“这个，这个怎么办？”教师为他演示将厚重的粘土慢慢推到空白处，他看了看，说：“我知道了。”然后他开始一边推一边填满空白的地方。之后，他双手握起奥莉薇的身体，用手心按压，尝试将凹凸不平的粘土整理平整。他告诉教师：“我想要Black的eye。”教师问他Black和eye的华文是什么，他想了想，说：“是黑色和眼睛。”教师将黑色粘土递给他，他捏下两小块，然后用手指捏成两个小球，粘到奥莉薇脸上。之后，他将一些红色粘土搓成条再压扁贴到奥莉薇身上。他说道：“我做衣服，红色的。因为奥莉薇穿红色的衣服。”
interpretation: 子彬能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: Math Mind: React to the Numicon! (Integrated domain: Kidzercise)
description:
During a Numeracy activity, Avery placed her hand in a feely bag to choose a Numicon piece. When she took out a 3-piece Numicon, she chuckled and said, "3..." The teacher asked, "Can you think of an action that your friends need to do three times?" Avery pondered for a while before replying, "Er... turn around and hi-five." The teacher repeated Avery’s suggestion and encouraged the group to follow the action. Avery and her friends enthusiastically turned around and gave high-fives three times. 

Later, when another child picked a 9-piece Numicon, Avery and the other friends joined in and counted the circles together. When the teacher asked how many the Numicon piece represented, Avery and the other children responded, "Nine!" As her friend suggested to run around the pillar for nine times, Avery participated in running nine rounds around a pillar, laughing as she completed the task.
interpretation:
Math Mind:

Avery demonstrated her ability to match numbers with quantity by recognizing the numeral "3" on the Numicon piece and relating it to an action done three times. She also showed engagement in counting by actively participating in counting the circles on a 9-piece Numicon alongside her peers. As Avery ran around the pillar, she was able to count, match her movements to the quantity, and return to the starting point upon completion. This indicates her growing confidence in associating number names with their corresponding quantities.


Kidzercise:

Avery displayed coordination and control in her gross motor skills as she turned her body and gave high-fives as part of the group activity. In addition, when challenged to run nine rounds around the pillar, Avery sustained her movement and successfully completed all rounds, demonstrating endurance and spatial awareness. Her ability to coordinate her movements while engaging in playful physical activities indicates developing strength, balance, and control over her body.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

Avery develops a positive self-concept by feeling good about her own competence and characteristics.

title: Fingerprint Exploration
description: Children explored the process by using their fingers to press onto ink pads and then transfer the imprint onto paper, discovering the effects of this hands-on activity.
interpretation:
With encouragement from her teacher, Shuyin first decided to try the black ink pad. After pressing her fingers onto it, she observed her hands turning black and noted, "They're all black and dirty." Her teacher reassured her that it would wash off. Shuyin pressed her finger onto the paper, then tilted it upwards to examine the imprint. After noticing the small lines, she used a magnifying glass for a closer look.


She experimented with different fingers using her sense of touch to feel the ink on her fingers and saw how it transferred to the paper, observing that her thumb made a larger print while her pinky left a smaller one. She used both red and black ink pads and noticed the different patterns she could create. This sparked her curiosity, and she became eager to experiment with all her different fingers to create fingerprints patterns.


Through this activity, Shuyin demonstrated her ability to use her senses and simple tools, like the magnifying glass, to explore both living and non-living things. Her growing interest in investigating objects and her ability to communicate her findings show her developing cognitive, sensory, and fine motor skills.

description: 老师提供一个彩虹伞和皮球，邀请并鼓励欣恩和朋友们一起进行彩虹伞游戏。老师请欣恩拉着彩虹伞的一个角和朋友们走圆圈，一会进一会儿出，老师又将皮球放到彩虹伞上，欣恩和老师、朋友一起拉着彩虹伞让皮球在里面滚动，接着欣恩和老师、朋友们一起将彩虹伞抛起来，大家钻进彩虹伞下面，哈哈哈地笑着。就这样在老师的带领下欣恩和朋友们变换着方式玩着游戏。游戏结束后，老师问：“欣恩和朋友一起玩游戏开心吗？”欣恩笑着看看老师。

Raylan was excited to try the ink pad of his choice, red then black. As he pressed his fingers onto the ink, he noticed his hands turning black and exclaimed, "Look, my hand is red!" His teacher reassured him that it was okay and would come off after washing his hands. With guidance, Raylan pressed his finger onto the paper and tilted his head sideways to closely observe the result. He noticed the imprints had lines and, using a magnifying glass, he excitedly pointed out the small lines to the teacher. This sparked his curiosity, and he became eager to experiment with all his different fingers or different colours to create fingerprints, fascinated by the patterns he could make. He also could recognise and compare his peers' fingerprints based on their size and shape, “Engracia’s finger is the smallest and Zac has the biggest!”


Through this activity, Raylan demonstrated his ability to use his senses and simple tools, like the magnifying glass, to explore both living and non-living things. He used his sense of touch to feel the ink on his fingers and saw how it transferred to the paper, while also keenly observing the fine details of the fingerprints. His growing interest in investigating objects and his ability to communicate his findings show his developing cognitive, sensory, and fine motor skills.

interpretation:
Shuo-Yun demonstrated growing engagement with the book and a little bit of the audio. With guidance and encouragement, he observed the teacher to learn how to read. He was able to put on the headphones with some assistance.


Initially, Shuo-Yun looked through the book, pointing to pictures of objects like a girl, car, and marker, but he didn’t want to use the audio. He was able to recognise the images and named them accordingly, “Car” and “Marker!” After a second attempt with the volume lowered, and with some gentle guidance, he began to follow along with the audio. He was able to turn the pages in sync with the pacing of the book and, with a few verbal cues from the teacher, such as "flip the page," he successfully read along while flipping the pages.


By the third reading, Shuo-Yun was able to read most of the sentences in the book aloud after the audio. He was occasionally able to read while pointing to one or two words. This shows his developing listening, word recognition, and comprehension skills as he connects visuals with text and demonstrates an understanding of the content.

title: 情绪娃娃
description: 老师请幼儿们围坐在自己身边，播放儿歌《情绪歌》，请他们听听歌曲里唱到了哪些情绪，然后提供开心、哭泣、生气、害怕四种表情的人偶娃娃，鼓励睿萱尝试说出表情娃娃的心情怎样，再说说自己心情怎样？睿萱先拿到开心表情的人偶娃娃，看了看，，老师问：“睿萱你拿到什么表情的娃娃？”她拿起来给老师看说：“开心。”但睿萱的表情没有显得开心，老师又请她再拿一个，老师问：“睿萱拿的表情娃娃，是什么表情？”睿萱没有回答，但睿萱皱了皱眉头，放下表情娃娃，接着又拿起一个伤心哭泣的表情娃娃。接着就想要哭了，老师问：“睿萱看到哭泣的娃娃想要哭，是吗？”睿萱说：“I want dad mummy.”老师安慰她，睿萱慢慢平静下来。
interpretation: 从《情绪娃娃》活动中，睿萱能与老师的对话，并能与老师、朋友分享自己的表情和心情，并且在老师的安慰下平静下来，展现出睿萱能与同伴、老师互动建立良好关系；对老师有信任感。

title: Guided Reading
description: The children were introduced to book awareness and learned how to use a book during the guided reading activity. They began to recognise sight words like "I," "am," and "like," and applied reading techniques such as using pictures for word prediction and pointing to each word while listening to the audio.
interpretation:
Kai En demonstrated engagement with the book and audio. With prompting, he observed the teacher and his peers to learn how to read. He was able to put on the headphones by himself with little to no assistance. Kai En followed the instructions with slight repetition, such as opening the book, repeating words, and pointing to the words as he read. For example, he needed a little more explanation to understand and follow the teacher's instructions and demonstration, when asked to open the book and repeat the words.


When listening to the audio, Kai En often repeated the last word or two of a phrase, such as "like" after hearing "I like reading." Gradually, he started to say the whole sentence. For example, after hearing the audio for "My teacher likes me," he would repeat the entire sentence. When asked to read a page without the audio, he could read parts of the sentence using the pictures to help him guess the words, like recognising the picture of a child writing on paper and saying "writing" when reading "I like writing.” This reflects his developing listening, word recognition, and comprehension skills, as he connects visuals with text and demonstrates an understanding of the read-aloud content.

title: February Show and Tell
description: Children are invited this February to share and talk about their favourite activity to do on weekends. This activity encourages self-expression as each child describes what they love to do, why it’s special to them, and what makes their weekend fun.
interpretation:
Zacchaeus brought his blue soccer ball and explained that he enjoys playing and kicking the ball with his daddy at the park on weekends. Using 4 to 5-word sentences, he clearly communicated the location ("I go to park"), the time ("I play on weekends"), and the activity ("I kick ball with daddy"). Through his actions, he demonstrated how he kicks and throws the ball, mimicking the movements of playing with the ball. 


When asked why he chose a ball, Zacchaeus was able to understand and respond, “I like balls and my daddy plays balls with me,” showing his ability to reason about his preferences and explain the bond he shares with his father during their weekend activity.

Zacchaeus displayed strong communication skills, using both verbal explanations and physical demonstrations to convey his favourite weekend activity, showing his ability to express thoughts clearly and effectively.

title: 逃家小兔故事续编
description: 教师邀请幼儿想一想，如果自己是故事里的小兔子，当他们想要逃离妈妈的时候会想要变成什么。然后妈妈如果想追到小兔一个话题展开讨论”的学习子并把它抓回家，又会变成什么。教师邀请幼儿使用句式“如果你变成……，我就变成……”来分享自己的故事。之后，老师为他们提供了彩色铅笔、马克笔、剪刀和纸，鼓励他们将刚刚分享的内容绘制到白纸上，然后用剪刀剪下一些图案或者图画粘贴到作品上制作一副长轴画。

title: My ‘Not a Box’ Project
description:
After reading the story Not a Box, the children were invited to create their own "not a box" structures using different pieces of cardboard. Prior to the activity, the children were challenged to transform 2D cardboard pieces into 3D structures. We watched a video and learned 10 different ways to connect cardboard pieces. While creating their structures, the children used various techniques depending on their design goals.

Abhigyan created a design inspired by the environment. After planning his design, he began collecting materials, starting with cardboard pieces and cardboard rolls. He observed his peers for inspiration before focusing on his own work. Abhigyan was seen cutting small tabs around the bottom of a cardboard roll. As he worked, he carefully ensured the tabs were evenly spaced, applying what he had seen in the demonstration video. He folded the tabs outward and secured them with tape. Proud of his creation, Abhigyan exclaimed, “Look! I made a tree!”

The teacher encouraged him to think about what else he could add to make it look more like a tree. Abhigyan replied, “I think I can add the leaves on top.” He took a rectangular piece of cardboard and cut a slot midway on both the rectangle and the cardboard roll. “I know! I can use the slot and put this on top,” he said as he slotted the cardboard piece onto the top of the roll, creating a canopy for his tree.

Next, Abhigyan continued building his bridge. He selected a long piece of cardboard and used a ruler to guide him. Applying the "bend" method, he made even creases along the cardboard, allowing it to curve into the shape of a bridge.
interpretation:
Abhigyan’s participation in this activity highlights his growing creativity and problem-solving abilities. He demonstrated resourcefulness and applied prior knowledge when exploring various ways to connect and construct 3D forms. His ability to recall techniques and adapt them to suit his design goals reflects a deepening understanding of structure and stability.


When encouraged to expand on his ideas, Abhigyan showed critical thinking and flexibility, considering new ways to enhance his design. His confidence and willingness to experiment illustrate his sense of agency and enthusiasm for learning through hands-on exploration. He also exhibited strong planning and precision skills, using tools thoughtfully to achieve his desired outcome. This experience provided a rich opportunity for Abhigyan to develop essential skills across multiple domains while fostering self-expression and confidence in his abilities as a designer and builder.

title: Partner Toss Challenge
description:
As part of our Kidzercise game, the children participated in a Partner Toss Challenge, where they practiced throwing and catching a ball with a partner. This activity focused on developing hand-eye coordination, control, and teamwork. The children started with short, gentle throws and gradually increased the distance as they gained more confidence. The challenge encouraged them to throw accurately and catch consistently while staying engaged with their partner.

Abhigyan was first given the task of throwing the ball. Excited to begin, he immediately tossed the ball toward his partner. After the first throw, his partner mentioned that she was not ready. Abhigyan responded by asking, “Ok, I will wait for you. Are you ready now?” Upon receiving confirmation, Abhigyan threw the ball again. Throughout the activity, Abhigyan experimented with different throwing strengths. When he tried throwing the ball with more force, it went past his partner. When he threw it more gently, the ball fell short. Although he did not reach the target, Abhigyan practiced adjusting the strength of his throws after each turn.

When it was his turn to catch the ball, Abhigyan showed improved body posture by leaning forward and stretching out his arms to reach the ball. At certain moments, he squinted his eyes as he felt the ball approaching, staying focused on tracking it as it came closer.
interpretation:
Through this activity, Abhigyan showed increased focus and experimentation with both throwing and catching the ball. As he practiced different throwing strengths, he demonstrated an understanding of how adjusting his throw could impact the distance and accuracy. Although he didn’t always reach the target, Abhigyan was engaged in the process of trial and error, which allowed him to refine his skills and experiment with different techniques.


When it was his turn to catch, Abhigyan displayed improved posture and awareness of his body’s position, demonstrating an understanding of how to properly prepare for a catch. His focus on tracking the ball, indicated by his squinting, shows that he is actively working on his hand-eye coordination and beginning to recognize the importance of focus when catching.


Abhigyan’s involvement in both throwing and catching indicates that he is on the path to becoming more confident and skilled in both activities. With continued practice, he will further develop his control, accuracy, and consistency in both throwing and catching.

title: Read and Sequence
description:
During the Lit Attack activity, the children engaged in reading a passage with decodable words and worked together to interpret its meaning. Arielle waited patiently while her partner read the first sentence. She then read the second sentence slowly, “He… is… a… /c/ /o/ /p/. Cuuh-o-p. Cop.” In the fourth sentence, Arielle read, “The dog… hid… in a bo… /x/… box.” She continued to the last sentence, saying, “The dog /h/ /o/ /p/ /s/… h…o…p… hop…s… hops on Tom.”

After finishing the passage, the pair looked at the pictures to match them to the sentences. As her friend picked up a picture to match the first sentence, Arielle said, “Yes… yes… it is correct because it shows the cop.” She then picked up a picture of the cop holding a dog for the sentence, “Tom went to find a dog.” Later, Arielle noticed there was no image to match the sentence, “Tom found the dog.” She discussed this with her partner, saying, “But if we put this one here, we cannot match it to the sentence ‘The dog hops on Tom.’”

After reasoning and discussing together, Arielle and her partner decided to rearrange the pictures. They replaced the first picture with an image of Tom the cop standing in front of a police station, explaining that it showed more clearly that Tom is a police officer.
interpretation: Arielle is developing her early reading and comprehension skills. During the Lit Attack activity, she used her decoding strategies to read new words and took her time to blend and pronounce them correctly. Arielle showed great problem-solving skills and reasoning as she carefully matched the pictures to the sentences. She also demonstrated strong communication skills by discussing her ideas with her partner and explaining her thinking. When she noticed that one picture didn’t match, Arielle worked with her partner to solve the problem, showing flexibility and teamwork. Her ability to reflect, adjust her choices, and collaborate with others highlights her growing confidence as a learner and her emerging leadership skills.

title: 手工奥莉薇
description:
教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。
子萱接过教师递给她的黏土，她说：“肉色。”教师点点头，告诉她也叫肤色，皮肤的肤。她笑着复述道：“肤色。”然后她将黏土放到桌上开始揉搓。然后，她用手掌按压黏土。她将黏土压扁后，用手指将黏土的边缘往四周推，尝试制作黏土‘煎饼’。待她制作好后，她将黏土煎饼覆盖到透明鸡蛋上。她指着鸡蛋上空白处问：“谢老师，这里怎么做？”教师邀请她先按压黏土厚重的地方，然后将多余的黏土推挤到空白处。听后，她开始按压和推挤黏土。教师递给她一个报纸卷，她问：“这个是什么？”教师邀请她猜测，她想了想，说：“我知道了，是鼻子。”教师点点头，邀请她用同样的方式制作一个小的黏土煎饼。待她做好后，她用黏土煎饼将报纸卷包裹起来，粘贴到奥莉薇的身体上。然后将奥莉薇鼻子和身体处的通过黏土推挤、按压衔接到一起。
interpretation: 子萱能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: 手工奥莉薇
description:
教师将奥莉薇手工展示给幼儿，鼓励他们观察立体的奥莉薇模型。然后出示手工所需要的材料，粘土、塑料鸡蛋、弹珠等材料。教师带领幼儿一步一步地制作奥莉薇手工。首先将肉色粘土揉成球，然后像摊印度煎饼一样在桌上展开。待他们摊开后，将粘土包裹在鸡蛋上。包裹好后，使用粘土和报纸卷制作奥莉薇的鼻子。之后，将粘土揉成四个“迷你小香肠”制作奥莉薇地手和脚。教师将参考图发给幼儿，邀请他们选择自己喜欢的图案制作奥莉薇的衣服和装饰。
家乐将黏土放到桌上用手揉搓。他将黏土搓成一个球后，用手掌按压黏土，然后用手指将黏土的四周往外推，将黏土推成一个‘大饼’。他将黏土大饼覆盖到透明鸡蛋上，按压和推挤黏土厚重的地方，将鸡蛋上的空白处都覆盖好。他用同样的方式制作了一个小的黏土饼，他将黏土饼覆盖到报纸卷上，然后将贴到奥莉薇身上制作奥莉薇的鼻子。教师又递给他一些黏土，他跟着教师的指引将黏土揉搓成条‘香肠’，然后分成两条‘香肠’和两条‘迷你香肠’。他将长条贴到奥莉薇的身体两边，制作它的手。他又将两条迷你‘香肠’贴在奥莉薇的身体下方，制作坐着的奥莉薇的脚。
interpretation: 家乐能够跟着教师的讲解，一步一步地使用粘土发挥自己的想象力制作手工奥莉薇。在教师的引导下，能够在制作过程中，耐心思考如何将粘土揉搓成不同的形状大小、进行颜色搭配等。

title: 颜色排序
description:
教师带领幼儿观察一些不同风格的绘画作品，鼓励他们细心观察。通过讨论，引导他们注意颜色的不同层次。例如，画面中有些部分使用了明亮的色调，而其他部分则使用了较深的颜色。从而引出颜色深浅的概念。教师出示色块，请幼儿观察这些颜色，带领他们从深到浅或从浅到深排列这些色块。之后，教师请幼儿创作色彩排序画，鼓励幼儿使用水彩颜料，按照从深到浅或者从浅到深的顺序选择颜料盘里的颜色，绘制出自己喜欢的图形进行排序。最后，教师邀请幼儿选择一种排序方式，将6张深浅不一的色卡按照选择的方式进行排序。
嘉乐问道：“Is it from dark to light?"教师告诉他dark是深，light是浅。他复述道：“Dark深，light浅，从深到浅。”教师邀请他从水彩颜料盘里选择5个颜色，进行深浅排序。他指着色彩盘里的蓝色看向教师，教师告诉他可以，但是下一个颜色要比这个颜色更浅。他蘸取一些蓝色，他一边画一边说：“Rabbit。”教师问他华文是什么。他说：“兔子。”教师夸他真棒。他笑着有蘸取了一些红色画到蓝色的前面。教师问他红色深还是蓝色深，他抿着嘴笑着不回答。教师告诉他是蓝色深，所以红色应该在蓝色的后面。他点点头，继续选颜色。等他完成绘制后，教师出示两个白板，介绍上面写的排序要求。嘉乐指着从浅到深说：“这个。”教师告诉他是从浅到深，他复述道：“从浅到深。”他拿起卡片看了看，教师告诉他白色是浅色。他将白色放在最前面，接着是黄色、绿色、粉红色。教师提醒他仔细观察绿色和粉红色哪个更浅，他看了看，将绿色和粉红色的位置调换了一下。
interpretation: 嘉乐通过观察绘画作品学习颜色的变化，学会了区分颜色的深浅。在教师的引导下，通过动手实践，选取色彩盘里的颜色和色卡按照要求排序，加深了对颜色深浅的理解，逐渐培养了对艺术作品色彩运用的感知力。

title: I can tell a story
description:
Devan and Tresor was exploring the character puppets from the book 'Painting a Picture' during Guided Reading session. He and Tresor opened the puppet bag and took out all the puppets. Whilst doing so, Devan looked at Tresor and said " See, she draw the mountain." as he was pulling out the puppets. Tresor replied him and said "yes, then later she will pant more things" In which, Devan responded and said "ya, have cow, then river also."

Once they are done with taking out all the puppets, Devan and Tresor described the various puppets to one another as they took turns to become the painter in the book and shared what they had painted. 

As they kept away the puppets after the exploration, Tresor asked Devan " you like to paint?" Devan answered that he liked painting and that he liked the colour red.
interpretation:
From the brief interaction that Devan had with his peer, he had displayed the ability to gain meaning by listening as Tresor shared about her knowledge on the guided reading book. 


He was also able to express himself clearly as his peers understood what he was sharing and responded accurately. However, he would need to work on his vovubulary bank as he tended to speak to speak in short sentences.

learning_goals.title: Gain meaning by listening.
Use expanded vocabulary and language for a variety of purposes.
Speak clearly and convey ideas effectively.

教师带领幼儿观察一些不同风格的绘画作品，鼓励他们细心观察。通过讨论，引导他们注意颜色的不同层次。例如，画面中有些部分使用了明亮的色调，而其他部分则使用了较深的颜色。从而引出颜色深浅的概念。教师出示色块，请幼儿观察这些颜色，带领他们从深到浅或从浅到深排列这些色块。之后，教师请幼儿创作色彩排序画，鼓励幼儿使用水彩颜料，按照从深到浅或者从浅到深的顺序选择颜料盘里的颜色，绘制出自己喜欢的图形进行排序。最后，教师邀请幼儿选择一种排序方式，将6张深浅不一的色卡按照选择的方式进行排序。
慈恩告诉教师：“我要画星星。”说完，她蘸取了一些粉红色颜料在白纸上画出一颗粉色的星星。她说：“我要从浅到深，这个是很浅的粉红色。”说完，她看了看颜料，说：“我要橙色。”她又在纸上画出一颗橙色的星星。待她画完后，她说：“谢老师，你看。我画好了，从浅到深。”教师出示两块分别写有从深到浅和从浅到深的白板，问她想要进行哪个排列顺序。她看了看，指着其中一块白板说道：“我要这个，从深到浅。”说完，她观察了一下卡片。然后拿出黑色卡片放在最前面，她一边放，一边说：“黑色，蓝色，绿色，粉色，黄色，白色。我好了。”
interpretation: 慈恩通过观察绘画作品学习颜色的变化，学会了区分颜色的深浅。还通过动手实践，选取色彩盘里的颜色和色卡按照要求排序，加深了对颜色深浅的理解，逐渐培养了对艺术作品色彩运用的感知力。

title: Exploring with coloured blocks
description:
During outdoor time, Jumaius was engaged in an exploration activity using see-through coloured blocks (e.g. red, blue, green, and yellow) to look at the world around them. He took a yellow coloured block and held it up to the light, observing how they changed the appearance of the environment around him. 

The teacher went over to him and asked, "What colour did you see around you, Jumaius?" He responded by pointing in front of him. The teacher prompted him, "Did you see the colour yellow? Say yellow." Jumaius nodded and said softly, "Yellow." The teacher acknowledged him and expanded on his words, "Yes, you see yellow! Let's try looking at the trees over there! What did you see?" Jumaius smiled and said, "Tree!" The teacher nodded and passed Jumaius a red coloured block, "What happens if we look through the red one?" 

He took the red coloured block from the teacher, prompting him to continue his exploration.
interpretation:
Throughout the activity, Jumaius demonstrated curiosity, problem-solving, and sensory exploration. The teacher's warm presence and guided questioning supported his sense of security and attachment, allowing him to engage in the activity in a safe and secure environment.


By being present and interacting with him, the teacher was able to make Jumaius feel valued and supported as he moved around the outdoor area and explored with ease. Additionally, the interaction with the teacher also helped to foster attachment and trust as the teacher reinforced Jumaius' confidence in exploring and expressing his thoughts. The shared enjoyment of exploration supports a positive teacher-child relationship, hence reinforcing the teacher's role as both a guide and a secure attachment figure. Moreover, Jumaius also demonstrated respect as he was able to listen attentively to the teacher's questions and responded appropriately.

title: 这是谁的水壶
description: 老师邀请幼儿将他们的水壶放在一起，带领幼儿玩游戏《这是谁的水壶》。老师一个一个指着水壶，请幼儿说出这是谁的水壶？老师指到耀曦的水壶问：“这是谁的水壶？”耀曦马上回答：“耀曦的。”接着老师让耀曦自己拿起一个朋友的水壶，老师问：“这是谁的水壶？”耀熙回答：“Husna的水壶。”老师说：“对，是Husna的水壶，请你把水壶给她好吗？”耀曦把水壶递给了Husna。老师说：“谢谢耀曦！”
interpretation: 从《这是谁的水壶》活动中，当老师指到耀曦的水壶问是谁的水壶时，耀曦马上回答自己的名字；老师请他拿起朋友的水壶并说说是谁的水壶时，耀曦也能够认出水壶是谁的，说出朋友的名字；把水壶给朋友，耀曦能够指认自己和朋友的物品，展现出耀曦的自我意识和对他人的认识进一步增强。

interpretation: 从《这是谁的水壶》活动中，当老师指到凯翔的水壶问是谁的水壶时，凯翔马上回答自己的名字；老师请他拿起朋友的水壶并说说是谁的水壶时，凯翔也能够认出水壶是谁的，说出朋友的名字；把水壶给朋友，凯翔能够指认自己和朋友的物品，展现出凯翔的自我意识和对他人的认识进一步增强。

title: 量词配对
description:
教师出示奥莉薇的着装图，带领他们一起讨论奥莉薇的衣服和饰品。然后邀请幼儿分享他们最喜欢的服装，鼓励他们分享自己的穿戴，引导他们关注这类物品。接着，告诉幼儿，“今天我们要学一种有趣的东西，叫做‘量词’。量词是用来数东西的，比如帽子，我们用‘一顶’来数。展示每一件服饰物品，并解释与其配套的量词。将量词卡片（如“顶”、“双”等）与相应的服饰物品放在桌子上，邀请幼儿根据物品选择正确的量词卡片并配对。
教师邀请媖绮参与活动，媖绮看了看卡片上的图片说：“我知道这个，奥莉薇红色的裙子。”教师邀请她找出字卡-裙子，并粘贴到活动板上。她看了看，拿起一张卡片说：“裙子。”待她贴好后，教师问她裙子应该用哪个量词，她答道：“一个裙子。”教师告诉她应该是一条裙子，并邀请她将字卡-条贴到活动板上。教师又出示一张图卡，问媖绮奥莉薇手上有什么。她说：“手套。”她看了看，从卡片堆里选出拿出字卡-手套贴到活动板上，教师问她手套要用什么量词，她想了想，说：“是一双。”她看了看字卡，手在量词卡中间徘徊。教师提醒双字是两个一样的字组合在一起。她拿起字卡-双，贴到了制定地点。然后读道：“一双手套。”
interpretation: 媖绮能够说出一些常见的服饰和量词的名称，能够理解不同物品对应了不同的量词，并将服饰和量词进行搭配。

title: Artwork sample: Butterfly Craft with Cake Filters
description:
Children created their own beautiful butterflies using cake filters! The process starts with children scribbling various shapes and patterns onto the cake filter with colourful markers. Once the design is complete, they drop some water onto the filter paper, watching in awe as the ink spreads and creates a stunning, blended effect across the paper. 

The filter paper was then folded in a pleated manner to form the wings of a butterfly.

This craft introduces children to the concept of how colours can blend and spread when water is added. It is also a way to develop their fine motor skills and understanding of cause and effect to foster an interest in art.

"What colours do you see in your butterfly?" the teacher asked.
"Black and pink," replied Matteo.

title: Animal Finger Puppet Play- Old MacDonald
description:
Cole is engaged in a finger puppet play through a song “Old MacDonald Had a Farm”. Educarer provided him with animal finger puppets for him to manipulate and explore with.

Cole was sitting on the floor in front of his educarer. Educarer invited him while prompting him the animal puppets arranged on the wooden puppet holder, “Cole, look what I have? I have many animals. Cole smiled in response and excitedly took the duck. “Oh, you like the duck.” Educarer said. Cole giggled gaily and babbled “du duck” while showing it to his educarer. “Yes! That’s right. It’s a duck.” Educarer answered him back. He then manipulated the duck and inserted it into his finger. Educarer started singing, “Old MacDonald had a farm, e, i, e, i,o. And on his farm he had some ducks, e, i, e, i o.” Cole was smiling and swayed his body left to right while listening to his educarer. With a duck puppet on his finger, he also moved it up and down. “Oh! Good dancing Cole.” Educarer praised him. After playing with the duck, he took the dog and said “du duck”. Educarer told him, “Cole, it’s a dog.” and continued singing the song “with a woof woof here and a woof woof there”. Cole tried babbling the sound “oof oof”. “Yes, you are right. The dog says, “woof, woof”, educarer explained. He then continued dancing while manipulating the puppet as educarer sang the song. 

Cole took the pig and also picked up the horse puppet on his other hand. He extended his left arm and showed the pig puppet to his educarer while saying “du duck”. “Oh! Oh! That’s a pig. And the pig says, “Oink! Oink!” educarer explained. As educarer continued singing, Cole stood up and bounced his body up and down. He was smiling and giggling while stomping his feet and swaying his hands with the puppets. “Wow! Good dancing Cole.” Educarer applauded him.
interpretation:
• Cole displayed strong interests in animals. He expressed his enjoyment in playing and manipulating the animal finger puppets during puppet play. He displayed high level of happiness, trust, confidence, curiosity and positive interactions during the activity.
  • He also shown strong interests in music and movements. He loves and enjoys dancing as he listened to songs and music.
  • Cole demonstrated good social interactions towards his educarer and sustained involvement during the activity. He was able to respond with enjoyment to his educarer through smiling, giggling, babbling and hand gestures.

title: Read and Sequence
description:
During the Lit Attack activity, the children engaged in reading a passage with decodable words and worked together to interpret its meaning. After reading, they were tasked with matching pictures to the sentences. Bowen began by reading the first sentence from the passage slowly, “Tim is a… kid.” After reading, Bowen turned to the images to find the matching picture. A friend noticed a picture of a boy and passed it to him. Bowen responded, “Yes, thank you.”

Bowen listened and observed attentively as his peers continued reading the passage. On his next turn, he read the sentence, “Tim… got his bag… with… a… zip.” He immediately picked up a picture of a bag and placed it in box number four.

Bowen worked collaboratively with his peers, checking each picture they picked up to ensure it matched the correct sentence. The group observed reasoning and discussed the order of their pictures. They re-reading the sentences carefully and reviewed the pictures to confirm their choices.
interpretation:
Bowen is developing his early reading and comprehension skills, demonstrating confidence in decoding simple sentences. During the Lit Attack activity, he read each sentence carefully, taking calculated pauses to blend the sounds in his head before reading the words aloud, without needing to individually decode each letter. Bowen also showed strong problem-solving skills by identifying and matching pictures to the sentences independently. His response, “Yes, thank you,” highlights his growing social skills and ability to work cooperatively with others.


Bowen’s attentive listening and observation skills were evident as he followed along while his peers read and contributed to the group’s success. He actively participated in discussions about the order of the pictures, demonstrating reasoning and critical thinking. His willingness to collaborate and check the group’s work shows his developing ability to engage in shared learning experiences with confidence and focus.

title: Threading Straws
description:
Cole was provided with jumbo dinking straws cut into pieces and a puppet wooden holder for him to engage in threading.

Educarer invited Cole to sit on the floor while showing him the materials. “Cole, look! I have some colourful straws for you. Let’s do threading ” educarer told him. Cole excitedly extended his right arm into the bin with straws and happily took some of them. “Do you know what we are going to do with these straws? Educarer asked him. Cole looked at her and babbled “ta ta” while showing him the straws. “Look, I pick up the straw with my pincer grasp and thread it here.” Educarer described the actions while showing him the process. Cole smiled and quickly dropped the straws back into the bin. Using his pincer grasp, he took one of the straws. “Yes, we take the straw one at a time” educarer explained. While holding the straw, he slowly aimed it into the stick (which size was same as the straw’s hole- which is challenging).  After adjusting and repositioning, he managed to insert the straw and pushed it down slowly. “Yay! You did it! Good threading Cole.” Educarer praised him. Cole smiled at her and clapped his hands in response. 

Cole continued doing the activity. With good pincer grasp and hand-eye coordination, he held the straw gently and threaded it into the stick. As the straw went in halfway, using his palm, he then pushed it down all the way to the bottom. “Wow! You did it well Cole.” educarer applauded him. He smiled and babbled “ta ta” in response. He continued threading the remaining straws. He picked them up one by one using his pincer and palmar grasp alternately. While threading, he looked so focused and determined by slowly eyeing the stick and poking the straw into it. He managed to thread all the straws into the puppet wooden holder.
interpretation:
• Cole’s fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination are developing very well. He displayed good pincer and palmar grasp while manipulating the materials. He demonstrated good hand-eye coordination while aiming the straws to the wooden stick holder to thread them. While threading, he displayed good control and coordination while readjusting and repositioning his hand/material.
  • As observed, he also displayed increasing sustained concentration and persistence during the entire activity.

title: Artwork sample: Butterfly Craft with Cake Filters
description:
Children created their own beautiful butterflies using cake filters! The process starts with children scribbling various shapes and patterns onto the cake filter with colourful markers. Once the design is complete, they drop some water onto the filter paper, watching in awe as the ink spreads and creates a stunning, blended effect across the paper. 

The filter paper was then folded in a pleated manner to form the wings of a butterfly.

This craft introduces children to the concept of how colours can blend and spread when water is added. It is also a way to develop their fine motor skills and understanding of cause and effect to foster an interest in art.

"Wow, look at all the colours you used on your butterfly!," said the teacher.
"Pink and black," James added.

title: Partner Toss Challenge
description:
As part of our Kidzercise game, the children participated in a Partner Toss Challenge, where they practiced throwing and catching a ball with a partner. This activity focused on developing hand-eye coordination, control, and teamwork. The children started with short, gentle throws and gradually increased the distance as they gained more confidence. The challenge encouraged them to throw accurately and catch consistently while staying engaged with their partner.

Bowen was first given the task of catching the ball. As his friend threw the ball, she noticed that Bowen was holding the catching pad but was not reaching out to catch it. She encouraged him to track the ball and extend his arm to catch it. Bowen listened and applied these strategies. While he missed the ball by only a small margin, his adjustments showed growth in awareness and technique.

When it was his turn to throw, Bowen confidently called out, “I’m ready!” before making his throw. He swung his hands back and moved them from his right side to his left, which caused the ball to go sideways. With gentle guidance from the teacher, Bowen practiced extending his arm forward for a more controlled and accurate throw. After a few tries, he successfully adjusted his movement and threw the ball in the correct direction.
interpretation:
Bowen’s participation in the Partner Toss Challenge demonstrated his willingness to listen, learn, and apply new strategies. When tasked with catching, Bowen initially showed hesitation when he did not fully extend his arm. However, he was receptive to feedback and quickly attempted to focus more on the ball and actively reach out to catch it. Although he did not catch the ball on his first few tries, his effort and perseverance were evident as he continued to adjust his technique, gradually getting closer to success.


When it was his turn to throw, Bowen’s enthusiasm was clear as he called out to his friend to get their attention. This demonstrated his confidence and readiness to participate. His initial throw was off-target, but with guidance, he learned to adjust his body movements, leading to a more accurate throw. This process reflects Bowen’s ability to adapt and grow his eye-hand coordination. Bowen is gradually developing both his physical skills and his ability to respond positively to guidance. With continued practice, Bowen will likely gain even more confidence in his coordination and teamwork.

title: Jump and Land
description:
In this Kidzercise activity, Charis and her peers participated in a jumping challenge that involves jumping over obstacles for distance, and jumping for height. After a short warm-up session, the children were guided through proper jumping technique which focuses on using both feet to jump and land while bending their knees to soften the impact. The children were also encouraged to swing their arms to propel their bodies forward.

When it was Charis’ turn, she coordinated her arm movements with how she bent her knees to build momentum. She was observed bending her knees before propelling herself forward. However, when she landed, she kept her knees locked, which caused her to lose balance. Charis tried again and focused on bending her knees. She was observed bending her knees slightly upon landing to cushion the impact. Upon landing, Charis was able to regain her balance more quickly than before.

During the next jumping for height challenge, Charis applied the same strategy. She was also observed taking her time, as advised by the teachers, ensuring she didn’t rush through the movements.
interpretation:
Charis showed increasing control and focus in her jumping skills. She coordinated her arm movements and bent her knees to build momentum before jumping. At first, she had trouble balancing when she landed because her knees stayed straight. However, she quickly adjusted by bending them slightly, which helped her land more smoothly and regain her balance faster.


During the jumping for height challenge, Charis used the same technique and took her time, as advised by her teachers. Her careful and thoughtful approach showed her growing confidence and ability to refine her technique. This experience highlights her progress in body coordination, balance, and learning from feedback.

title: My ‘Not a Box’ Project
description:
After reading the story Not a Box, the children were invited to create their own "not a box" structures using different pieces of cardboard. Prior to the activity, the children were challenged to transform 2D cardboard pieces into 3D structures. We watched a video and learned 10 different ways to connect cardboard pieces. While creating their structures, the children used various techniques depending on their design goals.

Using his design as a reference, Daxton began gathering a few cardboard pieces and experimented with different ways to connect them. He was observed cutting halfway through the width of his rectangular pieces and then slotting them together in the middle. Proudly, Daxton remarked, “Teacher Sammie, I used the slot method,” referring to one of the techniques from the video. He added, “These can be the rooms inside the house.”

Daxton continued assembling his structure, adding more rectangular pieces around the perimeter of the slotted pieces to form the shape of a house. He carefully cut out a small opening and used a hole puncher to create a hole at the top. Using a pipe cleaner, he attached a door that opened upwards, giving his house a functional entrance.

Daxton had also added two rectangular pieces to serve as the roof of his house. Once he was done, with some time to spare, he decided to create a person. Inspired by the strategies we learned to connect pieces and make them move, Daxton used a round head fastener to attach the arms and legs to his figure. After completing his work, Daxton proudly demonstrated how the arms and legs could move, saying, "Look! This is the person who lives in the house. He can move his arms and legs!"
interpretation:
Through this experience, Daxton demonstrated strong problem-solving abilities. Having watched the video earlier, he was equipped with the tools and strategies needed to confidently approach the challenge. Daxton applied the "slot" method independently, carefully manipulating the materials to transform 2D cardboard pieces into a 3D structure. His ability to recall and use this technique reflects his growing understanding of constructing with cardboard.


His creative use of a round head fastener to build a moveable figure reflects his understanding of basic building techniques and movable parts. Daxton adapted his design and refined his ideas as he built, thinking critically about how to achieve his goals. This hands-on experience allowed Daxton to experiment, make changes, and observe the results. His excitement in sharing his work highlights his ability to connect ideas to real life, strengthening his creativity and problem-solving skills.

She also showed a positive attitude toward working with her friends, helping them check their pictures to make sure they matched the sentences. This shows that Elizabeth is building her problem-solving skills, improving her reading comprehension, and enjoying learning with others.

title: Artwork sample: Butterfly Craft with Cake Filters
description:
Artwork sample: Butterfly Craft with Cake Filters
Children created their own beautiful butterflies using cake filters! The process starts with children scribbling various shapes and patterns onto the cake filter with colourful markers. Once the design is complete, they drop some water onto the filter paper, watching in awe as the ink spreads and creates a stunning, blended effect across the paper. 

The filter paper was then folded in a pleated manner to form the wings of a butterfly.

This craft introduces children to the concept of how colours can blend and spread when water is added. It is also a way to develop their fine motor skills and understanding of cause and effect to foster an interest in art.

"Can you point to the biggest colour on your butterfly?" asked the teacher.

title: Partner Toss Challenge
description:
As part of our Kidzercise game, the children participated in a Partner Toss Challenge, where they practiced throwing and catching a ball with a partner. This activity focused on developing hand-eye coordination, control, and teamwork. The children started with short, gentle throws and gradually increased the distance as they gained more confidence. The challenge encouraged them to throw accurately and catch consistently while staying engaged with their partner.

Ethan was first tasked with catching the ball. He positioned himself by stretching his arms out and leaning his body forward, showing readiness and focus. On his first attempt, he narrowly missed the ball but quickly adjusted his approach. During the next throw, Ethan demonstrated increased concentration, keeping his eyes on the rubber ball as it moved through the air. As the ball came closer, he tracked it carefully and managed to tap it with his catching pad. While he was unable to catch it, he showed good control in directing the ball. On his last turn, Ethan attempted to adjust his movements, aiming to soften his touch so the ball wouldn’t bounce away. He came very close to a successful catch.

When it was his turn to throw, Ethan gently swung his arm to toss the ball towards his friend. As his throw was a bit controlled, it fell short of the target. Recognising the need for a stronger throw, Ethan adjusted his swing, adding more force. His improved throw reached his partner and was almost caught. His ability to self-correct and refine his movements highlights his growing confidence and control in throwing and catching.
interpretation:
Through this activity, Ethan demonstrated growing confidence and control in both throwing and catching. He showed an understanding of how focus, tracking the ball, and adjusting movements contribute to success. His ability to make small changes, such as softening his touch while catching and adding more force when throwing, highlights his emerging coordination and problem-solving skills.


Ethan’s efforts to refine his technique, along with his willingness to self-correct and experiment with different strategies, show that he is developing a strong foundation in hand-eye coordination. With continued opportunities to practice, Ethan will further strengthen his ability to throw and catch with greater accuracy and consistency. His engagement and perseverance reflect his positive attitude toward learning new physical skills.

title: Work Sample - Sorting Treasures
description:
During the Treasure Matching activity, the children demonstrated their ability to match objects based on their own chosen attributes. They began by drawing and carefully cutting out treasure items such as jewels, coins, and other artifacts. As they worked, they thoughtfully considered different characteristics, such as the colour, shape, if the treasure was shiny, round, patterned or textured. Then the children organised their treasures into their chosen attributes.

Kadie sorted her treasures by their colours. She carefully grouped her treasures into colours like purple, pink, green, yellow and beige. She showed focus and patience while cutting the intricate shapes and adjusted her grip of the scissors when needed. When sharing her sorting choices, she confidently explained why certain items belonged together based on their colours.

Through this hands-on activity, the children practiced visual recognition, categorisation, and fine motor skills as they carefully sorted and grouped their treasures. The children also demonstrated perseverance as they navigated tricky cuts and refined their sorting choices with determination.

title: Read and Sequence
description:
During the Lit Attack activity, the children engaged in reading a passage with decodable words and worked collaboratively to interpret its meaning. Leanne began reading the passage, "/J/ /e/ /n/ Jen... has a /p/ pet... hen." She focused as her friends continued to read a sentence each. On her next turn, Leanne read, "The vet... /f/ ed... fed... the hen ten tr... /e/ ts." When the teacher corrected her, she repeated, "treats."

After the group finished reading the passage, they looked at the pictures to match them to the sentences. Leanne spotted a picture of a girl with a hen and immediately picked it up, saying, "This is the first one. This is Jen, and this is the hen." She continued working collaboratively, checking each picture that her friends picked up to ensure it matched.

When they were left with one picture, the group realised they might have placed an earlier picture incorrectly. Leanne reread the last two sentences of the passage and said, "I think we need to switch this one. This picture (number 10) should be here because the hen ate 10 treats.
interpretation:
Leanne demonstrated developing skills in decoding and comprehension during this activity. She confidently applied her phonics knowledge to sound out words, self-correcting with support when encountering unfamiliar words like “treats.” Her persistence and willingness to repeat the correct pronunciation reflect her growing accuracy and confidence in reading.


Leanne’s observation and logical reasoning during the sequencing task highlight her ability to connect the text with visual representations. When the group encountered a sequencing error, Leanne independently reread the passage and accurately identified the mismatch, showing her understanding of the text. This reflects her ability to self-correct and comprehend the text. Leanne is also demonstrating increasing independence when reading decodable passages, taking initiative to solve problems and verify her understanding.

learning_goals.title: Phonological Awareness: Decode unfamiliar words.
Comprehension: Use strategies to construct meaning from print.
Comprehension: Anticipate events in stories and make predictions.

title: Partner Toss Challenge
description:
As part of our Kidzercise game, the children participated in a Partner Toss Challenge, where they practiced throwing and catching a ball with a partner. This activity focused on developing hand-eye coordination, control, and teamwork. The children started with short, gentle throws and gradually increased the distance as they gained more confidence. The challenge encouraged them to throw accurately and catch consistently while staying engaged with their partner.

Leroy was first tasked with throwing the rubber ball to his partner. During his initial two throws, he experimented with different levels of force. His first two throws were too strong, sending the ball past his partner. After receiving guidance from the teacher to aim for the catching pad and use a gentler motion, Leroy adjusted his approach. 

His third throw showed improvement, landing closer to the target, and his final two throws were successful as his partner was able to catch his throw. 

When it was his turn to catch, Leroy initially missed, as he was not fully tracking the ball. After being reminded to keep his eyes on the ball, he adjusted his focus and successfully caught it once.
interpretation:
Through this activity, Leroy was able to build confidence in throwing and catching while developing better control and coordination. He explored different ways to throw the ball, adjusting his strength and aim to help his partner catch it.


At first, his throws were too strong, but with guidance, he learned to use gentler throws and aim more carefully.

When it was his turn to catch, Leroy discovered that keeping his eyes on the ball made a big difference. With practice, he was able to successfully catch the ball, showing his growing focus and perseverance.


This activity helped Leroy and his peers understand that small adjustments and practice can help them improve and succeed. It also encouraged them to work together, build confidence, and develop important movement skills that will support their physical growth.

learning_goals.title: Be aware of what the body can do and develop their locomotor skills.
Coordinate movements to perform tasks.

description:

title: Artwork sample: Butterfly Craft with Cake Filters
description:
Children created their own beautiful butterflies using cake filters! The process starts with children scribbling various shapes and patterns onto the cake filter with colourful markers. Once the design is complete, they drop some water onto the filter paper, watching in awe as the ink spreads and creates a stunning, blended effect across the paper. 

The filter paper was then folded in a pleated manner to form the wings of a butterfly.

This craft introduces children to the concept of how colours can blend and spread when water is added. It is also a way to develop their fine motor skills and understanding of cause and effect to foster an interest in art.

"What colours would you like to add on your butterfly?" asked the teacher.
"Green and purple!" Stephy replied confidently.
