title: 绘画我自己
description:
幼儿正在参与“语言斗”领域的“绘画我自己”的教学活动。教师引导幼儿观察自己的外貌特征，我们的脸上有眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴、耳朵等，引导绘画头发，绘画身体部位等。幼儿用绘画表达自己。
艾雯坐在桌前，眼睛盯着洁白的画纸，手里紧握着蜡笔，认真地思考着。她轻轻地在纸上画了一个圆圈，然后开心地说：“这是我的头！”老师微笑着问：“那你的眼睛呢？”她拿起黑色的蜡笔，专注地在圆圈里画了两颗圆圆的眼睛，一边画一边说道：“我的眼睛是圆圆的。”接着，她又用粉色蜡笔画了一个小小的弧线，说：“这是我的嘴巴，我的嘴巴说话，还会吃饭！”她开心地张开嘴，做了个咀嚼的动作。
艾雯画完五官，开始画身体，她用蜡笔拉出一条长长的线，说：“这是我的手，我的手可以抱抱妈妈！”她又画了两条小短线，指着它们说：“这就是我的腿，我的腿可以走路。”老师鼓励她：“艾雯，你画得很棒！你觉得还可以加些什么呢？”艾雯歪着脑袋想了想，然后兴奋地说：“头发！”艾雯满意地看着自己的作品，高兴地对老师说：“这是我自己！”她举起画纸，向旁边的小朋友展示，骄傲地介绍着：“看，这是我！”
interpretation: 在这次绘画活动中，艾雯通过绘画和语言表达，能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。尝试用华语表达自己的想法。她不仅认识了自己的身体特征，还增强了自我认同感，同时展现了她的创造力和想象力。

title: 颜色小怪兽
description:
老师邀请幼儿们参与我的情绪小怪兽活动。老师准备好彩色颜料、海绵拍、保鲜膜、假眼睛、彩纸、棉签若干。请幼儿们一起制作情绪小怪兽。老师介绍材料，并示范给他们看。
老师请翰毅自由选择自己喜欢的颜料，他选择红色、橙色、黄色、紫色和绿色颜料。老师询问他：“这是什么颜色？”他说：“yellow”老师鼓励他说：“黄色。”他跟随老师说出：“黄色”老师表扬他：“说得好！”并询问其他的颜色名称，引导他逐一说出颜色中文名称来。翰毅选择自己喜欢的颜料，双手用力挤压颜料瓶，在卡纸挤满颜料后，他说：“finish”老师鼓励他说：“完成了。”他看着老师微笑的说出：“完成了。”老师表扬他：“真棒！”老师帮助翰毅盖上保鲜膜。翰毅五指抓握住海绵拍，向下按压在有颜色的颜料上。待完成后，老师鼓励他揭开了保鲜膜。翰毅说：“老师help”老师引导他说：“老师帮我。”在我们一起的合作下成功的揭开保鲜膜，待他看到保鲜膜上的颜色时，他发出：“哇！”的感叹声。
在作品晾干后，老师准备了假眼睛、彩色纽扣、乳白胶、棉签和装饰物若干。请他使用棉棒粘胶水装饰彩色小怪兽。翰毅一只手中指和食指缝隙夹住棉棒粘胶水，另外一只手三指捏起假眼睛和纽扣装饰起情绪小怪兽。在他粘贴纽扣的过程中，他对棉签粘胶水滑动在卡纸上，来回打圈滑动，在逐一粘贴假眼睛、纽扣进行装饰。
interpretation: 翰毅可以积极参与情绪小怪兽活动，在活动中他能听懂老师的讲解，尝试使用语言表达自己的想法。可以选择自己喜欢的颜料挤压在卡纸上，尝试使用棉棒，独立粘贴假眼睛、纽扣等装饰物。增强自己对绘画的创意，同时促进手眼协调能力和手部精细动作的发展

老师请彩绚自由选择自己喜欢的颜料，她选择红色、橙色和黄色颜料。老师询问她：“这是什么颜色？”她说：“red”。老师鼓励她说：“红色”她看向老师微笑，老师说：“红、色”彩绚可以说出：‘红”老师表扬她真棒！并和她击掌庆祝。她微笑着回应，并拿起了红色颜料瓶，双手用力挤压在卡纸上。当颜料挤满后，彩绚放下颜料瓶。老师询问她：“你完成了吗？”她点点头。在老师的帮助下，成功的盖上保鲜膜。彩绚双手向下按压在有颜色的颜料上，并尝试使用食指在保鲜膜上打圈创作。老师表扬她:“做的很漂亮！”
在作品晾干后，老师准备了假眼睛、彩色纽扣、乳白胶、棉签和装饰物若干。请她使用棉棒粘胶水装饰彩色小怪兽。彩绚一只手使用棉棒粘胶水，另外一只手两指抓起假眼睛和纽扣装饰起情绪小怪兽。在她粘贴很多纽扣的时候，老师询问她：“这是小怪兽的什么啊？”她指向自己的眼睛，老师鼓励她：“真有创意，小怪兽有好多彩色的眼睛。”她微笑的拍手庆祝。
interpretation: 彩绚可以参与情绪小怪兽活动，在活动中她能听懂老师的讲解，尝试使用语言和动作表达自己的想法。可以选择自己喜欢的颜料挤压在卡纸上，尝试使用棉棒，独立粘贴假眼睛、纽扣等装饰物。增强自己对绘画的创意，同时促进手眼协调能力和手部精细动作的发展。

title: 我们一起庆祝生日吧
description:

        自由探索时间，轩伊走到建构空间，她拿了几块积木放在地板上，然后将积木堆叠，对齐。教师问轩伊：“轩伊，你用积木搭建的是什么呀？”轩伊回答教师说：“蛋糕。”教师又问道：“是你过生日吗？”轩伊点了点头。然后她边拍手拍唱起了歌：“祝你生日快乐，祝你生日快乐，祝你生日快乐......”她的朋友听到她的歌声，走了过来，和轩伊一起唱生日快乐歌，他们发出笑声。然后他们用玩具刀切“蛋糕”，他们切好“蛋糕”，轩伊拿起一块“蛋糕”给她的朋友，她的朋友做吃的动作，轩伊发出笑声。

title: Light Up Magnetic Tiles
description: During learning corner time, the children were exploring the various activities in different domain corners.
interpretation:
Shuo-yun was seen running around, occasionally stopping to observe his friends playing. Suddenly, he paused at the light board in the Curious Works corner, where his friend Ethan was engaged with magnetic tiles. 


As the teacher activated the light board, Shuo-yun’s face lit up. "Light! Colour!" he said excitedly, pointing at the vibrant display. He noticed that each magnetic tile emitted different colours, and the lines and centre dots on the tiles became more distinct under the light. Shuo-yun looked at Ethan and smiled, showing his friend what he had discovered. Their shared curiosity sparked a moment of connection as they explored the light and colours together. Through this experience, Shuo-yun not only engaged in cognitive exploration but also developed social-emotional skills by communicating with Ethan, fostering teamwork and mutual discovery.

title: May I have a doughnut, please?
description:
After listening to Please, Mr. Panda by Steve Antony, Rhea gained a deeper understanding of the importance of good manners when interacting with others. The story taught her how simple words like "please" and "thank you" can make conversations more respectful and kind.

To practice, Rhea and her friend took turns role-playing, politely asking for a doughnut. "Megan, may I have the pink doughnut, please?" Rhea asked. As they played, she successfully identified the colors of the doughnuts while making her requests. Each time her friend handed her a doughnut, Rhea remembered to say, "Thank you," reinforcing her understanding of polite communication. Rhea also engaged in dramatic play as she pretended to eat the doughnuts. "See, I eat up the pink and purple doughnuts."
interpretation: Rhea is in the process of learning how a simple request made with good manners can make others feel appreciated and more willing to share. The activity was not only fun but also helped reinforce the value of kindness and politeness in her everyday interactions with her friends. It also helped to foster her sense of others by saying out their names when interacting with them.

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of others (saying out the names of their peers) 培养对他人的认识，如：说出同伴的名字等。

title: 各式各样的面包
description: 教师讲述绘本《各种各样的面包》，邀请凯翔和朋友一起围坐在身边聆听故事。老师拿出书本给幼儿看封面，并问：“书本上是什么呀？”凯翔回答：“bread.I like eat Bread.”老师说：“面包，我喜欢吃面包。”凯翔重复老师的话：“面包，我喜欢吃面包。”老师说：“凯翔方形的面包在哪里？”凯翔指着方形面包：“Here，方形面包。”当老师讲到烤盘里有长面包、辫子面包、圆形面包等不同的面包时问：“凯翔你喜欢什么样的面包？”凯翔指着圆形面包说：“I like 圆形面包。”凯翔和朋友们一起有问有答，继续听老师讲书本，讨论着不同的面包。
interpretation: 在讲绘本《各式各样的面包》的活动中，凯翔听到老师问：书本上有什么时？凯翔用英文回答：bread.I like eat Bread.”当老师用华语说出他的意思时，凯翔能够重复说出；当老师问：方形面包在哪里时，凯翔回答：Here，方形面包。能表达出：I like 圆形面包。这表明他能逐渐从单词过渡到简单句子，凯翔的听与表达能力正在进一步发展中。由于处于双语环境，经常中英文合混使用。

title: May I have a doughnut, please?
description:
After listening to Please, Mr. Panda by Steve Antony, Megan gained a deeper understanding of the importance of good manners when interacting with others. The story taught her how simple words like "please" and "thank you" can make conversations more respectful and kind.

To practice, Megan and her friend took turns role-playing, politely asking for a doughnut. "I want yellow doughnut, please? Rhea." Megan asked. As they played, she successfully identified the colors of the doughnuts while making her requests. Each time her friend handed her a doughnut, Megan remembered to say, "Thank you." reinforcing her understanding of polite communication. She commented, “See, Teacher Michelle, I got so many doughnuts. Rhea give me.” Megan also engaged in dramatic play as she pretended to eat the doughnuts.
interpretation: Megan is in the process of learning how a simple request made with good manners can make others feel appreciated and more willing to share. The activity was not only fun but also helped reinforce the value of kindness and politeness in her everyday interactions with her friends. It also helped to foster her sense of others by saying out their names when interacting with them.

title: Sets of Things That Go Together
description: A tray was filled with a few sets of picture cards and children were invited to put the pairs of related objects side by side. Hwee Jeanne looked into the tray and picked up a picture of a spoon. “A spoon go with a bowl!” she said before picking up the picture of a bowl. She placed them side by side and continued to pair the other related objects such as shoes and socks, flower and pot, etc. While picking each picture card, Hwee Jeanne mentioned the name of each object too. She smiled at her teacher and said, “I am all done! So many pairs, right?” Her teacher nodded in agreement and praised Hwee Jeanne for completing the activity.
interpretation: This activity displayed Hwee Jeanne’s understanding towards what pairs of related objects that go together are. She showed confidence in picking up the pairs of picture cards with minimal guidance and was able to name each object.

learning_goals.title: Pair related objects (e.g: a cup to a saucer, a fork to a spoon)

title: Drawing Face Emotion
description: With the topic of “My Emotions”, children took turns to share about how they feel and were invited to draw their emotion on a paper. Hwee Jeanne chose a colour pencil and started drawing. She started by drawing a big circle and added the facial features. After completing, Hwee Jeanne shared with her teacher, “This is my happy face, the eyes, nose and my mouth is smiling! I like peach colour too.” “Well done, Hwee Jeanne! I can see all the facial features that you drew.” Her teacher acknowledged.
interpretation: Hwee Jeanne showed that while drawing her face emotion, she had her thought process as she was able to talk about her artwork. She used circles for the eyes and lines for the nose and smile. Hwee Jeanne smiled to show her satisfaction and felt proud of her drawing.

learning_goals.title: Talk about their own artworks (e.g: what the artwork is about and the lines, colours and shapes used).

title: 作品说明：创意逃家小兔
description:
在《逃家小兔》故事里，小兔和兔妈妈玩了一场你逃我追的游戏，无论小兔变成什么，逃到哪里，兔妈妈都会有办法抓到他。小朋友们在这个故事中，不仅看到了兔妈妈对小兔的爱，还看到了兔妈妈的勇敢和智慧。大家讨论，如果自己是那只小兔，会和妈妈玩怎样的“逃走”和“追赶”的游戏。小朋友们发挥想象，在图画纸上先画出图稿，创编了一个自己的“逃家小兔”故事，再用剪贴画的方式呈现，讲述给大家听。
        玮乐先在稿纸的下方画了一条长长的弯弯曲曲的线表示草地，在图画纸的中间画了一棵粗壮的树，在树上画了一些枝叶，再在树的两边各画了一个水果。他解释到：“这是一棵橙子树”、“我对妈妈说，我要逃走了，我要变成一个橙子。”、“妈妈说她会变成一个橙子树。”然后，他正确地仿写句子“我变成橙子，妈妈变成橙子树。”写好后，他还在画稿的右上角补充性地画了一个太阳。
        确定了画稿和内容，玮乐开始制作剪贴画。他剪了一条粗长的瓦楞纸做树干黏贴在图画纸的左边，剪了几条细短瓦楞纸做树枝黏贴在树干上。他将皱纹纸剪成一些小碎片，黏贴在树枝上做树叶，又在白色图画纸上画了一个橙子，涂上橙色，再细心地将果枝涂上棕色，小心翼翼地剪下黏贴在橙子树上。接着，他剪了一小片圆形的橙色纸做橙子贴在树枝上。最后，他在橙子树的边上黏贴了一根冰激凌棒，画了两串葡萄分别黏贴在两边。
         在故事分享时，小朋友们问为什么橙子树上有两个橙子？妈妈变的是橙子树，为什么画面上还有一棵葡萄树？他解释说，画的那个橙子是他变的，另外一个橙子是树上的橙子。他多做了一棵葡萄树，是因为他不想只有一棵树，他要做两棵树。
interpretation:
玮乐能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出他想要讲述的故事。

主要学习领域成果：

·  能清楚连贯地表达事情经过。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用华语表达出自己心中兔妈妈和小兔子的样子。

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

description:

       奕凯说：“我要画我变成一只老虎，妈妈变成一个饲养员。”很快，奕凯就用铅笔在图画纸上画了一只老虎的轮廓，然后，他很细心地一条一条画出老虎身上的花纹。接着，他在老虎的身边画了一个男生饲养员。他解释说：“这只老虎是我变的，这个饲养员是妈妈变的。”身边的朋友问他，为什么妈妈变成男的饲养员，他说：“因为我不会画女的头发。”最后，他在图画纸的上方，很有耐心地点了几朵云，又在老虎和饲养员的身后画了几条弧线，表示他们所站的位置是一片草地。所有的内容画好后，他用黑色马克笔将重要的线条描了一遍，凸显出了画面的艺术感。
        确定了画稿后，奕凯开始制作剪贴画。他先在橙色纸上画了一只老虎，剪下来黏贴在图画纸的下方。又在图画纸上画了一个穿长裙的妈妈饲养员，但是妈妈的发型依然像男孩一样。朋友示范画女孩子发型的方法，奕凯就模仿她，在妈妈的头上画了一条长长的向下的线。画好后，他剪下妈妈饲养员黏贴在老虎的身边。朋友说他的老虎做的太小了，奕凯说：“我再做一个大的老虎。”他用同样的方法画了一只大一些的老虎，剪下黏贴在小老虎的边上，并解释说：“这只小的老虎是弟弟奕峰，大的老虎是我。”接着，他剪了一些绿色皱纹纸碎片贴在图画纸的下方做草地，剪了一些蓝色的云黏贴在图画纸的上方。最后，剪了一片扇形黄色纸片恰到好处地贴在右上角做太阳。
interpretation:
奕凯能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出他想要讲述的故事。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

description:

       晋恺说他要变长一张桌子，妈妈就会变成一把椅子，因为椅子总是会和桌子在一起的。想好了内容，晋恺开始在图画纸上画画稿。他画了几笔后，说不要画了，他不会。老师就用简笔画的方法画了一张长长的桌子和一把椅子。看了示范后，晋恺说知道怎么画了。他先用铅笔画了一张长长的桌面，在桌面下画了两根桌腿。他解释说：“从一边看桌子，只能看到两个桌子的腿。”然后，他又用透视法画了一张椅子。因为还不熟练使用透视法，画出几条多余的线，在建议下，他擦掉了那几条线。然后，他仿写句子：我说：“我要变成一个桌子。”；妈妈说：“我就变成一把椅子。”虽然漏写了几个字，但写出的字都正确。最后，他用黑色马克笔将简笔画描了一遍，使线条看上去更有立体感。
       确定了画稿后，晋恺开始制作剪贴画。他剪了一条长长的薄纸板横着黏贴在图画纸上做桌面，又剪了四条细短的薄纸板做桌腿。接着，他剪了几条薄纸板黏贴成一张椅子放在桌子的一端。思棋说他的剪贴画看上去很“plain”，他想了想，就剪了一本小书黏贴在桌子上，又在桌子的上方剪贴了几盏彩色的灯。这样，整个故事画面就显得明亮和丰富了很多。
       在故事分享时，有小朋友问，为什么他做的故事画面和稿纸上画的不一样，他回答说：“因为我觉得这样好看。”
interpretation:
晋恺能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出他想要讲述的故事。

title: 作品说明：创意逃家小兔
description:
在《逃家小兔》故事里，小兔和兔妈妈玩了一场你逃我追的游戏，无论小兔变成什么，逃到哪里，兔妈妈都会有办法抓到他。小朋友们在这个故事中，不仅看到了兔妈妈对小兔的爱，还看到了兔妈妈的勇敢和智慧。大家讨论，如果自己是那只小兔，会和妈妈玩怎样的“逃走”和“追赶”的游戏。小朋友们发挥想象，在图画纸上先画出图稿，创编了一个自己的“逃家小兔”故事，再用剪贴画的方式呈现，讲述给大家听。
        傲天先在稿纸的下方画了一只大兔子和一只小兔子。他解释说：“大兔子是妈妈，小兔子是我。”、“我和妈妈在讲故事。”、“我说，我要变成一棵树。”、“妈妈说，她就变成一个园丁。”仿写好句子。
       确定了画稿的内容后，傲天开始制作剪贴画。他找了一小片瓦楞纸，从上面剪下了一条粗的长方形，黏贴在图画纸上做树干，又从上面剪下了三条细的长方形，黏贴在“树干”的上方做树枝。在各种彩色纸中，他选了淡绿色的皱纹纸剪成碎片，黏贴在“树干”做树叶。他尝试用白色图画纸剪一只兔子，但剪了几次都觉得不是他想要的样子，就用马克笔画了一只兔子，并彩上粉红色。他说：“这是妈妈变的兔子，我的妈妈喜欢粉红色的衣服。”接着，他剪了几小片黄色的纸和一小长条红色的纸，拼贴了一个水壶，又在树的边上贴了一小条细长的白纸，他解释说，这是妈妈兔子在给树浇水，没有谁这棵树就会死掉的。最后，他剪了一些黄色方形的纸黏贴在图画纸的上方表示云，一张故事画面就完成了。
interpretation:
傲天能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容能呈现出他想要讲述的故事。

主要学习领域成果：

·  能清楚连贯地表达事情经过。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用华语表达出自己心中兔妈妈和小兔子的样子。

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

title: 作品说明：创意逃家小兔
description:
在《逃家小兔》故事里，小兔和兔妈妈玩了一场你逃我追的游戏，无论小兔变成什么，逃到哪里，兔妈妈都会有办法抓到他。小朋友们在这个故事中，不仅看到了兔妈妈对小兔的爱，还看到了兔妈妈的勇敢和智慧。大家讨论，如果自己是那只小兔，会和妈妈玩怎样的“逃走”和“追赶”的游戏。小朋友们发挥想象，在图画纸上先画出图稿，创编了一个自己的“逃家小兔”故事，再用剪贴画的方式呈现，讲述给大家听。
        瑞晴说：“我会讲故事，小兔变成花，妈妈变成园丁。”她用马克笔在图画纸的左边熟练地画了几朵花，其中有一朵花长着一张兔子脸。在图画纸的右边，她画了一个兔妈妈变的园丁。妈妈的一只手里拿着篮子，另一只手里拿着水壶在给花浇水。然后，她照着字卡仿写句子“小兔说：我要变成花。”、“妈妈说：我就变成园丁。”
        设计好画面后，瑞晴开始制作剪贴画。她要求老师示范给她看剪花的方法，看完示范后，她按照老师的方法，先剪了三条小小细长的纸板分开贴在图画纸的下方作为花茎。然后，剪了两个红色圆纸片分别黏贴在左边的两根“花茎”的上端做花心。她本想剪一些小碎纸片做花瓣黏贴在“花心”周边，但是，她尝试了好几次都没能剪成她想要的形状。于是，就放弃了，用笔在“花心”周围画花瓣。画好花瓣，她又在“花心”上画了一些网格，看上去像向日葵花。看出来她是没有耐心一片一片地剪花瓣，老师就示范了另一种简单的方法。瑞晴看了，自信地说：“我知道，我知道了。”她用新的方法剪了一朵不一样的花。然后，她在这棵花的边上画了一个妈妈。老师提醒她要用剪贴的方法做妈妈，她看了看画，就剪了几张小碎片贴在“妈妈”的脸上做鼻子和眼睛。接下来，她在蓝色的纸上画了几朵云剪下黏贴在图画纸的上方，在黄色的纸上画了一个太阳剪下贴在右上角，一幅创意逃家小兔剪贴画就做好了。
       在分享故事的时候，瑞晴能说出画面的大概内容。
interpretation:
瑞晴能在理解故事内容的基础，用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得比较用心，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出想要讲述的故事。但是，在活动的过程中，她表现出有些缺乏耐心。需要多一些的时间来学习使用剪刀和仿写汉字。

主要学习领域成果：

·  能清楚连贯地表达事情经过。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用华语表达出自己心中兔妈妈和小兔子的样子。

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

title: 作品说明：创意逃家小兔
description:
在《逃家小兔》故事里，小兔和兔妈妈玩了一场你逃我追的游戏，无论小兔变成什么，逃到哪里，兔妈妈都会有办法抓到他。小朋友们在这个故事中，不仅看到了兔妈妈对小兔的爱，还看到了兔妈妈的勇敢和智慧。大家讨论，如果自己是那只小兔，会和妈妈玩怎样的“逃走”和“追赶”的游戏。小朋友们发挥想象，在图画纸上先画出图稿，创编了一个自己的“逃家小兔”故事，再用剪贴画的方式呈现，讲述给大家听。
        天煜说我不要讲新的故事，我要讲小兔变成鸟飞得远远的。他就三笔两笔快速地画了一只在飞的小兔子，然后在小兔的上方画了一只和小兔朝同一方向飞的大兔子，在大兔子的边上又画了一棵小小的树。他解释说：“小兔变成小鸟在飞，妈妈变成大鸟和他一起飞。”接着，他围绕小树画了一个圈，说：“妈妈变成了一棵树，让小兔回家。”画完后，他看着句子卡片，仿写“小兔变成小鸟飞得远远的......。”因为，他急着要做剪贴画，写了几笔就放弃了。
        设计好画面后，天煜开始制作剪贴画。他拿了一条别人剪好的粗长的瓦楞纸贴在图画纸上做树干，然后自己剪了几条细短的瓦楞纸贴在上面做树枝。他在各种彩色纸里挑了一片浅绿色的皱纹纸，剪碎黏贴在图画纸的下方做草地。接着，他尝试将绿色的小纸片剪成树叶的形状，但剪得都不满意，就吵着要老师帮。老师将树叶剪好，他一片片地涂上胶水，耐心地贴在了树枝上。最后，他在紫色的纸上画了一只小鸟，小心翼翼地剪下，头朝着树的方向黏贴好。他解释说：“这是小兔变的小鸟，他要飞到树上。”、“妈妈变成了树。”这时，他看朋友在用化妆棉做云，也拿了几片剪碎黏贴在图画纸的上方，并学着别人的样子，剪了一个圆圆的太阳贴在树的上方。
       在大家分享故事的时候，天煜一边听别人讲故事，一边在自己的剪贴画上画了一些建筑物。轮到他分享故事了自信地到白板前，指着做好的故事画面，清楚地说：“这是树，妈妈变的树，这是小兔变得鸟。这些是房子......”
interpretation:
天煜能在理解故事内容的基础上复述故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得比较用心，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出他想要讲述的故事。但是，在活动的过程中，不够有耐心。需要多一些的时间来学习使用剪刀和仿写汉字。

主要学习领域成果：

·  能清楚连贯地表达事情经过。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用华语表达出自己心中兔妈妈和小兔子的样子。

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

description:

        嶪峻先在稿纸的下方画了一条锯齿线表示草地，再在“草地上”上画了一棵有兔子头的树，然后，在边上画了一个小小的兔子的头。他指着小小的兔子头解释说：“小兔说要变成一个苹果，因为苹果是小兔变的，所以是兔子的形状苹果。”他接着解释说：“这个树是兔妈妈变的，兔妈妈说她要变成一个苹果树。”他看了看画面，又在妈妈树边画了一棵兔头苹果树。嶪峻解释说：“我不要妈妈一个树在这里，我要这个树和她一起。”接着，他在图画纸的上方又画了几朵不同形状的云，在右上角画了一个闪闪发光的太阳。
        设计好画面后，嶪峻开始制作剪贴画。他剪了一条粗长的瓦楞纸贴纸图画纸上做树干，剪了几条细短的瓦楞纸贴上做树枝。然后，他在各种彩色纸里挑了一片浅绿色的皱纹纸，小心地剪成碎片黏贴在树枝上和图画纸的下方做树叶和草地。接着，他剪了一个红色的苹果黏贴在树枝上。他看了看苹果，觉得好像少了点什么，就剪了一个小小的长条做果枝黏贴在苹果上。最后，他用化妆棉剪白云，看上去更有立体感。
       在讲故事的时候，小朋友们问：“为什么你的画稿有两棵树，故事画只有一棵树？”他解释说：“因为没有位了。”“为什么太阳和画稿上面不一样？”他指着剪贴画说：“这里也没有位，我就放在这边了。”
interpretation:
嶪峻能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细，所用的色彩能体现出故事环境的特点，画面内容详细地呈现出他想要讲述的故事。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

·  幼儿能用华语表达出自己心中兔妈妈和小兔子的样子。

·  幼儿能用制作故事画面的方式记录他们的想法和创意。

        许恩在稿纸上画了一个兔子形状的妈妈，兔妈妈双手朝一边拿着鼓槌在打鼓。她指着画面解释说：“这是我变的小鼓，妈妈就变成打鼓的人。”为了让画面看上更好看，她还在图稿上画了一些烟花、星星、月亮等。
        设计好画面后，许恩开始制作剪贴画。她在一张黄色的纸上画了一只有自己图像的鼓，剪下来贴在图画纸上，再用同样的方法做了一个“双手拿着鼓槌的打鼓人妈妈”。为了让画面看上去立体一点，她剪了三张细长的纸做“支架”贴在鼓的下面，又剪了一些细长的“烟花”贴在图画纸的上方。接着，她在图画纸的空白处涂上深蓝色表示夜晚。最后，她要求剪一点化妆棉做月亮，因为她看到的月亮是白色的，用化妆棉比用白纸做月亮更好看。
       在讲故事的时候，小朋友们问：“为什么你做的打鼓的妈妈和图稿上面的不一样？”她解释说：“因为我觉得妈妈这样很漂亮。”

title: 作品说明：创意逃家小兔
description:
在《逃家小兔》故事里，小兔和兔妈妈玩了一场你逃我追的游戏，无论小兔变成什么，逃到哪里，兔妈妈都会有办法抓到他。小朋友们在这个故事中，不仅看到了兔妈妈对小兔的爱，还看到了兔妈妈的勇敢和智慧。大家讨论，如果自己是那只小兔，会和妈妈玩怎样的“逃走”和“追赶”的游戏。小朋友们发挥想象，在图画纸上先画出图稿，创编了一个自己的“逃家小兔”故事，再用剪贴画的方式呈现，讲述给大家听。
        思棋在稿纸上画了一个长颈鹿和戴帽子的人，她解释说：“这个长颈鹿是我变的，这个是妈妈变的。”“我对妈妈说，我要变成长颈鹿，住在动物园里。妈妈说，如果我变成长颈鹿（住）在动物园里，她就变成一个照顾长颈鹿的人。”老师告诉她，在动物园里照顾动物的人叫“饲养员”，思棋就立刻补充说：“妈妈就变成饲养员，照顾我变的长颈鹿。”然后，思棋在稿纸上仿写出故事内容“我变成长颈鹿，妈妈变成饲养员。”
       图稿和内容确定了后，思棋开始用剪贴画的方式制作故事画面。她找到一张大小适中的黄色的纸，在纸上先画出长颈鹿的轮廓，再沿着轮廓线熟练地剪出了长颈鹿的形状，涂上胶水黏贴在图画纸的左边。接着，她用同样的方法剪了妈妈变的饲养员、蓝色的云、黄色的太阳、紫色的房子黏贴上去。最后，她又剪了一些绿色细长皱纹纸贴在画的下方表示是草地。

interpretation:
思棋能在理解故事内容的基础上创编故事情节，并能用简笔画的方式勾勒出要画的主要内容。剪贴画制作得精细、色彩明亮，画面内容详细地呈现出她想要讲述的故事。但是，她对作品要求完美，总是认为做的还不够好，在明确地知道自己可以在学习角时间继续修饰画面时，才肯暂时停止制作。

·  能清楚连贯地表达事情经过。

·  运用想象力创作故事画面。

综合学习领域成果：

title: Talking Tub: Learning About My Family
description: In this experience, the teacher invited the children to gather around a “Talking Tub,” a container filled with various objects related to the theme, 'family'. The children explored the items inside the tub, feeling and examining each one. As they did so, they discussed their observations with their peers and the teacher, using descriptive language to express their ideas. When it was Jun Yu’s turn, he took a moment to look through the tub before selecting a cookie model. He then shared, "Last time, I made honey cornflakes with my jie jie and mama." When asked if making honey cornflakes was something his family enjoys doing together, Jun Yu nodded enthusiastically and said "Yes!". Later, when another friend picked out labels that said mother, father, brother, and sister, his friend shared that he has a sister. Jun Yu eagerly joined the conversation and added, "Teacher Lilian, do you know, I also have a sister? Her name is Jing Xuan."
interpretation: Through these interactions, Jun Yu demonstrated the ability to use language for a variety of purposes - to describe, share experiences, connect with others, and elaborate on his thoughts. He demonstrated descriptive language when sharing a memory about making honey cornflakes with his jie jie and mama, giving a clear account of a family activity. Jun Yu also used language to communicate with others by contributing to a conversation about siblings, eagerly adding that he has a sister named Jing Xuan. Additionally, Jun Yu used language to clarify and elaborate on his ideas by offering more personal details.

learning_goals.title: Use expanded vocabulary and language for a variety of purposes.

title: Shape Race Slide
description: The teacher created large cutouts of various shapes (circle, square, triangle, rectangle and circle) and placed them at one end of the play area. The children picked a shape and then slid around the play space by alternating their legs. As they moved around the playground, they matched the shape they chose to real-world objects. Nikolai chose the shape circle and eagerly began sliding around the playground. He shuffled his feet back and forth swiftly, moving around the area with excitement and giggles. After a few moments, he stopped in front of the sensory bins and shouted, "Teacher Lilian, circle!" When the teacher arrived by his side, Nikolai explained, "Teacher Lilian, see, this is a circle." while lifting up the beach toy. Shuffling his feet back and forth once more, he quickly moved away from the sensory bins and discovered another circle on the playground structure. "Teacher Lilian, here!" he beamed, proudly pointing to the shape on the playground structure. When the teacher further probed him, Nikolai shared "This hole is like a circle."
interpretation: This experience revealed that Nikolai enjoyed learning and using math in his daily life by actively engaging with shapes in his environment. His excitement while moving around the playground and discovering circles in real-world objects, like the beach toy and the hole in the structure, demonstrated his ability to connect abstract concepts to tangible examples. This connection between the concept of shape and everyday objects helps solidify his understanding of mathematical concepts in a meaningful and fun way. As he identified these shapes and explained them to his teacher, he not only reinforced his understanding but also developed his math-related vocabulary.

learning_goals.title: Enjoy learning and using Math in daily experiences.

title: 老师“请帮忙”
description:
描述：
        在幼儿自由探索时间，轩伊走到生活技能空间，她拿起“穿吸管”的教具（一个盒子里面装有吸管和纸筒），她用右手拿起吸管左手拿起带有洞洞的纸筒，用吸管穿纸筒上的洞洞，过了一会，她拿着纸筒和吸管走到教师身旁，教师问轩伊：“轩伊，你是要老师帮忙吗？”轩伊看着教师点了点头说：“是的”，教师向轩伊示范如何将吸管穿进纸筒的洞洞里面，然后轩伊拿起吸管和纸筒重新尝试，她拿着吸管的上面去穿纸筒上的洞洞，教师告诉轩伊手要放在吸管的下面，这样才可以穿进去呢！轩伊继续尝试，终于将吸管穿进洞洞里面，她拿着穿进去的吸管给教师看，教师对轩伊竖起了大拇指，轩伊继续进行“穿吸管”的活动。
interpretation:
诠释：

      在进行“穿吸管”的活动中，轩伊能够在遇到问题时主动向教师寻求帮助，在教师引导轩伊将吸管穿进洞里面，她也主动将穿好的吸管向教师展示，展现出幼儿对教师的信任感。轩伊也能够在活动中用简单的词汇与教师进行沟通。

learning_goals.title: Foster a sense of trust in adults 通过回应与互动，培养幼儿对成人的信任感。

title: May I have a doughnut, please?
description:
After listening to Please, Mr. Panda by Steve Antony, Louka gained an emergent understanding of the importance of good manners when interacting with others. The story taught him how simple words like "please" and "thank you" can make conversations more respectful and kind.

To practice, Louka and his friend took turns role-playing, politely asking for a doughnut. "Gracie, the orange doughnut, please" As they played, he successfully identified the colors of the doughnuts while making his requests. Each time his friend handed him a doughnut, Louka remembered to say, "Thank you.", reinforcing his understanding of polite communication.
interpretation: Louka is in the process of learning how a simple request made with good manners can make others feel appreciated and more willing to share. The activity was not only fun but also helped reinforce the value of kindness and politeness in his everyday interactions with his friends. It also helped to foster his sense of others by saying out their names when interacting with them.

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of others (saying out the names of their peers) 培养对他人的认识，如：说出同伴的名字等。

title: 绘画“我自己”
description:
幼儿正在参与“语言斗”领域的“绘画我自己”的教学活动。教师引导幼儿观察自己的外貌特征，我们的脸上有眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴、耳朵等，引导绘画头发，绘画身体部位等。幼儿用绘画表达自己。
家悦拿着画纸，认真地思考了一下，便开始用黑色蜡笔在纸上画出一个大大的圆形。他仔细地在圆形里添上两个圆圆的眼睛，并在中间画了一个鼻子，还给自己画上了嘴巴。他边画边观察自己的手指，随后在画的旁边加上了手臂。他时而皱起眉头思考，时而开心地笑着继续画，最后满意地举起自己的作品，开心地展示给老师和小朋友们看。教师问他： 家悦，你画的是什么呀？家悦回答说： 这是我！我的脸，眼睛、鼻子和嘴巴！”老师说：“ 你画得真棒！你的眼睛好大，是在看什么呢？” “ 看我的朋友！” 他指着嘴巴说：”这是大大的嘴巴，我在笑！“
interpretation: 在这次绘画活动中，家悦通过绘画和语言表达，能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。尝试用华语表达自己的想法。家悦认识了自己的外貌特征，还通过语言表达增强了他的自信心和表达能力！

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（听）- 听指令：能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。
语言学习成果（说）- 交谈：尝试用华语与人交谈。
语言学习成果（写）- 写前准备：喜欢涂涂画画，能画出较直、横的线，基本能控制笔的方向。

title: 今天谁来学校了？
description: 上午圆圈时间，教师带领班级幼儿围坐在出席版前进行点名活动“今天谁来学校了？”。教师看着颖杰说到：“颖杰，颖杰在哪里？”颖杰笑嘻嘻的站了起来。教师引导他说：“颖杰找一找你的小照片在哪里呀？”颖杰笑着跑到出席版前，很快在下面一排小照片中找到了自己的照片。他把小照片取下来，展示给教师和同伴看。教师轻轻拍着出席版说：“今天谁来学校了？把小照片粘贴到出席板上吧！”颖杰点点头说：“嗯！”教师唱着：“颖杰，颖杰来学校！”他边点头边把自己的照片粘贴到出席板上。教师夸奖他说：“颖杰做的真棒！请你挥挥手跟大家打个招呼吧！”颖杰笑着看向教师和同伴。教师引导他说：“大家好！我是颖杰！”颖杰举起右手挥了挥。教师再次引导他：“大家好！”颖杰边挥手边说：“大家好！”教师说：“我是?"他马上大声说：“颖杰！”教师夸奖他说：“颖杰真棒，能跟大家打招呼介绍自己的名字！来击掌！”颖杰笑嘻嘻的和教师击掌，然后跑回去坐下来看教师和同伴继续点名。
interpretation: 通过观察可以看出颖杰知道自己的华文名字。当教师叫他的名字时，他会给予回应。颖杰能够将自己的名字与自身联系起来，对自己的身份有了一定的认同感。颖杰能够准确找到自己的照片，说明他对自己的外貌特征有一定的印象，能够将照片中的形象与自己联系起来，这是自我意识发展的重要表现。颖杰能把照片粘贴到出席板上，他知道自己在学校。颖杰能在教师的引导下和同伴打招呼并向同伴介绍自己的名字。通过这种公开的表达，他逐渐学会在集体场合中展示自己，有助于培养其社会交往技能。在整个活动过程中，颖杰表现出高度的自信、快乐和享受，非常棒！

title: 绘画“我自己”
description:
幼儿正在参与“语言斗”领域的“绘画我自己”的教学活动。教师引导幼儿观察自己的外貌特征，我们的脸上有眼睛、鼻子、嘴巴、耳朵等，引导绘画头发，绘画身体部位等。幼儿用绘画表达自己。
翊枫坐在桌前，兴致勃勃地拿起铅笔，在白纸上画了一个大大的圆形，作为自己的脸。他瞪大眼睛，仔细地看着自己的手，再看看纸上的圆圈，思索着下一步该画什么。随后，他开始在圆圈里添上两个圆圆的眼睛，并用力地点上瞳孔，像是在强调自己的眼神。接着，他小心翼翼地画出一条弯弯的线,画出微笑的样子。画着画着，他突然停下来，抬头对老师说：“老师，我要画头发！”于是，他拿起铅笔，在头顶一笔一划地画出了几条线条，表示头发，翊枫看着老师得意地笑了。
interpretation: 在这次绘画活动中，翊枫通过绘画和语言表达，能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。尝试用华语表达自己的想法。他不仅认识了自己的外貌特征，还通过语言表达增强了他的自信心和表达能力！

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（听）- 听指令：能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。

语言学习成果（写）- 写前准备：喜欢涂涂画画，能画出较直、横的线，基本能控制笔的方向。

title: 作品分析——《生气的脸》
description:
《生气的脸》活动围绕绘本《菲菲生气了——非常、非常的生气》展开，帮助幼儿认识和表达“生气”这一情绪，并通过语言与艺术创作加深理解。活动开始时，教师展示生气表情的照片，引导幼儿观察并描述表情特征，如皱眉和撅嘴。随后，幼儿通过照镜子模仿生气表情，并用华语表达自己的观察。接着，幼儿使用马克笔在纸盘上绘制“生气的脸”，再通过双面胶、吸管、扭扭棒等材料进行装饰，进一步展现情绪感受。最后，幼儿展示作品并参与整理材料，培养责任感。活动提升了幼儿的语言表达能力和创造力，帮助他们更好地理解和管理情绪。

  王宇阳在创作过程中，先使用蓝色马克笔在纸盘上绘制生气的表情。他画出两道倾斜的粗眉毛，使表情更具张力，并用简单的线条勾勒了圆圆的眼睛，嘴巴部分呈现出弯曲状，表现出生气时紧闭嘴唇的特征。在装饰阶段，他选择了多种颜色的材料，进一步丰富作品。他使用红色扭扭棒制作嘴巴，使情绪表达更加鲜明，并用蓝色、黄色和绿色的吸管装饰眉毛部分，增强立体感。他在鼻子位置使用了红色扭扭棒，使面部更加生动。
interpretation: 王宇阳的作品以纸盘为基础，充分利用马克笔、扭扭棒和吸管等材料，展现了“生气的脸”主题。他用蓝色马克笔勾勒出五官，其中眉毛向下倾斜，表现出生气时的情绪特征，嘴巴采用弯曲线条，突出了愤怒的面部表现，使表情更加生动。装饰部分，他用红色扭扭棒制作嘴巴，强化了生气的情绪表达，并使用蓝色、黄色和绿色吸管在眉毛部分进行装饰，使整体作品更加立体，增加了视觉冲击力。此外，他在鼻子部分加入了红色扭扭棒，丰富了面部细节，使作品更具完整性。从整体来看，该作品在色彩运用、材料搭配和情绪表达上表现突出，能够清晰地传达“生气”这一情绪。王宇阳在创作过程中展现了较强的观察力和创造力，能够结合自身的情绪体验进行艺术表达，作品具有较强的个性化特征。

learning_goals.title: 描述和说明他们在艺术作品中的想法和构思，开始有意识地把各种艺术元素组织在一起，创造出艺术视觉表现，如：用颜色表达情感；用线条营造动感；用模板创作各种图案。
谈论他们朋友的作品。

title: 作品分析——《生气的脸》
description:
《生气的脸》活动围绕绘本《菲菲生气了——非常、非常的生气》展开，帮助幼儿认识和表达“生气”这一情绪，并通过语言与艺术创作加深理解。活动开始时，教师展示生气表情的照片，引导幼儿观察并描述表情特征，如皱眉和撅嘴。随后，幼儿通过照镜子模仿生气表情，并用华语表达自己的观察。接着，幼儿使用马克笔在纸盘上绘制“生气的脸”，再通过双面胶、吸管、扭扭棒等材料进行装饰，进一步展现情绪感受。最后，幼儿展示作品并参与整理材料，培养责任感。活动提升了幼儿的语言表达能力和创造力，帮助他们更好地理解和管理情绪。


  曾思睿在创作过程中，先使用蓝色马克笔在纸盘上绘制生气的脸部表情。她画出了向下倾斜的眉毛，使表情更加愤怒，并用简单的圆点表现眼睛，使面部特征更加直观。嘴巴部分采用弯曲的“倒U”形状，突出了撅嘴的情绪特征。在装饰阶段，她使用了不同颜色的扭扭棒进行丰富，使作品更加生动。她用蓝色和紫色的扭扭棒制作眼睛，增强了作品的立体感；鼻子部分使用橙色扭扭棒，使整体作品的视觉中心更加突出；嘴巴部分则采用红色扭扭棒，进一步强化了生气的情绪。整个过程中，她表现得十分专注，并尝试调整材料的位置，使作品更加完整。完成后，她主动向同伴展示自己的作品，并表达自己的创作想法。
interpretation: 曾思睿的作品以纸盘为基础，运用了马克笔、扭扭棒等材料，成功表现了“生气的脸”主题。她用蓝色马克笔绘制五官，其中眉毛向下倾斜，突出了生气的情绪特征，嘴巴采用“倒U”形状，展现出紧闭嘴唇、撅嘴的愤怒情绪，使整体表情更加生动。在装饰部分，她使用了蓝色和紫色的扭扭棒制作眼睛，使面部特征更具层次感，同时使用橙色扭扭棒作为鼻子，增强了作品的对比度，使视觉焦点更加突出。嘴巴部分采用红色扭扭棒，使愤怒的情绪表达更加直观。从整体来看，该作品在色彩搭配、材料运用和情绪表达上较为丰富，能够直观地传达“生气”的情绪。曾思睿在创作过程中展现了较强的观察力和创造力，能够结合自身的情绪体验进行艺术表达，作品具有较强的个性化特征。

title: 作品分析——《生气的脸》
description:
《生气的脸》活动围绕绘本《菲菲生气了——非常、非常的生气》展开，帮助幼儿认识和表达“生气”这一情绪，并通过语言与艺术创作加深理解。活动开始时，教师展示生气表情的照片，引导幼儿观察并描述表情特征，如皱眉和撅嘴。随后，幼儿通过照镜子模仿生气表情，并用华语表达自己的观察。接着，幼儿使用马克笔在纸盘上绘制“生气的脸”，再通过双面胶、吸管、扭扭棒等材料进行装饰，进一步展现情绪感受。最后，幼儿展示作品并参与整理材料，培养责任感。活动提升了幼儿的语言表达能力和创造力，帮助他们更好地理解和管理情绪。


  余光扬在创作过程中，先使用蓝色马克笔在纸盘上绘制生气的表情，但与其他幼儿不同，他选择了绘制一个完整的人物形象，而不仅仅是脸部。他用圆形勾勒头部，并画出简洁的五官，同时手脚以简单的线条表现，使作品更具叙事性。在装饰阶段，他使用黑色扭扭棒制作一个向下倾斜的装饰，增强了人物的表情特征，同时用红色扭扭棒制作头发，使整体形象更具个性。他还选择了黄色、绿色的吸管装饰手部，使作品更加丰富。在整个过程中，他认真地调整各个材料的位置，展现了对画面整体感的关注，并在完成后向同伴展示自己的作品，表达自己的创作理念。
interpretation: 余光扬的作品不同于一般的“生气的脸”创作，他选择了完整表现一个“生气的人物”，展现出较强的构思能力。他用蓝色马克笔勾勒出人物轮廓，其中头部比例较大，五官采用简单的圆形与线条，使表情清晰可辨。黑色扭扭棒呈现明显的向下倾斜趋势，突出愤怒的情绪。红色扭扭棒用于头发装饰，使形象更具特色。黄色和绿色的吸管分别用于表现人物的手部细节，使作品在层次感上有所增强。从整体来看，该作品具有较强的故事性和想象力，幼儿不仅表达了“生气”的情绪，还赋予作品一定的情境化表达。他在创作过程中展现了良好的空间感和色彩搭配能力，同时通过添加不同材料，增强了作品的立体感和视觉吸引力，展现了独特的创造力。

title: 拔萝卜
description:
在今天的晨间活动中，老师首先带领幼儿们一起唱早安歌，一起签到问好。我们一起倾听音乐《拔萝卜》，并邀请他们一起牵手互动玩拔萝卜的游戏。幼儿们在游戏互动中，建立与朋友们良好的关系。老师和幼儿们打招呼问好，并请他们来粘贴自己的名牌。
当老师询问：“勇霖、勇霖在哪里？”他能听懂老师的话语，看向老师拍拍自己的胸口。老师请鼓励他说：“我、我在这。”他微笑的看着老师尝试说出：“我”。老师表扬他：“说的很棒！”老师请他找到自己的名牌，粘贴到学校里。他可以正确的找到自己名牌，独立的粘贴在学校里。
在音乐游戏《拔萝卜》活动中，老师邀请幼儿们牵手互动一起玩拔萝卜游戏，他主动伸出双手牵住朋友，并跟随音乐左右晃动双手。在音乐中出现“嘿呦嘿呦”时，他一直看向老师。当音乐结束老师说：“萝卜成功拔出来了”，他微笑着和老师拍手庆祝。
interpretation: 勇霖可以参与拔萝卜音乐活动。并可以尝试使用语言和动作，表达自己的想法。能够认识自己的名字，独立粘贴好自己的名牌。在游戏过程中，他能听懂老师的话语，主动与朋友牵手互动。表明了他自我意识发展良好，可以回应自己的名字

在音乐游戏《拔萝卜》活动中，老师邀请小朋友们牵手互动，一起来玩拔萝卜游戏。她主动的伸出双手牵住朋友和老师，并跟随音乐左右晃动双手。在音乐中出现“嘿呦嘿呦”时，函豫哈哈的笑出声来。当音乐结束老师说：“萝卜成功拔出来了”，她微笑着拍手庆祝。
interpretation: 函豫可以积极参与拔萝卜音乐活动，并可以认识自己的名字，独立粘贴好自己的名牌。在游戏过程中她能听懂老师的话语，表现出热情和友好，主动与朋友牵手互动。从活动中，她表示自我意识发展良好，可以回应自己的名字。

domains.title: Psycho-social Self 心理-社会行为

title: 作品分析——《生气的脸》
description:
《生气的脸》活动围绕绘本《菲菲生气了——非常、非常的生气》展开，帮助幼儿认识和表达“生气”这一情绪，并通过语言与艺术创作加深理解。活动开始时，教师展示生气表情的照片，引导幼儿观察并描述表情特征，如皱眉和撅嘴。随后，幼儿通过照镜子模仿生气表情，并用华语表达自己的观察。接着，幼儿使用马克笔在纸盘上绘制“生气的脸”，再通过双面胶、吸管、扭扭棒等材料进行装饰，进一步展现情绪感受。最后，幼儿展示作品并参与整理材料，培养责任感。活动提升了幼儿的语言表达能力和创造力，帮助他们更好地理解和管理情绪。


  何嘉樂的作品以纸盘为基础，结合绘画与立体装饰来展现“生气的脸”。他首先使用蓝色马克笔在纸盘上勾勒出五官，眉毛呈向下倾斜的弧度，眼睛圆而有神，嘴角微微上扬，呈现出略带不满的神情。其次，他选用了黄色和蓝色的吸管作为眉毛和眼睛，横向排列的方式让眉毛呈现出明显的下压趋势，突出了愤怒的情绪。竖着的蓝色吸管代表鼻子，使五官更加清晰，而嘴巴则由红色和蓝色的扭扭棒构成，嘴角向下弯曲，形成了明显的不满和生气的表情。整体作品结构分明，通过不同材质的组合，增强了表情的立体感和情绪表达。
interpretation: 何嘉樂的作品在细节刻画和材料运用上展现了较强的表现力，他通过巧妙的设计，将“生气”的情绪生动地呈现出来。在五官结构上，他利用黄色和蓝色的吸管作为眉毛和眼睛，使其具有立体感，同时眉毛向下压的设计强化了愤怒的视觉效果，使整体表情更具张力。竖直排列的蓝色吸管作为鼻子，不仅让面部比例更加协调，也增强了作品的层次感。此外，他在嘴部的设计上选用了红色和蓝色的扭扭棒，将嘴角下压的形态展现得十分明显，这种紧闭且微微下弯的嘴形表达了一种隐忍的不满情绪，而非夸张的怒吼或大张嘴巴，赋予了作品更丰富的情绪层次。整体来看，何嘉樂在作品中通过绘画与立体装饰结合，使“生气的脸”具有强烈的表现力，同时也反映出他对情绪表达的敏感度和创造力。

learning_goals.title: 描述和说明他们在艺术作品中的想法和构思，开始有意识地把各种艺术元素组织在一起，创造出艺术视觉表现，如：用颜色表达情感；用线条营造动感；用模板创作各种图案。
谈论他们朋友的作品。

title: 情绪小怪兽
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与我的情绪小怪兽活动。老师准备好彩色颜料、海绵拍、保鲜膜、假眼睛、彩纸、棉棒若干。请他们一起制作情绪小怪兽。老师介绍材料，并示范给他们看。
老师帮助章易穿上小画衣，请他自由选择自己喜欢的颜料进行活动。他选择红色、橙色、黄色、蓝色和紫色颜料。老师询问他：“这是什么颜色？”他看着老师。老师鼓励他说：“这是红色。”他尝试说出：“红色”，每当他拿起一瓶颜料，老师都会询问他：“这是什么颜色？”他在老师的鼓励，能尝试复述出颜色的名称。老师夸奖他：“说得好！”他微笑的拿起紫色颜料双手抓握住颜料瓶，用力挤压在黑色卡纸上。当挤满颜料后，老师询问他：“你完成了吗？”他微笑的点头，并拿起旁边的保险膜。老师鼓励他说：“完成了。”在老师的帮助下，他成功的盖上保鲜膜。他右手五指抓握住海绵拍，向下按压在有颜色的颜料上，待每个颜料都按压过后，他尝试独立揭开保鲜膜。老师表扬他:“真厉害！”
在作品晾干后，老师准备了假眼睛、彩色纽扣、乳白胶、棉签和装饰物若干。请他使用棉棒粘胶水装饰彩色小怪兽。他一只手使用棉棒粘胶水，另外一只手三指抓起假眼睛和纽扣装饰起情绪小怪兽。在他粘贴纽扣的时候，老师询问他：“这是小怪兽的什么啊？”他指向自己的嘴巴，老师鼓励他：“真有创意，纽扣做小嘴巴呀！”他微笑的继续粘贴起来。
interpretation: 章易可以积极参与情绪小怪兽活动，在活动中他能听懂老师的讲解，选择自己喜欢的颜料挤压在卡纸上。可以尝试使用棉棒，独立粘贴假眼睛、纽扣等装饰物。增强自己对绘画创意，同时促进手眼协调能力和手部精细动作的发展。

title: 作品分析——《生气的脸》
description:
《生气的脸》活动围绕绘本《菲菲生气了——非常、非常的生气》展开，帮助幼儿认识和表达“生气”这一情绪，并通过语言与艺术创作加深理解。活动开始时，教师展示生气表情的照片，引导幼儿观察并描述表情特征，如皱眉和撅嘴。随后，幼儿通过照镜子模仿生气表情，并用华语表达自己的观察。接着，幼儿使用马克笔在纸盘上绘制“生气的脸”，再通过双面胶、吸管、扭扭棒等材料进行装饰，进一步展现情绪感受。最后，幼儿展示作品并参与整理材料，培养责任感。活动提升了幼儿的语言表达能力和创造力，帮助他们更好地理解和管理情绪。


  Inara 的作品以纸盘为基础，结合绘画和立体装饰来呈现“生气的脸”主题。在绘画阶段，她使用橙色马克笔勾勒出两个圆形的眼睛，并用竖线表现眼泪的流动感，同时用蓝色马克笔画出排列整齐的小圆圈，形成面部轮廓，使表情更加完整。此外，她还用红色的马克笔绘制了一个实心的圆形作为鼻子，并添加红色、橙色和灰色的小点作为装饰，使画面更加丰富和生动。在装饰阶段，Inara 运用了多种立体材料增强作品的表现力。她选择了黑色扭扭棒作为一侧的眉毛，使表情更加鲜明；黄色、绿色和蓝色的吸管构成了额头和鼻子的部分，使脸部结构更加立体。嘴巴由红色和蓝色的扭扭棒组成，下弯的嘴角突出了生气的情绪。
interpretation:
Inara 的作品充分运用了绘画和立体装饰的结合，使“生气的脸”主题得到了生动呈现。从绘画层面来看，她使用橙色和蓝色的马克笔勾勒出五官，并通过竖线和小圆圈构建出眼泪和脸部轮廓，使得表情更具层次感和细节刻画。尤其是眼泪的表现，展现了她对情绪的细腻观察，突出了生气中可能伴随的委屈情绪。此外，红色实心圆形的鼻子和点缀的小色块增加了画面的丰富性，使作品更加完整和协调。

在立体装饰方面，Inara 选择了黑色扭扭棒来强化眉毛，赋予角色更加鲜明的愤怒特征。吸管的使用使额头和鼻子的结构更具立体感，增强了作品的空间层次。特别是嘴巴部分，她通过红色和蓝色的扭扭棒搭配，创造出明显下压的嘴角，成功表达了愤怒的情绪。整体来看，该作品在色彩搭配、材料使用和情绪表达上都较为突出，表现了 Inara 对愤怒情绪的理解，并通过创造性的方式进行了呈现。

title: 数学脑——《故事接龙》
description:
在《故事接龙》活动中，幼儿积极参与，通过观察图片、倾听故事和动手排序的方式，完成了菲菲情绪变化的故事排序。教师首先通过神秘箱激发幼儿的兴趣，然后引导幼儿回忆《菲菲生气了》的故事内容。幼儿在抽取图片后，仔细观察并用自己的语言讲述图片内容，他们互相倾听，并尝试根据故事发展逻辑进行排序。在排序过程中，幼儿不断调整自己的理解，以确保顺序正确。最终，所有幼儿共同复述完整的故事，展示了他们对故事内容的理解和排序能力的提升。同时，幼儿通过倾听同伴的讲述，提高了注意力和语言表达能力，与同伴建立了良好的互动。

  在活动过程中，诗恩最初尝试独立完成故事排序，她仔细观察手中的图片，并根据自己的记忆进行排列。在完成初步排序后，诗恩主动检查，发现某些部分可能需要调整，于是她重新整理了一遍。但尽管经过自我调整，仍有两处排序不正确。此时，教师引导她选择继续查阅书本或请同伴帮助，诗恩选择了向同伴寻求支持。随后，在熙恩的帮助下，两人共同合作，对图片顺序进行仔细调整，最终成功完成正确排序。整个过程中，诗恩展现了独立思考的能力，同时也表现出良好的合作意识，愿意接受建议并进行修正。
interpretation:
在本次活动中，诗恩的行为体现了教学目标和学习成果的核心要求。首先，她能够按照菲菲的情绪发展变化进行故事排序，这说明她具备基本的逻辑思维能力，并能够理解故事情节的时间顺序。其次，她在初步完成排序后，主动检查并尝试调整，表明她在排序过程中具有一定的自我反思意识，能够根据要求调整多个图片的顺序，从而符合“根据要求把三个或更多东西排序”的学习成果。

  此外，诗恩在发现自己仍然有需要改正的地方时，愿意听取教师的引导，并选择与同伴合作完成任务，这体现了她“能认真聆听同伴讲述故事图片内容”的目标要求。在同伴的帮助下，她成功调整了错误排序，表现出团队合作精神和良好的沟通能力。这一过程不仅帮助她巩固了故事顺序的理解，还培养了她在集体活动中的倾听习惯和合作能力。

  在本次活动中，陈熙恩首先凭借自己的记忆，主动对《菲菲生气了》的故事图片进行排序。她独立完成初步排列后，没有急于求助，而是仔细观察图片，逐步核对故事的发展顺序。她发现其中有两三张图片的顺序需要调整，于是有针对性地进行了修改。在未借助书本或他人帮助的情况下，熙恩通过自身的理解和逻辑推理，成功完成了故事的正确排序。整个过程中，她展现出高度的专注力和独立思考能力，能够有效运用故事情节的线索来进行排序，同时也展现出较强的观察力和对情绪变化的理解能力，符合活动的教学目标要求。

陈熙恩的表现很好地体现了活动的教学目标和学习成果。她能够按照菲菲的情绪发展变化完成故事排序，说明她对故事的时间顺序有清晰的认知，并能独立进行逻辑推理。此外，她在完成初次排序后，能够自我检查并主动调整两三张图片的顺序，符合“根据要求把三个或更多东西排序”的学习成果，展示了较强的分析能力和逻辑思维能力。

  在整个过程中，熙恩并未依赖教师或同伴的帮助，而是通过自主观察和推理来完成排序，体现了她的独立学习能力。同时，她认真聆听教师讲述故事，并将故事情节内化为自己的认知，这符合“能认真聆听同伴讲述故事图片内容”的目标要求。她对故事的情绪变化理解准确，并能迅速调整顺序，使排序正确无误，充分体现了她的专注力、逻辑思维能力以及自主解决问题的能力，展现了优秀的学习习惯和良好的认知发展水平。

interpretation:
蔡明凯的活动表现很好地契合了教学目标和学习成果。他能够按照菲菲的情绪发展变化完成故事排序，展现了对故事情节顺序的理解能力，并通过逻辑推理进行调整。同时，他在最初排序后，主动进行自我检查和调整部分图片，符合“根据要求把三个或更多东西排序”的学习目标，展现了较强的分析和判断能力。此外，他在调整后，并未直接确认自己的结果，而是积极使用书本进行对照检查，这反映出他具备良好的自学能力，并能够运用适当的学习工具来验证自己的判断。

  整个过程中，他能够认真聆听故事内容，依据图片的细节进行推理和调整，展现了较强的专注力和耐心。同时，他通过对比书本确认正确排序，体现了严谨的学习态度和独立解决问题的能力。这次活动不仅巩固了他对故事顺序的理解，也培养了他细致观察、自主学习和逻辑思考的能力，与教学目标高度吻合。

title: 作品展示：扭一扭，毛根变小兔
description:
小朋友们读故事书《逃家小兔》，喜欢小兔和妈妈玩“逃跑”和“追捉”的游戏，喜欢小兔在“逃跑”的过程中变来变去、活泼可爱的样子，小朋友们要自己动手做一只可爱的小兔。
       毛根是一种柔软、弯曲灵活，通过扭扭捏捏就能做出不同造型的手工材料。小朋友们玩毛根，将毛根弯曲成不同的形状，做出故事里的大石头、帆船、大树等造型。但是，当他们尝试用毛根做一只小兔时则遇到了很大的挑战，多数幼儿只能扭出小兔的两个长长耳朵。在老师的示范下，小朋友们跟着一步一步地弯曲和扭捏毛根，终于成功地制作了一只他们想要的可爱的小兔。
interpretation:
主要学习领域成果：

•运用不同的方式制作平面和立体的艺术作品。

•用力量控制手眼协调能力来完成某项任务。

•活动中，遇到挑战能展示出努力、不放弃的学习品质。

综合学习领域成果：

•幼儿能用毛根制作立体作品-小兔。

•发展动手操作能力，幼儿能手眼协调地弯曲毛根。

learning_goals.title: 开始学习各种基本的艺术技巧：版画、粘土创作、中国画、拼贴画、铁丝造型、将所发现的材料组合等。

title: 数学脑——《故事接龙》
description:
在《故事接龙》活动中，幼儿积极参与，通过观察图片、倾听故事和动手排序的方式，完成了菲菲情绪变化的故事排序。教师首先通过神秘箱激发幼儿的兴趣，然后引导幼儿回忆《菲菲生气了》的故事内容。幼儿在抽取图片后，仔细观察并用自己的语言讲述图片内容，他们互相倾听，并尝试根据故事发展逻辑进行排序。在排序过程中，幼儿不断调整自己的理解，以确保顺序正确。最终，所有幼儿共同复述完整的故事，展示了他们对故事内容的理解和排序能力的提升。同时，幼儿通过倾听同伴的讲述，提高了注意力和语言表达能力，与同伴建立了良好的互动。

  在活动中，蔡昀杉首先独立尝试根据自己的记忆，对《菲菲生气了》的故事图片进行排序。她完成初步排序后，并未立即确认，而是主动检查是否有错误，并进行自我调整。然而，在调整后，她仍发现有四到五处顺序不正确。此时，教师给予她两个选择——自行查阅书本或请同伴帮忙，昀杉最终选择了寻求同伴的帮助。在诗恩的协助下，两人共同分析图片的逻辑顺序，并进行了进一步的调整。经过耐心调整，她们最终正确地完成了故事排序。整个过程中，昀杉展现了较强的观察能力，同时在面对挑战时，表现出良好的合作意识和开放的学习态度。
interpretation:
昀杉的表现很好地体现了教学目标和学习成果。她能够按照菲菲的情绪发展变化完成故事排序，展现了对故事情节的理解能力和逻辑思维能力。虽然她在第一次排序后发现了错误，但她能够主动检查并进行调整，符合“根据要求把三个或更多东西排序”的学习目标。同时，她在面对排序错误时，愿意接受教师的建议，并选择与同伴合作，这不仅体现了她的团队协作意识，也符合“能认真聆听同伴讲述故事图片内容”的目标要求。

  此外，在诗恩的帮助下，昀杉学会了通过倾听他人的意见来改进自己的排序，并最终完成了正确的故事顺序。这一过程不仅提升了她对情绪变化的理解能力，也锻炼了她在团队合作中的沟通能力和耐心。整个活动帮助她培养了反思能力、协作能力以及解决问题的策略，使她在今后的学习中能够更好地应用这些经验。

在《故事接龙》活动中，幼儿积极参与，通过观察图片、倾听故事和动手排序的方式，完成了菲菲情绪变化的故事排序。教师首先通过神秘箱激发幼儿的兴趣，然后引导幼儿回忆《菲菲生气了》的故事内容。幼儿在抽取图片后，仔细观察并用自己的语言讲述图片内容，他们互相倾听，并尝试根据故事发展逻辑进行排序。在排序过程中，幼儿不断调整自己的理解，以确保顺序正确。最终，所有幼儿共同复述完整的故事，展示了他们对故事内容的理解和排序能力的提升。同时，幼儿通过倾听同伴的讲述，提高了注意力和语言表达能力，与同伴建立了良好的互动。

  在活动过程中，黄子睿最初尝试根据自己的记忆对《菲菲生气了》的故事图片进行排序。他独立完成初步排序后，并没有立即确认，而是主动观察图片，检查是否有错误。他发现有部分图片的顺序需要调整，于是进行了修改。然而，调整后仍然有两到三处顺序不正确。当教师询问他是否需要查看书本或请其他幼儿帮忙时，子睿选择了自行查阅书本来进行比对。他将图片放在书本上进行详细核对，并根据书本的内容进行了最终调整，最终成功完成了正确的排序任务。
interpretation:
黄子睿的活动表现充分体现了教学目标和学习成果。他能够按照菲菲的情绪发展变化完成故事排序，表明他对故事的时间顺序有较清晰的理解。在排序过程中，他能够自主进行检查和调整，符合“根据要求把三个或更多东西排序”的学习目标。此外，在发现错误后，他没有直接寻求同伴的帮助，而是选择利用书本资源进行自我修正，这表明他具备较强的自主学习能力和解决问题的意识。

  在整个过程中，子睿展现了较强的观察能力和逻辑思维能力。他通过对比书本细节，认真调整排序，最终成功独立完成任务，体现了他的耐心和专注力。此次活动不仅帮助他进一步巩固了故事排序的概念，也培养了他善于运用工具解决问题的学习策略。

title: 海浪鼓游戏 PTC
description: 祥宏在俯卧练习爬行时，老师拿出海洋浪鼓摇晃让海浪鼓发出海浪的声音，让后放在祥宏前方，鼓励祥宏试着玩，祥宏用手拍打海浪鼓，发出啪啪的声音，祥宏用手推拉海浪鼓，海浪鼓里面的小圆球撞击鼓面会发出海浪的声音，祥宏暂停动作聆听，然后再次反复推拉追逐海浪鼓。祥宏在反复的动作后发现了海浪鼓的正确玩法，和因果关系，祥宏沉浸在海浪鼓发出的海浪声中。

title: 好忙的蜘蛛
description:
老师通过阅读绘本《好忙的蜘蛛》，讲述蜘蛛的生活习性和身体特点，引导幼儿对蜘蛛有初步的认识。随后，老师邀请幼儿通过创意美术活动来表现自己对于蜘蛛的理解。在进行美术活动时，老师首先邀请幼儿使用油画棒绘制蜘蛛网，然后使用水粉颜料进行描绘背景。在这一过程中，老师引导幼儿观察油画棒和水粉的分离反应。接下来，幼儿使用轻粘土、活动眼睛和扭扭棒制作小蜘蛛，体验各种材料的运用。
詠皓选择了黄色的蜡笔绘制蜘蛛网，他右手五个手指和手掌合作握住油画棒进行以圆形涂鸦。蜘蛛网的部分完成后，他依旧是用右手五指握笔，然后在老师的引导下将毛笔蘸水，选取了粉色开始上色，并且在老师的引导下发现自己的蛛网并没有被水粉颜色覆盖。他抬起头看着老师向老师分享：“我的蜘蛛网”。在制作小蜘蛛时，詠皓选用了白色的轻粘土，他拿起轻粘土捏了捏，然后放在晾干的蛛网画作上，用手轻压成椭圆形。他选择了两个眼睛，老师询问他：“只要两个眼睛吗？”他点点头。然后选择了六根不同颜色的扭扭棒插到轻粘土里作为蜘蛛的脚。做好后，他笑着将作品展示给老师看，并表示想要在旁边看其他小朋友进行活动。
interpretation: 詠皓对于活动很感兴趣，在创作过程中，他使用不同的绘画工具与不同的材料结合，展现出了不断进步的绘画和创作能力，培养了詠皓对于艺术的兴趣。

title: 贴五官
description: 上午以关系为本的课程活动时间，教师带领班级幼儿一起玩“贴五官”游戏。教师为幼儿介绍了布置在墙面上空白的娃娃的脸和各种五官图片并示范了游戏玩法。教师对班级幼儿说：“小朋友们，谁要过来玩这个有趣的游戏，为卡通娃娃贴上五官呀？”培耀听到教师的话后，小身子不停地往前凑。教师问他：“培耀你要来试试吗？”培耀笑着点头说：“ya！”他迅速走到放有五官图片的小盒子旁，小手在一堆图片中翻找着。他拿起一张眼睛的图片，仔细地看了看说：“Eyes。”教师询问他：“培耀要给娃娃贴上眼睛吗？”培耀用力地点点头说：“眼睛。”他拿着眼睛图片粘贴到娃娃的脸上。但第一次没有贴准，眼睛贴得有点偏上了。培耀看着贴歪的眼睛，小眉头皱了起来。教师在一旁引导：“培耀，再调整一下哦，眼睛要在眉毛下面一点呢。”培耀迅速把眼睛图片揭下来，重新调整位置，这一次成功地把眼睛贴在了合适的地方。教师夸奖他：“培耀贴的真棒！”他笑着继续找到另外一只眼睛也贴了上去，然后抬头看向教师。教师继续引导他：“培耀真棒，把眼睛贴好了！现在我们再来找找鼻子在哪里，把它也贴上去吧。”培耀受到鼓励后，更加积极地投入到活动中。他又在图片堆里翻找出鼻子的图片，一边念叨着“鼻子”，一边把鼻子贴到了正确的位置。紧接着他又找到了嘴巴的图片粘贴娃娃的脸上。贴好后他笑着指着娃娃的脸看向教师。教师及时表扬他：“培耀真棒，把鼻子和嘴巴都贴好了！”教师继续问他：“那培耀的嘴巴在哪里呢？”培耀笑着指了指自己的嘴巴说：“嘴巴。”教师说：“对了，培耀知道自己的小嘴巴在哪里，太厉害了！我们来击掌吧！”培耀笑着跟教师击掌，然后跑开看同伴继续玩这个游戏。
interpretation: 在活动中培耀展现出了强烈的好奇心。他先是主动靠近，得到教师的允许后，他又立刻去翻找五官图片开始玩游戏，都表明他对这个活动充满了兴趣和探索的欲望。通过参与贴五官活动，他有机会去触摸、观察和摆弄各种图片，进一步激发了他对周围事物的探索热情。培耀能够模仿说出“眼睛”“鼻子”和“嘴巴”等词语，并且将对应的图片与词语联系起来，这说明他已经开始理解图片、物体与词语之间的关系。他还能根据教师提问准确的指出自己嘴巴正确的位置，真棒！在整个活动过程中，培耀表现出高度的自信、快乐和享受，非常棒！

title: 分享活动：我最爱的……
description:
老师鼓励幼儿和爸爸妈妈讨论自己最爱的物品，并将其带来学校。来到学校后，老师鼓励幼儿轮流来到台前向朋友展示和介绍自己最喜欢的物品，尝试使用简单的语句：“我是……”、“我最爱的是……”来进行表达。
老师请幼儿坐在毯子上，并邀请坐好的幼儿先进行分享。詠皓听到老师的话快速的坐下，将脚盘起来后看向老师。老师邀请詠皓进行分享，詠皓笑着走到前面，用手拨弄自己带来的玩具车，并在老师的引导下分享：“我是康詠皓，这是我的车车。”“我最爱的是车车”，他说完后看着老师的积木配件，说：“它装那些积木”，并且展示给小朋友们，一边对应形状一边说：“看哪一个是（一样的）。”他还分享了自己喜欢这辆车的理由：“因为他是一辆倒车，可以这样拉出来，积木倒出来。”老师夸奖詠皓：“詠皓真棒，可以介绍自己和自己最喜欢的物品。”在分享完毕后，他坐回地毯上，继续倾听下一位朋友的分享。
interpretation: 詠皓在活动中的表现体现了他不断发展的语言表达能力和自信心。通过詠皓的分享展现出他对自己的名字、身份和喜欢物品有了初步的认知。

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of self-concept and identity 培养自我概念和认同感，如：能使用代词“我”。

domains.title: Psycho-social Self 心理-社会行为

title: Sort Them Out
description:
Some cut-out shapes (squares, triangles, circles) were placed in a tray together with three blank pieces of paper. Children were tasked to sort the cut-outs by one attribute on their own.

Mason looked into the tray and took out a circle piece, “This one is circle!” he said. “That’s right, Mason, it is a circle, where do you want to put this shape?” his teacher prompted. “Here!” Mason replied while putting the circle piece onto a blank paper. He took another circle piece and placed it onto the same paper. “This is square! I put here cause not same.” Mason shared as he took a square piece and placed it on a blank paper. He went to take a triangle piece and placed it on the third blank paper. “There! Three shapes already. Now I can put some more.” He continued. “That’s right, Mason, I see that you have sorted them by shapes. Good job!” His teacher responded. Mason went on to sort all the remaining pieces in the tray and cheered when he was done.
interpretation: Mason displayed his ability to sort objects by one attribute and for this activity, he chose to sort them by shapes. Mason was also able to identify and name the three shapes independently too. Well done, Mason!

learning_goals.title: Sort objects by one attribute (i.e: colour, shape, or size)

title: My Emotion Colour
description:
Children were invited to think of an emotion and a colour that represents that emotion. They were invited to tear the coloured paper into smaller pieces to do an emotion collage. 

“I want yellow!” Mason told his teacher while picking a piece of yellow paper. “Sure, Mason, go ahead and tear the paper into smaller pieces.” His teacher encouraged. Mason held the end of the paper with both hands and used force tear the paper. He showed his teacher and smiled, “I did it.” His teacher praised him for the effort and Mason continued to tear and paste the papers. “I done! This is my surprised colour, you see.” Mason told his teacher while showing his surprised expression.
interpretation: Mason was able to understand the objective of the activity and managed to tear and paste the paper on his own, ensuring that the pieces fitted within the paper. Mason expressed his thoughts on choosing a coloured paper and a corresponding emotion by talking about his completed artwork. He smiled in satisfaction and was proud to talk about his artwork to his teacher.

learning_goals.title: Talk about their own artworks (e.g: what the artwork is about and the lines, colours and shapes used).

title: 数学脑 -- 投票统计
description:
教师引导幼儿分享妈妈承担家务的付出与爱，讨论表达感恩的方式（如帮拿物品、拥抱、说谢谢等），记录方法后组织投票。幼儿用自制头像卡片选出喜爱方式，集体统计票数并比较结果，过程中锻炼专注力与数算能力，强化尊重与感恩意识。

      活动开始时，教师蹲下身平视幼儿，双手摊开指向白板，微笑提问：“妈妈在家做什么家务，有煮饭吗？”佘余凯思考了一会儿，举起右手身体前倾喊道：“ Aunty cook ！”并追问：“那你难过流眼泪的时候，妈妈会做什么？”佘余凯歪头笑着回答：“妈妈hug me！”随后教师邀请幼儿分享“爱妈妈的方法”，佘余凯踮脚指向白板上的“帮拿纸巾”图片，大声说：“take tissue for 妈妈！”投票环节中，他低头专注地在卡片上画自己的头像，反复确认后贴在“帮妈妈拿纸巾”一栏。统计票数时，他跟随教师手指逐一数数：“1、2、3…5！这里有5个！”。
interpretation: 佘余凯在活动中展现出较强的自主行动意识：选择投票目标并完成头像绘制，他持续关注白板内容、检查投票卡并参与数算。整个活动过程中他的参与度相对较高，有时需要在教师的引导下才能够持续专注。从目标达成看，他成功用简单符号完成投票卡，并能在教师引导下一次性准确数算至5个物品，符合“累计到5个或以上”的数学目标，同时通过表达对妈妈的感恩行为，初步实现了情感教育目标。

description:
教师引导幼儿分享妈妈承担家务的付出与爱，讨论表达感恩的方式（如帮拿物品、拥抱、说谢谢等），记录方法后组织投票。幼儿用自制头像卡片选出喜爱方式，集体统计票数并比较结果，过程中锻炼专注力与数算能力，强化尊重与感恩意识。

     活动开始时，教师蹲下身平视幼儿，双手摊开指向白板，微笑提问：“妈妈在家做什么？”林晋毅立即举起右手，身体前倾喊道：“妈妈打扫the room,打扫房间 ！”教师点头记录“打扫房间”。并随后邀请幼儿分享“爱妈妈的方法”，他踮脚指向白板上的“拥抱”图片，大声说：“hug 妈妈,拥抱！”投票环节中，他低头专注地在卡片上画自己的头像，反复确认后贴在“拥抱”一栏，并向同伴们展示拥抱这个动作。统计票数时，他跟随教师手指逐一数数：“1、2、3…5！这里有5个！”。
interpretation: 林晋毅在活动中展现出较强的自主行动意识：独立选择投票目标并完成头像绘制，他持续关注白板内容、检查投票卡并参与数算。整个活动过程中他的参与度相对较高，有时需要在教师的引导下才能够持续专注。从目标达成看，他成功用简单符号完成投票卡，并能在教师引导下一次性准确数算至5个物品，符合“累计到5个或以上”的数学目标，同时通过表达对妈妈的感恩行为，初步实现了情感教育目标。

title: 骑三轮车
description: 下午游乐场时间，在教师的带领下培耀和同伴一起来到游乐场玩耍。进入游乐场后，培耀笑着跑到三轮车旁，小手熟练地抓住车把。教师问她他：“培耀，你要骑三轮车吗？”他笑着点点头说：“Ya！”只见他用双手抓着车把，然后抬起左脚跨过车座敏捷地坐到了三轮车上。教师问他：“培耀要骑车出发了吗？”培耀用力点点头，抬起右手挥了挥跟教师说：“拜拜！”他把小脚稳稳地踩在地面上，腰背部也挺直着，保持着身体的平衡。然后培耀开始快速地走起来，小脚丫交替着用力，带动着三轮车向前行进。速度越来越快，不一会儿就从快走变成了小跑。他的眼睛专注地看着前方，小脸上洋溢着自信和快乐的笑容，和同伴你追我赶的前进。当遇到需要转弯的地方时，培耀灵活地转动车把，身体也跟着微微倾斜，三轮车就顺利地拐过弯去。当遇到迎面有同伴走过来时，他会双手用力抓住车把，挺直腰背，双脚同时用力踩在地上使三轮车停下来，避免与同伴相撞。等同伴走过去后，他继续带动三轮车向前走，然后逐渐加速跑起来。教师在一旁关注着培耀的表现，大声鼓励道：“培耀，你骑得太棒啦！看到同伴会停下来让路你做的真好！加油！”培耀听到教师的夸奖，脸上的笑容更大了，还回头向教师挥了挥手，然后又加快速度向前骑去。
interpretation: 通过观察可以看出培耀对骑三轮车很有兴趣，他能手握车把，抬起小脚平稳地骑在三轮车上面。培耀的双手握住车把控制方向，双脚交替蹬地提供动力，腰背部挺直保持身体稳定，身体各个部位的肌肉相互配合，共同完成骑行动作。他坐在三轮车上可以快速地走和跑，这表明他的腿部肌肉力量和粗大动作发展良好。在转弯时，培耀能够灵活地转动车把并调整身体的倾斜角度，保持三轮车的平衡，顺利完成转弯动作。通过这个活动，培耀的粗大动作和四肢、腰背部肌肉的协调运动能力也都得到了很好的锻炼。在整个活动过程中培耀展现出了高度的快乐、自信和活力。

learning_goals.title: Foster gross motor development (walk, run, jump, bend, kick, throw, etc.) 发展粗大动作，如：走、跑、双脚跳、弯腰、踢、丢球等。
Develop a sense of balance （walk along a non-linear pathway/line/balance beam with little or no support, jump from a low platform and maintain balance）发展平衡感，如：锻炼四肢、腰背部肌肉的协调运动能力。

title: 好奇乐 -- 观察牙齿
description:
谢翰辉正在参与好奇乐领域的探索活动—观察牙齿。教师向幼儿示范如何用平面镜观察自己的牙齿，并鼓励幼儿轮流站在镜子前观察自己的牙齿，同时引导幼儿说出牙齿的颜色（黑色/白色）、大小（大大的/小小的）等特征。教师鼓励幼儿两人一组，轮流扮演牙医的角色，使用放大镜和电筒来检查同伴的牙齿，看是否有蛀牙。

       翰辉打开手电筒，来到平面镜前，用电筒照着自己的嘴巴，眼睛盯着镜子观察牙齿。老师问：“请问你的牙齿是什么颜色的？”他扭过头来看着老师回答道：“白色。”接着他左手拿放大镜，右手拿手电筒，观察同伴的牙齿。老师问他看到了什么，他说：“White。”接着老师问他的同伴有没有蛀牙或者黑色的牙齿，他回答道：“没有。”然后，老师引导他用句式完整地表达一次，他复述道：“她的牙齿是白色的。”
interpretation: 谢翰辉在活动中展现出明确的自主探索意识：主动操作手电筒与放大镜观察牙齿，并积极切换“牙医”角色，体现对工具使用和任务流程的自主掌控。通过快速响应提问、完整复述句式等行为，可见其认知处于积极投入状态，表现出对事物的好奇心和兴趣；同时也能够在老师的引导下结合句式说出自己的观察所见。

learning_goals.title: 观察与讨论有生命和无生命的事物：开始能用简单的语句描述他们的发现。
利用感官和简单的工具与设备（如：放大镜、平衡秤、磁铁、电筒）进行探索：使用工具帮助他们专注于观察对象，并确定观察对象的特征。

title: 今天谁来学校了？
description: 上午圆圈时间，教师带领班级幼儿围坐在出席版前进行点名活动“今天谁来学校了？”。教师看到培耀还在图书区看书，便引导他说到：“培耀，培耀在哪里？”听到教师的话，培耀把书放回书架里，然后笑嘻嘻的跑到出席版前。教师继续引导他说：“培耀找一找你的小照片在哪里呀？”培耀很快在下面一排小照片中找到了自己的照片。他把小照片取下来，边展示给教师和同伴看边说：“培耀”。教师轻轻指着出席版上学校的标志说：“今天谁来学校了？”培耀马上举起自己的小照片放到学校的标志上。教师笑着夸奖他说：“真棒！培耀来学校了。请你把小照片粘贴到出席板上吧！”培耀笑着边点头边把自己的照片粘贴到出席板上。教师夸奖他说：“培耀做的真棒！请你挥挥手跟大家打个招呼吧！”培耀笑着看向教师和同伴。教师引导他说：“大家好！我是馬培耀！”培耀举起右手挥了挥。教师再次引导他：“大家好！”培耀边挥手边小声模仿说：“大家好！”教师说：“我是?"他马上大声说：“馬培耀！”教师夸奖他说：“培耀真棒，能跟大家打招呼介绍自己的名字！来击掌！”培耀笑着和教师击掌，然后跑回去坐下来看教师和同伴继续点名。
interpretation: 通过观察可以看出培耀知道自己的华文名字。当教师叫他的名字时，他会给予回应。培耀能够将自己的名字与自身联系起来，对自己的身份有了一定的认同感。培耀能够准确找到自己的照片，说明他对自己的外貌特征有一定的印象，能够将照片中的形象与自己联系起来，这是自我意识发展的重要表现。培耀能把照片粘贴到出席板上，他知道自己在学校。他能在教师的引导下和同伴打招呼并向同伴介绍自己的名字。通过这种公开的表达，他逐渐学会在集体场合中展示自己，有助于培养其社会交往技能。在整个活动过程中，培耀表现出高度的自信、快乐和享受，非常棒！

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of self (responding to their names) 培养自我意识，如：回应自己的名字等。
Foster social skills at all times – routines, interactions and activities 在常规活动、互动和体验中，初步培养社会交往技能。

title: I Can Sing a Rainbow!
description:
Sarah Mishel was invited to explore a colourful wooden xylophone set. As she struck each bar, she noticed the different sounds produced. While playing, she narrated her actions, saying, “I hit the red one, then orange, then blue.”

The teacher responded, “Wow! You have so many colours, just like a rainbow!” Sarah then started singing, “I can sing a rainbow, sing a rainbow, you can sing it too.” The teacher encouraged her by saying, “That’s very good singing, Sarah.”

Sarah smiled, picked up a hand clapper, and began clapping at a fast pace while continuing to sing the song.
interpretation: Sarah Mishel demonstrates growing expressive language skills by narrating her actions while playing (“I hit the red one, then orange, then blue”) and naming colours accurately. She engages in conversation, responding appropriately to the teacher and making connections by recalling and singing a familiar song. Her speech is clear, and she confidently expresses herself through both words and singing.

description:
老师与他在大自然区域互动。
刚开始他听老师唱歌，接着就拍拍手配搭；然来，他用双手拍打盖在轮胎的板来制造节凑配搭老师的唱歌。
接着他爬去拿一个手摇铃，跪着敲盖在轮胎的板再次来制造节凑配搭老师的唱歌。
越敲越起劲，他就站起来敲节凑更加强壮；更加开心。
他达到创造音乐节凑初步发展目标，真棒！

title: 鳄鱼牙齿有几颗？
description:
在角落游戏时，教师出示纸质鳄鱼嘴巴模型，带领幼儿观察并讨论鳄鱼头部的外形特征。老师鼓励幼儿根据观察猜测鳄鱼的牙齿数量，邀请幼儿用手指点数的方式数出牙齿数量。通过活动，幼儿学习到一次计数一个物品，鼓励幼儿学习数五或以上数字。

 当教师邀请隽恩测鳄鱼的牙齿数量时，隽恩大声说：“5”，并在数牙齿时，一直看着模型牙齿数数，隽恩使用手指数一数每颗牙齿，与猜测结果进行对比。隽恩一边用手指出鳄鱼的牙齿，一边说：一，二，三，四，五“。当老师问：“隽恩，鳄鱼有几颗牙齿？” 隽恩一边手比五，一边告诉老师：“五”。接着隽恩又重复玩了不同数量的鳄鱼牙齿教具，他能一一说出正确的牙齿数量。
interpretation: 隽恩能够数数一至五，隽恩一边用手指出鳄鱼的牙齿，一边说：一，二，三，四，五“。他能积极与认真的完成活动，他能理解一个口头指示，并按照指示完成数鳄鱼牙齿的任务。隽恩多次重复的玩游戏，表现出专注和耐心。表示他的专注力和坚持不懈的态度。

learning_goals.title: 一次计算一个物品，准确地累计到5个或以上。

title: 一起种植苋菜
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与种植苋菜活动。老师介绍材料杯子、水、泥土和苋菜种子，鼓励幼儿感知认识材料。老师首先示范如何种植苋菜种子，鼓励幼儿将种子放进泥土中，帮种植好的植物浇水。
老师拿出苋菜种子，对幼儿们说:“你看这是什么?”Vikranth 看向老师。老师说：“这是苋菜种子，你看它的叶子是什么颜色？”Vikranth 伸出小手触摸种子袋子上画的红色的苋菜。老师对他说：“苋菜长大是红色的，我们要不要一起种苋菜。”Vikranth 看向老师点点头。老师分发装好的泥土，鼓励他们感知认识泥土和种子。Vikranth 闻一闻泥土和苋菜，又尝试五指抓握一把泥土，触摸感知泥土放下。看向自己的小手沾上黑色的泥土，伸手示意老师看。老师询问他：“要擦擦手吗？”他点点头。老师边帮助他擦手，边鼓励他说：“黑色的泥土。”Vikranth 可以复述说出：“黑”老师表扬他：“真棒！”在出示苋菜种子的时候，他那起种子的袋子放在耳朵旁边左右摇晃，微笑的看向老师。老师问他：“你听到什么声音？”他很大幅度的摇晃苋菜种子口袋。老师说：“听起来像沙沙声。”Vikranth 尝试快速摇晃种子口袋，再次倾听声音。老师把苋菜种子倒出来放在盘子上，鼓励幼儿们观察。Vikranth 低头看向种子，又伸出小手捏起苋菜种子揉捏。老师询问他：“苋菜的种子是大大的还是小小的。”他捏起苋菜种子给老师看。老师说：“苋菜的种子是小小的。”我们可以把小小的苋菜种子放进泥土中。Vikranth 五指抓握一把种子，放进泥土中。老师表扬他：“真厉害！”在种子种好后，Vikranth 可以独立抓握纸杯给种植好的种子浇水。老师和他击掌庆祝，他微笑着伸出手回应老师。
interpretation: Vikranth 可以参与种植苋菜的活动。并可以听懂老师的话语，使用动作表达自己的想法。并可以通过闻一闻、听一听、看一看、触摸等多感官的观察泥土和种子。通过苋菜种子种植活动，初步培养他对自然环境的兴趣和好奇心。

title: 穿大鞋向前走
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起玩穿大鞋子向前走活动。老师准备好纸板做好的大鞋子，示范如何进行游戏。鼓励幼儿们尝试穿着大鞋子，保持身体平衡的向前走。
老师拿出纸板做好的大鞋子，对幼儿们说：“你看这是什么？”紫萱看向老师手里的鞋子说：“shoe”老师鼓励她说：“鞋子。”她可以尝试说：“鞋，”老师表扬她：“真厉害！”老师说：“谁要穿大鞋子？”紫萱看向老师说：“Levelle ”老师鼓励她说：“我、紫萱要玩。”她回复老师说：“我。”老师表扬紫萱：“好棒呀！”并帮助紫萱穿好大大的鞋子。并扶助紫萱，鼓励她向前行走。她刚开始有一些不稳，牵着老师的手低头看着自己的脚丫。在行走的过程中，她抬起头放开老师扶助的手，尝试小步向前行走。渐渐的她加快了行走的速度，步子也逐渐变大。还可以穿鞋大鞋子转弯，蹲下站起来。
interpretation: 紫萱可以参与穿大鞋向前走活动。并可以听懂老师的话语，尝试使用语言和动作表达自己的想法。她可以穿着大鞋子保持平衡向前行走，还可以独立蹲下站起来,表明紫萱平衡和粗大动作的发展良好。

title: 穿大鞋向前走
description:

”彩绚跑过来看老师手里的鞋子，老师介绍纸板做的鞋子，并引导彩绚观察。彩绚双手拿起大鞋子看了看，又用手拉动上面的绳子。老师对她说：“你想要穿大鞋子吗？”彩绚看着老师微笑的点点头。老师鼓励她说：“我要穿。”彩绚拍拍自己的胸口，尝试说：“我。”老师表扬她：“很棒！”询问她：“你要穿什么颜色的鞋子？”她指黄色的大鞋子。老师鼓励她说：“黄色。”她微笑的低下头。老师边帮助彩绚穿大鞋子的时候，她观察老师的动作，并抬起脚配合老师穿鞋子。穿好大鞋子站起来的时候，她牵住老师的手站着观察自己的小脚。老师说：“我们向前走好不好？”彩妆慢慢的抬起脚向前迈开脚步，在向前走路的过程中，她一直低头看自己的脚。在慢慢的行走中，彩绚逐渐放松下来。可以抬起头，保持平衡向前行走。
interpretation: 彩绚基本可以参与穿大鞋子向前走活动。她可以听懂老师的话语，使用动作和语言表达自己的想法。并可以尝试新事物，战胜害怕勇敢的保持平衡向前行走。

老师拿出纸板做好的大鞋子，对幼儿们说：“你看这是什么？”哲恩看向老师手里的鞋子，大声的说：“shoes。 ”老师鼓励他说：“鞋子。”哲恩马上模仿老师说：“鞋子。”老师夸奖他：“说得好！”老师边做动作边询问小朋友们：“这个鞋子是很大还是很小啊？”哲恩双手张开说：“很大。”老师微笑的和他击掌，并肯定的说：“哲恩真棒！这个鞋子很大。”我们可以比一比，这个鞋子大不大。哲恩踩在大鞋子面，蹲下来低头观察自己的脚丫，然后尝试穿大鞋子。老师询问他：“你要穿大鞋子吗？”哲恩说：“yes”老师鼓励他说：“是的，我要穿。”哲恩尝试缓慢的说出：“是的，我要穿。”老师表扬他：“真厉害！”在他穿好大鞋子后，他双手分开撑住地板，向上抬起屁股成功的站起来。低头观察自己的脚丫和鞋子，尝试调整脚步向前行走。走了几步发现很稳后。他目视前方，微笑的向前行走。并且迈开的步伐逐渐变大，行走的速度也越来越快。还可以独立的转弯、双脚并拢停止。
interpretation: 哲恩可以积极的参与穿大鞋向前走的活动。可以听懂老师的话语，尝试使用语言表达自己的想法。同时可以穿大鞋子尝试站立、行走、转弯、加速走、停止等动作。说明哲恩的平衡和粗大动作发展良好。

title: 小手拍拍
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与小手拍拍的活动。在游戏中请他们认识自己的身体部位和名称，并找一找都在哪里。
当老师询问：“小手拍拍、小手拍拍，手指伸出来，嘴巴在哪里？用手指出来”，勇霖跟随老师一起拍手,并尝试指出自己的嘴巴。在老师询问：“耳朵在哪里？”他看着老师指自己的耳朵。老师夸奖他：“很棒！能够准确的找到自己的五官在哪里。”勇霖微笑的看向老师。当老师出示人脸粘贴板时，请小朋友来贴一贴。他拿起五官并尝试粘贴到人脸上。老师询问他：“嘴巴在哪里？你可以找出来吗？”勇霖低头寻找,找到嘴巴后看向老师。老师表扬他：“真厉害！这么快找到嘴巴。”老师鼓励他说：“嘴巴。”勇霖看着老师拿起嘴巴贴在粘贴板上，又低头找起来其他的五官。
interpretation: 勇霖基本可以参与小手拍拍活动。可以听懂老师的话语，使用动作表达自己的想法。同时能跟随老师一起拍手找五官，通过匹配游戏互动，与老师和朋友建立良好关系。

title: 折返跑
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与折返跑活动。出示材料沙包，引导他们观察和认识。并示范折返跑的规则，从红色圆形起点出发，跑到蓝色三角锥处蹲下拍一下三角锥。在跑回红色圆形起点，蹲下拿起沙包。折返跑回蓝色三角锥处放下沙包，跑回红色的圆形起点，完成折返跑活动。
老师出示沙包鼓励幼儿们观察和认识。勇霖五指抓握拿起沙包，左右摇晃甩了出去。他又拾起地上的沙包，放在耳朵处来回摇晃。老师询问他：“你听到什么声音？”他摇晃沙包的频率更大。老师说：“你听到沙沙声吗？”他看向老师点点头。老师邀请他一起和朋友参与折返跑活动。勇霖站起来，与老师牵手从红色圆形出发。在跑到三角锥的过程中，勇霖逐渐的加快了步伐。从慢走过度到快走。到了老师三角锥处，放开老师的手弯腰拍了拍蓝色三角锥。又独立站起来转过身向红色圆形起点处行走，老师鼓励他：“加油快点跑，”他加快了行走的步伐。到了红色圆形处，单手捡拾旁边的沙包，又尝试跑回蓝色的三角锥。弯腰蹲下双手拿起沙包，尝试放在三角锥顶端。试了一次掉下来，他又拾起沙包再次尝试。当成功的把沙包放在三角锥顶端，微笑的自己拍拍手庆祝。老师鼓励他跑回红色圆形处。他又站起来，转身往红色圆形起点处跑。成功的完成了折返跑活动，老师与他击掌庆祝，他微笑的伸出小手回应。
interpretation: 勇霖可以参与折返跑活动，并能听懂老师的话语，使用动作和微笑回应老师。也可以听懂规则，尝试完成折返跑活动。在活动中他可以做到弯腰、蹲下和三角锥击掌、能独立站起来转身向回跑，表明了他粗大动作发展良好。

title: 折返跑
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与折返跑活动。出示材料沙包，引导他们观察和认识。并示范折返跑的规则，从红色圆形起点出发，跑到蓝色三角锥处蹲下拍一下三角锥。在跑回红色圆形起点，蹲下拿起沙包。折返跑回蓝色三角锥处放下沙包，跑回红色的圆形起点，完成折返跑活动。
老师出示沙包鼓励他们观察和认识。章易五指抓握拿起沙包，又放在耳朵处来回摇晃。老师询问他：“你听到什么声音？”他摇晃沙包的频率更大。老师说：“你听到沙沙声吗？”他看向老师微笑着点点头。老师邀请他一起和朋友参与折返跑活动。他站起来，独立的走到红色圆形处。当老师说：“开始”时，他双手前后摆动、迈开步伐向前跑起来。在跑到三角锥处，他逐渐的减慢了步伐，慢慢的蹲下来伸出小手拍拍蓝色的三角锥。在站起来转过身向红色圆形处奔跑。到了红色圆形处，弯腰单手捡拾旁边的沙包，又跑回蓝色的三角锥。弯腰蹲下双手拿起沙包，尝试放在三角椎顶端。在成功后他转身跑回红色圆形处，成功的完成了折返跑活动。老师与他击掌庆祝，他微笑的伸出小手回应。
interpretation: 章易可以参与折返跑活动，并能听懂老师的话语，使用动作和微笑回应老师。他可以听懂规则，尝试完成折返跑活动。在活动中，可以做到弯腰保持平衡，下蹲放下沙包、拍打蓝色三角锥。也可以双手摆动加快步伐奔跑起来，并能独立站起来、转身向回跑，表明了他粗大动作发展良好。

title: 三月份：有趣的感观袋  （PTC )
description: 老师精心制作了两个感官袋：一个装有鲜花，另一个装有小木鱼，并注入水后密封。依璇对袋中漂浮的花朵和鱼充满好奇，忍不住用手触摸、拍打，甚至用手按压鲜花和小木鱼。依璇在探索中感到快乐，抬起头来，满怀喜悦地望着老师。

Develop focus and concentration  through sustained involvement in routines, transitions and experiences 通过常规活动、互动和体验，初步培养婴幼儿的持续参与-注意力。
Foster curiosity and exploration in a well-planned environment with intentional interactions 通过精心创设的环境和互动，初步培养好奇心和探索意识。

title: 小兔子跳跳跳
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起玩小兔子跳跳跳活动。老师准备好扁扁的圆形呼啦圈排成一排。示范如何进行游戏，幼儿们尝试模仿小兔子，双脚弯曲、向上跳过呼啦圈。
老师拿出呼啦圈，对他们说：“你看这是什么？它是什么形状的？”翰毅说：“circle”老师鼓励翰毅说：“呼啦圈、圆形。”他微笑着缓慢复述出：“呼啦圈、圆形。”老师表扬他：“说得好！”并和他击掌庆祝。老师讲解玩法，并示范如何模仿小兔子，双脚弯曲向上跳进呼啦圈。翰毅看向老师的时候，已经开始尝试跳入呼啦圈中。在老师播放音乐小兔子跳跳跳时，翰毅可以尝试双腿并拢向上起跳，成功的跳入呼啦圈。落地的时候也能保持平衡，两只脚一前一后的落在地上。在反复尝试中，翰毅从一个呼啦圈跳进另一个呼啦圈时，要重新调整步伐。逐渐过度到可以双手放在头上做小兔子耳朵，双脚连续跳过呼啦圈，不需要调整步伐。而且跳的很高，落地也非常稳。
interpretation: 翰毅可以参与小兔子跳跳跳活动。并可以使用语言和动作，表达自己的想法。翰毅可以双脚跳，平稳的落在地上，表明他粗大动作发展良好。

title: 我的表情变变变
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起参与我的表情变变变活动。老师出示镜子，鼓励幼儿们照着镜子观察自己的表情。老师播放音乐，表演我的表情变变变。变成高兴、生气、沮丧、思考、惊讶等表情。鼓励他们观察和模仿，感知表情的变化。
老师出示镜子，对他们说：“你看这是什么？”彩绚看着镜子里的自己，露出微笑。老师鼓励她：“哎呦镜子里的彩绚微笑了，是感到开心了吗？”彩绚微笑的抬头看向老师。老师介绍表情高兴开心的时候我们都会哈哈笑出声，生气的时候我都是撅嘴巴，“哼”扭头不理人。她边看老师做的表情边哈哈的笑出声。老师播放音乐我的表情变变变，鼓励小朋友们一起坐动作表演，每当老师做我的表情变变变的时候。双手挡住脸在打开做开心、生气等表情时，彩绚都会哈哈的笑出声来。在音乐声中她可以尝试使用动作，模仿老师双手捂脸在打开微笑。老师表扬她：“做的很好！”并与她击掌庆祝。她微笑着回应老师的动作。老师鼓励彩绚照镜子，看看自己开心、生气、沮丧都是什么表情。她低头看着镜子里的自己。
interpretation: 彩绚可以积极参与我的表情变变变活动并可以听懂老师的话语，使用动作和微笑回应老师。她可以尝试模仿老师做我的表情变变变，双手捂脸在打开做开心的表情。

title: 一起来浇水
description:
老师邀请幼儿们参与一起来浇水活动。老师准备了小水桶、纸杯、水和小水盆等工具。鼓励幼儿们观察植物，尝试使用工具给植物浇水。
老师拿出自然区的植物，对幼儿们说：“你们看这些花盆里的土都干了，我们要不要给它浇浇水啊？”紫萱看着老师点头。老师鼓励她说：“要。”紫萱可以模仿老师说：“要。”老师表扬她：“真棒！”并和她击掌庆祝。老师拿出工具，并让她观察，选择自己喜欢的工具浇水。紫萱选择了红色纸杯，老师询问她：“你选的是什么啊？”紫萱低头看向自己手里的纸杯，又看向老师。老师鼓励她说：“纸杯。”她可以尝试说出：“杯。”老师鼓励她：“说的好！”并引导她使用杯子舀水浇花。紫萱可以单手抓握杯子装水，在移动到花盆前向下倒水。在第一次尝试浇花，水不小心倒出来了。她马上低头观察，并调整方向，抬高水杯向叶子的上方浇水。在浇水成功后，老师夸奖紫萱：“真厉害！”她微笑着继续舀水浇花。
interpretation: 紫萱基本可以参与一起来浇水活动。在活动中，她可以尝试使用语言和动作，表达自己的想法。通过观察和探索给植物浇水的活动，初步培养了她对自然的兴趣和好奇心。

title: Shapes Race Slide
description: The teacher created large cutouts of various shapes (circle, square, triangle, rectangle and circle) and placed them at one end of the play area. The children picked a shape and then slid around the play space by alternating their legs. As they moved around the playground, they matched the shape they chose to real-world objects. Caleb chose the shape circle and eagerly began sliding around the playground. He shuffled his feet back and forth swiftly, moving around the area with excitement. After a few moments, he stopped in front of the tires and shouted, "Teacher Lilian, circle!" while pointing to the tires. When the teacher arrived by his side, Caleb explained, "This thing is like a circle." before shuffling his feet back and forth once more. He quickly moved away from the tires and discovered another circle near the ropes. "Teacher Lilian, another circle!" he beamed, proudly pointing to the circle shape at the top of the structure.
interpretation: This experience showed that Caleb enjoyed learning and applying math in his daily life by actively exploring shapes around him. His excitement and enthusiasm as he moved around the playground and found circles in objects like the tires and the playground structure highlighted his ability to identify shapes and relate them to real-life examples. When Caleb pointed out the circles on the tires and the structure without hesitation, he not only showed that he recognized the shapes but was also able to connect them to familiar items, thereby reinforcing his understanding of geometric concepts. His lively interaction with the teacher and his use of language to describe the shapes also helped expand his math vocabulary.

learning_goals.title: Enjoy learning and using Math in daily experiences.

title: Shape Race Slide
description: The teacher created large cutouts of different shapes (circle, square, triangle, rectangle, and oval) and placed them at one end of the play area. The children picked a shape and then slid around the space, alternating their legs. As they moved around the playground, they matched the shape they chose to real-world objects. Arthur selected the oval and excitedly began sliding across the playground. He swiftly shuffled his feet, moving with great enthusiasm. After a few moments, he stopped beneath the playground structure and called out, "Teacher Lilian, oval!" while pointing to an oval-shaped opening. When Teacher Lilian arrived, Arthur explained, "This is like an oval," before resuming his playful shuffling. He then moved away from the structure and discovered another oval shape on the steps leading to the slide. "Teacher Lilian, I found another oval!" he beamed, proudly pointing to the shape on the step.
interpretation: This experience revealed that Arthur enjoyed learning and using math in his daily life by actively engaging with shapes in his surroundings. His excitement as he slid around the playground and discovered ovals in real-world objects, such as the oval opening under the playground structure and the oval shape on the slide steps, showed his ability to identify shapes and connect them to familiar items. By pointing out these shapes confidently, Arthur demonstrated his understanding of geometric concepts, linking abstract shapes to concrete examples.

title: Number Slide Adventure
description: The children went to the slide area at the playground, where the teacher had placed number cards ranging from 1 to 10 at the bottom of the slide. One by one, each child took a turn sliding down, picked up a card, and called out the number they selected. Afterward, they were encouraged to connect the number to a daily experience. When it was Dylan’s turn, he beamed with excitement and eagerly marched up the stairs to slide down. He grabbed the number card marked with the number 10. When the teacher asked him to identify the number on the card, Dylan promptly said, "Ten!" After a brief moment of thought, the teacher asked Dylan to recall an experience that related to the number 10. Dylan then said, "I saw 10 houses when I come to school today."
interpretation: When Dylan picked the card marked with the number 10, he immediately recognized it and called out, "Ten!" This demonstrated his ability to recognise numerals and their meanings. The teacher then prompted Dylan to connect the number to a real-life experience, and Dylan was able to recall seeing "10 houses on my way to school today." This connection between the number 10 and his daily experience showed that Dylan was able to apply his counting skills in a meaningful way, reinforcing his understanding of numbers through real-world examples.

title: Exploring “Love You Forever” By Robert Munsch
description: Following the read-aloud of “Love You Forever” the previous day, the teacher led a group discussion focused on deepening the children's understanding of the story. The discussion began with identifying the main characters of the book. The teacher then asked the children to recall the sequence of events from the book. A friend kickstarted the discussion by saying “The mummy carry the baby and rock him back and forth”. Chloe then jumped onto the conversation and shared “The boy throw, take the mama’s watch then drop inside the toilet bowl and flush it.” As the discussion continued, it reached the climax of the story. The question “How do you think the man feels when he is standing at the stairs?” was posted to the children. Chloe shared “He’s sad”. When probed, Chloe continued by saying “because he miss his mama.”
interpretation: This experience showed Chloe gaining meaning by listening as she actively engaged in the group discussion, listening to her classmates' contributions and building upon them with her own thoughts. When her friend began the conversation by recalling an event from the book, Chloe attentively listened and then contributed her own observation, adding to the understanding of the storyline. As the discussion continued and the children reflected on the emotional aspects of the story, Chloe listened carefully and understood the teacher’s question about the man’s feelings and responded thoughtfully. Her answer, “He’s sad,” “because he miss his mama” showed that she was able to comprehend the emotional depth of the story. Through this experience, Chloe demonstrated her ability to gain meaning by listening to the content of the story and the insights shared by her peers and teachers.

learning_goals.title: Gain meaning by listening.

title: Exploring "Love You Forever" By Robert Munsch
description: Following the read-aloud of “Love You Forever” the previous day, the teacher led a group discussion focused on deepening the children's understanding of the story. The discussion began with identifying the main characters of the book. After hearing a friend identify “The boy” as one of the main characters, River exclaimed “The mama!” The teacher then asked the children to recall the sequence of events from the book. A friend kickstarted the discussion by saying “The mama go and rock the baby.” The teacher questioned whether that was the start of the book and River verbalised "No! She gave birth to the baby!"
interpretation: This experience showed River gaining meaning by listening as she actively engaged in the group discussion and demonstrated her understanding of the story. When her friend identified “The boy” as one of the main characters, River added to the conversation by exclaiming, “The mama!” This response showed that she had been following the discussion and had a clear grasp of the key characters in the story. When the teacher asked the children to recall the sequence of events, River listened attentively to her peer's statement about the mama rocking the baby. She then responded with her own insight, verbally correcting the sequence by saying, "No! She gave birth to the baby!" This demonstrated that River was not only listening to her peers but also carefully listening to the teacher's prompts and instructions. By processing the story's details, making connections, and using her understanding of the plot, River contributed meaningfully to the discussion.

title: Rainbow Sorting Garden
description: The teacher set up a mini "garden" space filled with colorful paper flowers in various shapes (such as circles, triangles, and squares) and sizes. Alongside the garden, there were ‘flower pots’ labeled with specific attributes, "yellow circles" and"blue triangles." Elish looked through the tray of flowers and picked up a flower made with yellow circles. She planted the flower in the ‘yellow circle’ flower pot and moved back to the tray. Rummaging her hand through the flowers, she stopped at the sight of yellow and picked the flower up. After examining the shape on the flower, she looked up at the teacher. The teacher probed, “Elish, is this flower made with yellow circles?” Almost immediately, Elish shook her head. The teacher continued, “What’s different about this flower?” Elish responded, “This is square.” Nodding her head, the teacher asked, “Ah, so the yellow color is right, but the square shape is wrong?” Elish nodded and placed the yellow square flower back on the tray.
interpretation: This experience showed Elish’s ability to match objects by two attributes—color and shape—through her thoughtful approach to sorting the flowers. Initially, she successfully matched the yellow circle flower with the "yellow circle" flower pot, demonstrating her understanding of both the color and shape attributes. When Elish selected a yellow flower that was a square, she recognized that while the color was correct, the shape did not match the designated ‘yellow circle’ label. Her ability to notice the difference in shape and correctly identify that it was a square instead of a circle indicates her understanding of grouping by two attributes—color and shape—and her capacity to distinguish between them. Her self-correction further shows her skill in categorizing objects by multiple attributes, as she understood that both the color and the shape needed to be right for the flower to go in the correct pot.

learning_goals.title: Match objects by two attributes (e.g: colour and shape, colour and size)

title: Rainbow Sorting Garden
description: The teacher set up a mini "garden" space filled with colorful paper flowers in various shapes (such as circles, triangles, and squares) and sizes. Alongside the garden, there were ‘flower pots’ labeled with specific attributes, "yellow circles" and"blue triangles." Damien looked through the tray of flowers and picked up a flower made with blue triangles. While planting the flower into the ‘blue triangle’ flower pot, he muttered “blue triangle over here.” and swiftly moved back to the tray. Rummaging his hand through the flowers, he stopped at the sight of blue and picked the flower up. After examining the shape on the flower, he showed it to the teacher and placed it down. He then continued to pick out and plant all the ‘blue triangle’ flowers accurately into the ‘blue triangle’ flower pot. When the teacher picked out the blue circle flower and asked “Earlier, I saw you pick this flower up but you put it down again. Why?”, Damien shared without hesitation “This is not triangle!” The teacher continued to ask “So can you tell me what’s the same and what’s different?” Damien swiftly replied “They are same colour but not the same shape.”
interpretation: This experience demonstrated Damien’s ability to match objects by two attributes—color and shape—through his careful observation and decision-making. When Damien selected the blue triangle flower and correctly placed it into the "blue triangle" flower pot, he showed that he could accurately match both the color and the shape of the flower to the label on the pot. As he continued to pick and place all the ‘blue triangle’ flowers into the correct pot, it is evident that he understood the need to consider both attributes simultaneously when sorting. When Damien came across the blue circle flower and initially picked it up, he noticed that while the color was correct, the shape did not match the ‘triangle’ attribute. His decision to place the flower back on the tray and explain, "This is not triangle!" showed his clear recognition that both the color and shape must match for proper sorting. When the teacher asked him to describe the similarities and differences, Damien’s swift and accurate response, “They are same colour but not the same shape,” further demonstrated his ability to distinguish and match based on two attributes.

title: Stop and Go Balance Challenge
description: The teacher explained the green and red signals: green meant moving forward with various movements, and red required stopping and balancing on one leg. The teacher then demonstrated different movements and encouraged the children to try. Dylan started by walking when he saw the green signal. When the teacher changed to the red signal, he swiftly stopped in his place and lifted his left foot. His body slanted to the right, so he stretched his arms out to his sides and leaned to the left to maintain his balance. He stood on his right foot for five seconds before putting it down. As the teacher introduced jumping, Dylan began jumping with both feet off the ground. When the signal changed to red again, Dylan quickly lifted his left foot and stretched both arms out, stably keeping his balance.
interpretation: This experience showed moving with balance and control as Dylan demonstrated the ability to respond quickly to the green and red signals while maintaining stability. When moving, he was able to adjust his movements—whether walking or jumping—while ensuring he didn’t lose control of his body. Upon the red signal, Dylan demonstrated control by immediately stopping and lifting his left foot, carefully adjusting his body posture to counterbalance any instability. His ability to stretch his arms and lean in the opposite direction to maintain his balance showed how he was using control over his body movements. Dylan’s quick adjustments and ability to stably hold his balance during both walking and jumping movements demonstrated his developing skills in moving with control.

learning_goals.title: Move with balance and control.

title: Numicon Puzzle Art
description: The children were provided with a collection of mixed-up Numicon pieces and were challenged to sort them based on two different attributes. The teacher shared with David two specific attributes: red Numicon pieces with 5 circles. Digging into the mixed-up Numicon pieces, David picked out a red Numicon and counted out loud “1, 2, 3, 4, 5!” When asked if it was the right Numicon piece, red with 5 circles, David exclaimed “Yes!” and placed it on his plate. Afterward, the teacher encouraged David to pick out a Numicon piece that he liked and David chose the pink Numicon piece with 7 circles. He then picked out another 2 pieces with the same attributes. When asked which two attributes his Numicon piece had, he proudly said, "Teacher Lilian, this is pink. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7!"
interpretation: Through this experience, David demonstrated his ability to match objects based on two attributes: color and the number of circles. When the teacher asked him to find a red Numicon piece with 5 circles, David understood that both attributes needed to match. He carefully selected a red Numicon piece and counted the circles aloud, saying, “1, 2, 3, 4, 5!” After confirming that both the color (red) and the number of circles (5) were correct, he confidently placed the piece on his plate. When asked about the attributes of his chosen Numicon, David proudly said, "Teacher Lilian, this is pink. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7!" This statement showed that he understood he needed to consider both the color (pink) and the number of circles (7) to identify and match the correct pieces. Through these actions, David clearly demonstrated his ability to match objects based on both the color and the number of circles.

title: Family Tree Creation
description: In this creative activity, children used materials collected from yesterday’s walk, along with various art supplies, to construct their own family tree. Caleb took twigs and poked them into a paper cup, creating the base of his tree. He then grabbed a piece of paper and a pencil to draw out his family. First, he drew a circle and added a smiley face with pigtails, saying, "This is my mama." Next, he drew his father, followed by himself. When asked about his younger brother, Caleb exclaimed, "Oh!" and proceeded to draw his brother inside his mother’s body. As he continued drawing, Caleb said, “I draw my didi very small.” He then used a pair of scissors to carefully cut out the figurines and pasted them onto the twigs with tape and glue. As Caleb arranged each figure on the tree, he proudly pointed to each one, explaining who they were.
interpretation: This activity demonstrated that Caleb was beginning to become familiar with and differentiate the application of each conventional art media through his thoughtful use of various materials. For example, Caleb used a pencil to draw his family members, showing an understanding of how to create detail and structure. He applied scissors to cut out the shapes, demonstrating his ability to work with tools and manipulate paper for specific purposes. The glue and tape were used to attach the figures to the twigs, indicating his grasp of adhesive materials and their role in assembling and securing components. By selecting and applying each material in the right context—drawing for representation, cutting for shaping, and gluing/taping for assembly—Caleb showed growing proficiency in using the appropriate media to enhance his artwork and create a cohesive, meaningful project.

learning_goals.title: Begin to become familiar with and to differentiate the application of each conventional art media.

title: Journal: Feelings Towards Family
description: Children reflected on a question posed by the teacher in relation to this term’s topic, Learning About My Family. Chloe took some time to think about how she feels when she is with her family. After reflecting, she picked up her pencil and began to draw a circle with a smiley face in the middle of her book. When her teacher asked, “Tell me more about your drawing,” Chloe responded, “This is me.” To her right, she drew another circle with a smiley face and a rectangle beneath it. “And then this is my mummy. We are happy together,” she explained. As she described her drawing, she added several downward lines on both sides of her mother’s face, saying, “My mummy has long hair.” Then, to her right, Chloe drew another circle with a smiley face and a rectangle beneath it, saying, “This is my daddy.” When asked how she feels with her family, Chloe replied, “Happy, all happy because my family is here.” Through her drawings and words, Chloe expressed a clear sense of warmth, happiness, and connection to her family.
interpretation: This experience demonstrated Chloe’s ability to represent her experiences and feelings through artwork in several meaningful ways. By choosing to draw a circle with a smiley face to represent herself and her family, Chloe used familiar symbols—such as the smiley face and simple shapes—to communicate positive emotions. Her addition of downward lines to her mother’s face to represent long hair showed her ability to incorporate specific details into her artwork to reflect real-life features, demonstrating an awareness of how to represent people visually. Furthermore, her choice to place her family members next to one another, along with her description of them being "happy together," revealed how Chloe used her drawings to express emotional connections and a sense of togetherness. These revealed her growing ability to use art as a tool to communicate personal experiences, feelings, and relationships.

learning_goals.title: Represent experiences and feelings (e.g: personal event, field trip) through artworks.

title: Family Hop
description: Inspired by the traditional hopscotch, the hopscotch rectangles were labeled with family-related words such as “Mother,” “Father,” “Brother,” “Sister,” “Grandmother,” “Grandfather,” “Uncle” and “Aunt”. Instead of numbers, the children were encouraged to hop through these family titles, saying the words aloud as they landed on each rectangle. Looking at the first rectangle, Dylan stopped for a few seconds before looking up at the teacher. The teacher then proceeded to sound out the different letters and prompted Dylan to blend the sounds together. “Grandfather!” Dylan exclaimed before jumping onto the blue rectangle with the word ‘Grandfather’. Looking at the word on the next rectangle, Dylan paused for a few seconds before saying “Mother!” and jumping into the rectangle. Jumping onto the next few rectangles, Dylan shouted “Grandmother, father, sister.” Stopping in front of the green rectangle, Dylan looked up at the teacher and received the clue “You have 2 of these in your family. Sound out the first letter.” Dylan said “Brr, brother!” and jumped onto the rectangle.
interpretation: Through this experience, Dylan demonstrated his growing understanding of the concept of print. His ability to sound out letters and blend them into words, such as when he identified "Brother" from the clue, demonstrated his understanding of letter-sound correspondence. Dylan was able to recognize and read family-related words like "Father," "Mother," and "Sister," showing that he understands how print corresponds to meaning. Additionally, by identifying the first letter of the word ‘Brother’ as ‘b’, it demonstrated his knowledge of print from left-to-right manner, mirroring the way we read text.

learning_goals.title: Print Awareness: Show some understanding of concepts about print.

title: Numicon Feel and Math
description: In this activity, children were given a variety of textured items, including fabric swatches, bubble wrap, envelopes, plastic bags, and paper bags, placed within a sensory bin. The children were encouraged to explore the materials freely, taking time to feel and engage with each texture. After familiarizing themselves with the items, they were tasked with sorting the materials into groups based on shared characteristics. River engaged actively with the materials during the exploration phase. When she picked up a Dunkin' Donut box, she smiled and said, "Donuts?" before correctly identifying the material as "Cardboard" when asked. After her friends had their turns, River selected a piece of bubble wrap. She began pinching the bubbles and commented, "This is plastic," before walking over to the plastic pile and adding it to the group of plastic items. When recapping her sorting process, River explained that she knew the items in the plastic pile were made of plastic because they were smooth and made a unique sound when touched.
interpretation: River demonstrated her ability to sort objects by simple features, such as texture and material, during the activity. She began by exploring the materials through touch and observation, accurately identifying the Dunkin' Donut box as "Cardboard" based on its texture. When she picked up the bubble wrap, she used both tactile and auditory cues to identify it as "plastic," noting its smooth texture and the distinct sound it made when squeezed. River then sorted the bubble wrap with the other plastic items, showing her ability to categorize based on material. When explaining her process, she connected the texture and sound to the material, clearly demonstrating her understanding of how to sort objects by their features.

learning_goals.title: Sort objects by simple features (e.g: texture or material)

title: Family Adventures on the Map
description: The children recalled a memorable family trip—either a vacation overseas or a special outing within Singapore. They then created a simple drawing that reflected the sights, activities, or moments they remember from that experience. When questioned, Railynn thought for a moment before answering "Japan. I see the volcano. Mount Fuji. I stay in this house with my family. I like because it is cold." With encouragement, Railynn took the pencil and first drew zigzag lines on the bottom of her paper before adding circles and semicircles to create flowers. She then drew a house in the middle of the paper before adding a mountain beside the house.
interpretation: Through this experience, Railynn reflected her ability to make simple recordings of observations through drawing. After recalling her family trip to Japan, she was able to identify and describe key aspects of her experience, such as the volcano - Mount Fuji, staying in a house with her family, and enjoying the cold weather. When Railynn drew her picture, she captured the essence of her memories and observations through her drawings. The circles and semicircles could symbolize the flowers she saw during her trip. The house and mountain likely represent the key places she experienced, such as the place she stayed and the iconic Mount Fuji.

title: “Love You Forever” Story Leaves
description: The children recapped the story Love You Forever by Robert Munsch. They referred to the storybook as a guide to discuss key elements of the narrative. Afterward, the children worked in pairs to select scenes, characters, or symbols from the story to illustrate using markers. Elish and her partner engaged in a conversation as they decided on what to draw. Elish's partner asked, "What do you want to draw?" and Elish thoughtfully responded, "The grandma die." As they negotiated which character each would illustrate, Elish stated, "I draw the grandma then you draw the papa." Elish then began her drawing, first creating a circle with two dashes inside. When asked what she had drawn, she replied, "Eyes closed." Curious about her reasoning, the teacher asked, "Why are the grandma’s eyes closed? Was she sleeping or did she have no eyes?" Elish shook her head and, when asked if the closed eyes signified the grandma's passing, she nodded in affirmation.
interpretation: This experience revealed Elish’s ability to represent ideas and stories through pictures and dictation. Through her drawing, Elish symbolized a significant event from the story Love You Forever—the death of the grandma—by illustrating a circle with two dashes for eyes. This showed that she understood the symbolic meaning of "eyes closed" in the context of the story. Elish also demonstrated her communication skills when she explained to her partner that she wanted to draw "the grandma die" and later clarified to the teacher that the closed eyes meant the grandma had passed away.

learning_goals.title: Represent ideas and stories through pictures, dictation, writing and play.

title: Classroom Treasure Groups
description: The children participated in a creative "hunt" around the classroom, searching for related items such as writing tools, toys, and art supplies. Once they had gathered their finds, they organized the objects into groups based on their similarities. Afterward, the children planned their splatter painting by assigning a specific colour to each group. For example, red splatters represented art supplies, while blue symbolized toys. With their plans in place, the children moved to the shower area to engage in the splatter paint activity. Nikolai first took the paintbrush dipped in blue paint and moved slightly away from the paper. Aiming at the paper, he threw the paintbrush onto it, creating a big blob of blue in the top left corner. Then, holding onto the paintbrush, he flicked his wrist to create a dotted line from one side of the paper to the other. He marveled at the result, laughing and saying, "woah."
interpretation: This experience highlighted Nikolai's experimentation with a variety of techniques, especially in his approach to splatter painting. He began by using the paintbrush to throw blue paint onto the paper from a distance, creating a big blob in the top left corner. This technique allowed him to experiment with a more spontaneous, larger application of paint. Then, Nikolai explored a different technique by holding the paintbrush and flicking his wrist, which produced a dotted line across the paper. His excitement and reaction, saying "woah," showed his sense of discovery as he observed the results of his actions. By combining both throwing and flicking techniques, Nikolai was able to explore different ways of applying paint, demonstrating his willingness to experiment and engage with the creative process in a variety of ways.
