title: My Body Leaf Craft
description:
Diane noticed the craft materials on the table and was immediately drawn to them. Without waiting for an invitation, she took a seat and began touching and feeling the leaves, running her fingers over their textures before picking some up. She turned to the teacher and said, “I want, I want,” as she eagerly selected materials to begin her artwork.

Placing her hands on the adhesive sheet, Diane observed how the surface stuck to her palms each time she touched it. She tapped on the sheet repeatedly, watching as her hands momentarily adhered to the sticky surface before pulling away. She then started pressing leaves, twigs, and branches onto the sheet, carefully arranging them to create her craft. As she explored the materials, she reached into a bag filled with additional natural items, taking over the bag and looking for more twigs and branches to add to her artwork.

While working, Diane noticed that some of her leaves were falling off the sheet. She pointed to them and said, “It is dropping.” Seeing a friend using tape to secure their leaves, she immediately asked, “I want, I want,” before taking a piece of tape. Holding it with both hands, she carefully pressed it down onto the leaves and adhesive sheet, ensuring they remained in place. At the end of the activity, Diane looked at her finished piece and said, “All done.”
interpretation: Diane demonstrated curiosity and engagement in the craft-making process. She explored different materials through touch and observation, adjusting her approach when she noticed that some of the elements were not sticking properly. She demonstrated a keen interest in the sensory aspect of the craft, actively feeling and observing how materials adhered to the sticky sheet. Her persistence in securing the elements of her artwork reflects her developing independence and ability to make adjustments based on what she observed.

title: Emotion Sorting Garden
description:
Mason was tasked to create his own flower as part of the class "Emotion Sorting Garden". 

"Mason, which colour would you like to use to create your flower?" asked the teacher. "I want choose yellow." replied Mason. "Why did you choose yellow?" asked the teacher. "I like yellow." said Mason. "How does yellow make you feel?" replied the teacher. "Happy." said Mason. "Alright Mason, can you think of a time you felt happy?" asked the teacher. "I feel happy when my papa play basketball with me." replied Mason. "Thank you, Mason. Let's start making your flower now." said the teacher. 

Mason made his own own flower by drawing out one of his hands with a pencil on the yellow coloured paper before the teacher helped him to cut it out for him. He attached his yellow flower to the yellow straw by taping it down with a scotch tape.
interpretation: Mason was able to observe and talk about how the colour 'yellow' made him feel, and he was able to relate it to the happy emotion. Furthermore, he was able to share how this colour would relate to his own personal happy experience.

Her use of the cookie cutter reflected her openness to new tools and further exploration, while her reaction to the dough sticking to her finger showed both enjoyment and curiosity about textures. Overall, Aletheia’s participation aligned with the learning objective by fostering her curiosity and hands-on discovery.

title: Slotting Shapes
description:
Jayden was provided with a box featuring three flat holes, each corresponding to a circle, equilateral triangle, and square cut-out. He was encouraged to explore and slot the shapes into the holes. 

Jayden began by picking up a yellow square cut-out with a pincer grasp in his right hand, while using his left hand to support the square and keep it steady for insertion. He lowered his body and eye level to align with the hole, carefully pushing the cut-out through the slot with focused intent.

As he gained confidence, he attempted to hold cut-outs in both hands, trying to slot them in simultaneously. When he successfully inserted part of a shape, he used his fingers or thumbs to gently push the remaining portion through, verbalising his action by saying "go in!".

When the box moved during his attempts, Jayden adapted his strategy—he began holding onto the top of the box with one hand to stabilise it while using his other hand to push the cut-out through, demonstrating problem-solving skills as he adjusted his approach.
interpretation:
Jayden’s engagement in this activity highlights his developing fine motor skills. His pincer grasp to pick up the cut-out shows increasing finger strength and precision, while stabilising the shape with his other hand demonstrates improved hand coordination.

His ability to align the shape with the slot and push it through indicates growing hand-eye coordination. Using his fingers or thumbs to guide the shape further illustrates fine motor refinement.

When the box moved, Jayden adjusted his grip to stabilise it, reflecting an awareness of force, control, and bilateral coordination. Overall, his sustained focus and independent exploration show his progress in grasp control, coordination, and fine motor manipulation.

title: Parking Cars
description:
As part of the transportation theme, Aletheia was invited to participate in the "Parking Cars" activity, where she explored matching red, blue, and yellow toy cars to their corresponding coloured parking lots.
 
Aletheia approached the activity in a structured and systematic manner. She began by selecting a yellow car from the pile, confidently identifying its colour by saying, “yellow” before placing it into the matching yellow parking lot. She then scanned through the remaining cars, searching for a blue one to match with the blue parking lot. Continuing this pattern, she carefully filled up all four parking lots in the row closest to her.

As she moved on to the top row, which was further from her, she noticed that she could not find a red car in the pile. Instead of stopping or seeking help immediately, she removed the red car which she had already parked in the bottom row and placed it in the top red lot. She then turned to the teacher and asked, “no more?” When reassured that more cars were available and given additional ones, she smiled and continued matching them correctly, completing the parking lots with enthusiasm.
interpretation:
Aletheia’s engagement in the "Parking Cars" activity demonstrates her early numeracy development. Her ability to sort cars by colour shows an emerging understanding of classification, a foundational numeracy concept. By verbalising “yellow” as she placed the car, she exhibited colour recognition, contributing to mathematical thinking.


Her decision to find a matching red car and relocate one she had already placed highlights cognitive flexibility and logical reasoning. Her question, “no more?” reflects an understanding of quantity and the concept of "having enough," further supporting early numeracy awareness.


Aletheia’s smile and persistence in matching the cars to their lots demonstrate both her enjoyment of the activity and her ability to focus, reinforcing her developing mathematical skills.

While exploring, Odelia suddenly picked up a firetruck puzzle piece and gave it a push down the ramp. Unlike the cars, the flat puzzle piece moved at a different pace and in a different way. She watched in amazement, noticing the difference in movement. When the teacher prompted her to try releasing both a puzzle piece and a car together for comparison, she broke into a wide smile and eagerly said "yes!", running off to retrieve the items.

This marked the beginning of a deeper exploration, as Odelia became fascinated by testing different objects. She started gathering items from around the classroom, including a ball, toy egg, cup, spoon, and brush, and excitedly pushed them off the ramp one by one, closely observing how each moved differently.
interpretation:
Odelia’s engagement in the ramp activity showed her curiosity and eagerness to experiment with movement and speed. She began by rolling the vehicles manually, then progressed to independently releasing them, demonstrating growing confidence in exploring cause-and-effect relationships.


Her decision to test a puzzle piece, an object without wheels, highlights her ability to notice differences and explore beyond the intended materials. Her excitement to compare objects shows emerging analytical skills and the ability to make predictions.


By testing various classroom objects, Odelia demonstrated strong curiosity and initiative, reflecting the learning objective of fostering exploration and experimentation.

title: Pop The Bubble Dramatisation
description:
During the outdoor walk, Levi showed interest and enjoyment in music and movement as he engaged with the song “Pop the Bubble.” As the music played, he followed the lyrics and actions, demonstrating his understanding of the song’s rhythm and instructions.

When the song prompted “Blow!” Levi opened his mouth wide and exhaled as if blowing bubbles. He held up his fist, pretending it was a bubble, and dramatically “popped” it with his other hand. As the song counted from 1 to 10, Levi focused on his fingers and held up five fingers while saying, “Five.”
interpretation: Levi demonstrated his ability to listen and respond to music through movement and gestures. His use of pretend play, such as imagining a bubble in his hand, participation in counting through finger counting highlighted his engagement in the song and his sustained involvement and enjoyment in music-based activities.

title: Fun With Ramps
description:
As part of our exploration on the theme of “transportation”, Angela was provided with inclined ramps of different heights and encouraged to explore rolling different vehicles of their choice down the ramp. 

Angela first began her exploration by holding a vehicle with both hands, stretching her body forward to manually guide it down the ramp as far as she could before letting go. Upon seeing the car roll down, she laughed and pointed excitedly before running to retrieve it. She repeated this action multiple times, choosing to experiment with different types of vehicles independently.
When the teacher gently asked if she would like to try pushing the car down the ramp instead, Angela nodded and responded, “orh.” After watching a demonstration, she smiled and enthusiastically said, “push!” before attempting to push the car off the ramp with a bit too much force. With guidance, she gradually learned to adjust her strength and give the car a gentle nudge, allowing it to roll smoothly. On her own, she also began to position the car carefully before letting it go, showing an increasing awareness of how the setup affected the movement. Angela showed sustained interest in the activity, repeatedly engaging with the ramps and vehicles throughout.
interpretation:
Angela’s engagement in the ramp activity reflects her curiosity and interest in exploring her environment. She started by manually guiding the vehicle, investigating cause-and-effect relationships. Her excitement to experiment with different vehicles shows a growing motivation to explore.


Her response to teacher prompting—watching the demonstration, adjusting force, and attempting with enthusiasm—demonstrates her willingness to learn and adapt. This reflects her developing problem-solving skills. Her independent attempts to position and release the cars suggest an emerging awareness of spatial relationships.


Angela’s continued engagement and joy in the activity show her deep curiosity and understanding of movement and force, aligning with the learning objective to foster meaningful exploration.

title: Who’s Here Today?
description:
As part of the class attendance activity, children were invited to pick up their own pictures and place them on the class train to indicate their presence in school. When Odelia heard her name being called, she immediately stepped forward and accurately selected her own picture without hesitation. Instead of placing it in the carriage section of the train, she placed it at the head of the train, where the question "Who is here today?" was displayed. She laughed as she stuck it down and pointed to it, showing amusement at her unique placement.

After completing this, Odelia picked up a friend's picture and accurately identified the child before handing it to him, demonstrating her recognition of her peers.
interpretation: Odelia’s ability to recognise and retrieve her own picture upon hearing her name highlights her growing sense of self-awareness. Her confident response indicates that she is developing an understanding of her own identity within the class community. By choosing to place her picture at the head of the train, she displayed initiative and a sense of playfulness, demonstrating that she is comfortable exploring different ways to engage with the activity. Additionally, her decision to pick up a peer’s picture and accurately pass it to him showcases her awareness of others. This suggests that she is not only able to match names to faces but is also developing a sense of social connection with her classmates. Odelia’s engagement in this activity highlights her developing ability to respond to her name and identify others, both of which contribute to her growing sense of self and sense of others.

title: Bull's Eye
description:
The teacher set up targets for the children to aim and hit with the balls prepared for them to throw at. Children were shown how to throw the ball with teacher's demonstration.

When it was Mason's turn, Mason picked up a yellow ball from the red bucket with his right hand. "Mason, which target would you like to hit?" asked the teacher. "I want hit the duck." replied Mason. "Alright, you may start now." said the teacher. 

Mason lifted his right arm up high with the yellow ball behind his ear, looked at the duck target in front of him, and he moved his arm in a forward direction while releasing the ball. The yellow dropped in front of him, and he picked it up again to throw it again. The yellow ball hit the side of the cubby shelf. Mason picked up a red ball from the red bucket with his right hand. He raised his right arm up high with the red ball behind his ear, aimed at the duck, and he swung his right arm downwards while releasing the red ball, and the red ball went in the left direction of the duck that he wanted to hit. Mason tried again while picking up another yellow ball in the red bucket, and he managed to hit the target.
interpretation: Mason was able to coordinate movements perform the throwing task. He was also able to throw a ball in the right direction, aiming at a target with reasonable accuracy.

learning_goals.title: Coordinate movements to perform simple tasks.

title: Passing The Bus-shaped Pillow To My Friend
description:
During a group activity, children were invited to pick an item and pass it to a friend, encouraging them to recognise and associate names with their peers.

When called upon to share the toy bus, Angela smiled and ran up to hug the bus pillow. When asked who she would like to share it with, she initially approached a friend who was not ready to accept it. The teacher then suggested that since her Friend O was not ready to accept it yet, would she like to try sharing it with Friend J? Angela accurately identified her and made her way towards Friend J, but held onto the toy instead of passing it over. When prompted to pass it over, she firmly said, “no!” The teacher then suggested Friend A, and Angela walked towards her, correctly recognising her before once again saying, “no.” After looking around for a moment, Angela pointed to a teacher instead. When asked if she would like to share the toy bus with the teacher, she smiled and nodded before handing it over. She then turned back and smiled at another teacher, appearing pleased with her choice.
interpretation:
Angela’s enthusiasm in running up to hug the toy bus demonstrates her excitement and eagerness to engage in the activity. Her initial attempt to share the toy, despite her friend not being ready to accept it, reflects her growing willingness to interact. When the teacher offered suggestions, Angela accurately identified each named peer, demonstrating her ability to associate names with individuals. However, she also displayed a strong sense of autonomy, making independent decisions about whom she wished to share with. By ultimately choosing a teacher instead of a peer, Angela asserted her preferences while still engaging in the act of sharing. Her smile upon handing over the bus suggests she felt satisfied with her decision, reinforcing her confidence in social interactions.Angela’s response to her name being called shows her developing sense of self, as she smiled and eagerly ran to hug the bus pillow when her name was called. This demonstrates her ability to recognise her own name, an important step in fostering a sense of self.


In terms of fostering a sense of others, Angela showed her awareness of her peers by correctly identifying Friend J and Friend A when prompted. Although she hesitated to share the toy with them, her ability to recognise and approach her peers demonstrates her understanding of others’ names and identities. Her final decision to share the toy with the teacher further highlights her growing social awareness and ability to engage with others. This progression reflects her development in both recognising herself and others in a social context.

title: Let's Leap!
description:
Hwee Jeanne participated in a movement activity. She practised how to leap over the obstacles (e.g. Cones, rope) in front of her before she was asked to leap over multiple obstacles.

Hwee Jeanne began running towards the first obstacle, and when she was near the obstacle, she lifted up both her arms and her left leg up high, and placed her them across the obstacle before lifting her right leg over the obstacle. Hwee Jeanne did the same movement for the second obstacle. While she was at the third obstacle, she lifted up her right leg up high to crossover first before her lifting her left leg over the obstacle. Hwee Jeanne completed the last obstacle by lifting her left leg over first before the lifting her right leg over the obstacle.
interpretation: Hwee Jeanne was able to move with balance and control when she was leaping over the obstacles with her legs. Furthermore, she was also able to complete the obstacle course by moving around the space on narrow paths without bumping into things.

learning_goals.title: Move with balance and control.

title: 小怪兽盲盒
description:
老师邀请幼儿们一起探索小怪兽盲盒活动。老师出示准备好的怪兽盲盒，鼓励幼儿们通过小手触摸，探索感知物品的软硬和认识不同材质。
老师出示小怪兽盲盒，询问紫萱：“你看到什么？”紫萱低头看向怪兽盲盒，手指盲盒上的眼睛。老师询问她：“你看到怪兽的眼睛呀！”紫萱点点头。老师鼓励紫萱说：“眼睛。”紫萱很快复述说出：“眼睛。”老师表扬她：“真棒！”她低头发现了怪兽绿色湿巾缠住的大嘴巴。老师鼓励她：“你把手伸进去，看看你能摸到什么？”紫萱低头把手伸进去摸了起来，拿出来了一只小黄鸭。老师询问她：“你摸到了什么？”她伸长胳膊把手里的小黄鸭拿给老师看。老师鼓励她说：“鸭子，黄色的鸭子。”紫萱尝试说：“鸭子，嘎嘎。”老师表扬她：“真厉害！还能模仿鸭子的叫声。”她低头又尝试把手伸进小怪兽的嘴巴里，不一会儿她摸到了一个紫色的毛球。老师询问紫萱：“这是什么？”紫萱看向手里的毛球，又看向老师。老师鼓励紫萱：“这是毛球，紫色的毛球。”紫萱尝试说出：“球和紫色”。老师表扬她：“真棒！”老师询问：“紫萱你捏一捏紫色的毛球，它是软的还是硬的。”紫萱听懂老师说的问题，小手五指抓握用力捏住毛球。老师表扬她：“很棒，毛球是软软的捏起来可以变小。”紫萱低头观察手里的毛球，又捏了捏。
interpretation: 紫萱可以积极参与小怪兽盲盒活动并可以听懂老师的话语，尝试使用动作和语言表达自己的想法。她能够在与老师的互动中，认识自己的名字了解软和硬不同的材质。

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of self (responding to their names) 培养自我意识，如：回应自己的名字等。

title: My Favourite Food Now
description:
The children had an exciting hands-on experience crafting their favorite foods using air-dry clay. This activity encouraged creativity, sensory exploration, and fine motor skill development while allowing the young artists to express their personal preferences in food.
To add vibrant colors to their creations, the children used polymer clay to blend and infuse rich hues into the white air-dry clay.
This activity not only fostered artistic expression but also reinforced sensory and motor skills through hands-on manipulation. It was a wonderful experience for the children, sparking joy and creativity while deepening their appreciation for the art of clay modeling.

learning_goals.title: Talk about their own artworks (e.g: what the artwork is about and the lines, colours and shapes used).

title: Walking Through The Jungle!
description:
Maeve was encouraged to walk through a pathway in the jungle. Maeve placed her right foot on the chair. Then, she placed her left foot onto the chair after shifting her weight to her right leg. After gaining balance, Maeve alternated her legs to walk across the chairs. 

Maeve wobbled a little but regained her equilibrium with her hands stretched. As she reached the last chair, she turned her body orientation to the right. Maeve bent her knees, jumped from the chair and landed with them bent. She was delighted and decided to walk through the pathway again.
interpretation: Maeve fostered gross motor development by walking on an elevated platform (the chairs) with no support. She developed a sense of balance by jumping from the chair and maintained her balance when she landed on the floor.

Develop a sense of balance (walk along a non-linear pathway/line/balance beam with little or no support, jump from a low platform and maintain balance) 发展平衡感，如：锻炼手部、腿部肌肉的力量及协调运动能力。

title: Let's Take Turns!
description:
Caden and his friend were practicing how to step on the pedal to open the bin. They each took a ball and stood in front of the bin. Caden realizing that his friend did not know how to step on the pedal, offered to help by stepping on the pedal. The bin opened, and Caden waited for his friend to put the ball in, "Ava go first!" before he placed his orange ball into the bin. 

Again, Caden and his friend took a yellow ball each and made their way to the front of the bin. Caden waited for his turn and said, "I wait for Ava!" When his friend thanked him, Caden gave a smile and responded, "You're welcome!"
interpretation: Caden fostered a sense of sharing and respecting rights of others by displaying turn-taking. He was empathic towards others, recognizing there are others other than himself. He recognized that fostering a positive relationship with others begins with pro-social behaviours. Hence, he communicated using approriate social skills to help his friend to open the dustbin.

learning_goals.title: Foster interactions, attachment and relationships with adults and children 通过与成人和同伴的互动，建立良好的关系。

title: 颜色找朋友
description:
教师向幼儿介绍蓝色和红色的呼啦圈，班级里面红色和蓝色的物品，邀请幼儿进行颜色分类的活动，将红色的物品放进红色的呼啦圈里面，将蓝色的物品放进蓝色的呼啦圈里面。
        教师向立仁示范如何进行活动，教师拿起一个红色的物品放进红色的呼啦圈里面，又拿起一个蓝色的物品放进蓝色的呼啦圈里面。立仁开始做活动，他拿起一个红色的番茄，将红色的番茄放在红色的呼啦圈里面，教师指向呼啦圈里的番茄问立仁：“立仁番茄是什么颜色的呀？”立仁回答教师：“蓝色。”教师纠正立仁说道：“这是红色的。”立仁复述教师的话“红色。”然后立仁又拿了一个蓝色的碗放在蓝色的呼啦圈里，教师继续问立仁同样的问题，立仁回答教师：“蓝色。”教师对立仁竖起大拇指。
interpretation:
诠释：

      在进行活动的过程中立仁能够按照颜色进行分类，找到红色和蓝色的物品，将其放在对应的呼啦圈里面。立仁也能够用简单的词汇与教师进行沟通。

title: 观察牙齿
description:
幼儿在参与“好奇乐”领域的《观察牙齿》的教学活动中，教师为幼儿准备“大镜子”。请幼儿认识了解自己的牙齿，使用镜子来为自己的检查牙齿，看是否有蛀牙。
思彤小朋友坐在桌前，面前摆着一面小镜子。她睁大眼睛，张开嘴巴，好奇地观察自己的牙齿。她用小手指了指自己的嘴巴，仔细地看着镜子里的倒影。桌上还有一个牙齿模型，是用来辅助认识牙齿结构的。老师问;’思彤，你的牙齿是什么颜色的呢？“思彤笑着说：”是白色的！“ “你的牙齿有什么特别的地方吗？”老师又问。思彤张大嘴巴认真看了起来，接着说：“好多哦！有的小小的，有的大大的！” 老师回答她：对呀，我们的牙齿有不同的形状哦！那你平时怎么保护你的牙齿呢？” 思彤回答说：”要刷牙！早上刷，晚上也要刷！"老师夸她说：“你太棒了！”思彤开心地点点头：“我要每天刷牙，牙齿就会白白的！没有蛀牙。”
interpretation: 这个过程中，思彤通过观察镜子中的自己，对牙齿有了更深的认识,展现她对牙齿奥秘的好奇心和兴趣，能利用感官和简单的工具“大镜子”进行探索。并且通过对话学习了牙齿的保护知识。

title: 观察牙齿
description:
幼儿在参与“好奇乐”领域的《观察牙齿》的教学活动中，教师为幼儿准备“大镜子”。请幼儿认识了解自己的牙齿，使用镜子来为自己的检查牙齿，看是否有蛀牙。
Diyansh 坐在桌前，拿着镜子观察自己的牙齿。他告诉老师：“我的牙齿好多！我可以看到。”老师说: “太棒了！你仔细看看，你的牙齿都一样吗？”Diyansh: “不是的！牙齿小小的，牙齿大大的！” Diyansh很认真照镜子说：’我的牙齿是白色的，我每天要刷牙。”他拿起牙刷，开始在牙齿模型上练习刷牙，上面刷、下面刷。
interpretation: 这个过程中，Diyansh通过观察镜子中的自己，对牙齿有了更深的认识,展现他对牙齿奥秘的好奇心和兴趣，能利用感官和简单的工具“大镜子”进行探索。并且通过对话学习了牙齿的保护知识。

description:

彦丰小朋友坐在桌前，面前摆放着一面小镜子。他好奇地盯着镜子里的自己，小心翼翼地张开嘴巴，露出一排整齐的小牙齿。他缓缓地靠近镜子，仔细地观察自己的牙齿形状和颜色。老师问他：“彦丰，你看到牙齿是什么怎样的呢？‘他回答说：“老师，是小小的，白白的。”接着，彦丰用小手指轻轻地触摸自己的门牙，尝试着数一数牙齿的数量。他时不时地调整角度，让自己看得更清楚。他看到旁边的牙齿模型，彦丰歪着头，思考着自己的牙齿和模型里的有什么不同。他睁大眼睛，嘴巴张得更大，观察了好一会儿。
interpretation: 这个过程中，彦丰通过观察镜子中的自己，对牙齿有了更深的认识,展现他对牙齿奥秘的好奇心和兴趣，能利用感官和简单的工具“大镜子”进行探索。并且通过对话学习了牙齿的保护知识。

title: Replicating sounds of nature in the classroom
description:
Using materials in the classroom, the children had to recreate sounds that they hear in nature. Using books, stationery and other materials found in the classroom, the children had the opportunity to be creative to recreate sounds like rain and walking. 

Talia went to the music corner and explored a few instruments by playing them. She played with the wooden percussion sticks and brought them to the group. As the children were seated in a circle, Talia waited until it was her turn, before she played the instruments. Knocking the instruments together, she created sounds. When she was done, she looked at her friends and said, "Guess what kind of nature sounds I made?". Her friends guessed and made a few suggestions, "Rain sounds! Walking sounds? Sounds of shoes?". Talia smiled a small smile and said, "Ching Ruth is right. I am making the sound of shoes walking at the courtyard!".
interpretation:
Talia displays an ability to identify and create a sound that she hears from the external environment such as at the courtyard. She creates music using musical instruments from the classroom and was able to articulate her thoughts and ideas clearly.


Social and Emotional Competencies:

  1. Develop self-awareness
  2. Build Relationships with Family, Friends and Significant Adults

title: Match and Celebrate Pairs
description: During a numeracy pairing activity, the teacher provided a variety of items for the children to find and pair things that would work well together. Asher first picked out a whiteboard duster and then looked over the items. The teacher went on to ask him, "What can you use together with this whiteboard eraser?". Asher then reached out to pick a whiteboard marker. The teacher then prompted him to show everyone how he would use the items. Asher proceeded to use the marker to draw on the whiteboard then using the duster to erase his drawing. When encouraged to explain what he did, Asher then shared "I use the marker to draw on the whiteboard then I can use the eraser to erase."
interpretation: Asher's selection of the whiteboard earser and marker showcases shows his ability to recognize objects that are commonly used together, demonstrating an understanding of practical, real-world pairings. His live demonstration of how his items worked together also solidified his understanding of how the two items complement each other in function. Asher’s explanation of his actions displaye how he was able to  think in a logical sequence — drawing first, erasing second. This demonstrates an understanding of cause and effect, an important component of early numeracy and cognitive development.

learning_goals.title: Pair related objects (e.g: a cup to a saucer, a fork to a spoon)

title: Identifying themselves and their friends.
description: To help the children get to know each other more, the teacher prepared a fun activity. She showed everyone’s photo and encouraged the kids to point to their friends’ pictures as she called out their names. When it was Elroy's turn, he immediately picked his own photo and proudly said, "Elroy," while pointing to himself. As the teacher named his peers, Elroy confidently chose the correct photos and even called out their names. He received a high five for his effort, and he beamed with a sweet smile in response.
interpretation:
Elroy’s act of pointing to his own photo and confidently saying his name demonstrates emerging self-recognition, showing that he can identify himself. His ability to recognize and call out the names of his peers indicates that he is familiar with them.


Moreover, in class, Elroy not only knows his peers' names but is also aware to their belongings. He consistently greets his peers by name and makes sure to acknowledge them every morning when he arrives at school, reflecting the close relationships he shares with them. Overall, these experiences clearly demonstrate that Elroy is not only enhancing his recognition skills but also developing a strong sense of belonging and connection with his peers.

learning_goals.title: Foster sense of others (identifying others to their names) 培养对他人的认识，如：指认同伴等。

title: Fastening nuts and bolts.
description: To help the children foster their fine motor skills, they were encouraged to explore nuts and bolts by fastening them together and turning the nuts onto the bolts using their hands and fingers. During the activity, Elroy asked help from his teacher to fasten the nut onto the bolt, and once it was secured, he began turning the nut using his palmar grasp. Afterward, he explored further by twisting the nut with his pincer grip. Elroy continued to explore independently, repeatedly twisting and turning the nut using both his hands and fingers.
interpretation:
Elroy using his palmar grasp to turn the nut shows his ability to engage larger hand movements, which are essential in early motor development. As Elroy continued exploring with his pincer grip, he was practising his fine motor skills and improving his ability to manipulate objects. 


Elroy's fine motor skills are also evident in his daily routines at school, such as holding his spoon with a palmar grasp and picking up small objects from the floor using a pincer grasp. Additionally, during sports classes or playtime on the playground, he demonstrates his ability to grasp objects like balls and the steering wheel of a toy car. These actions evidently shows his developing fine motor skills and his increasing curiosity in exploring objects.

title: Rainbow Sort and Choice
description: During learning corner time, Adaline went over to the Math Mind corner and pulled out the tray of materials used in a colour sorting activity. There were coloured plates and a variety of colour items for her to sort on matching coloured plates. Adaline laid out six plates (red, yellow, blue, green, purple and black) and proceeded to carefully sort all the items onto the matching coloured plates. Adaline was able to independently sort all the items available correctly onto the coloured plates with little teacher facilitation. The teacher then commended her for an amazing attempt and she smiled widely in response.
interpretation: Adaline showcaseed her ability to identify colours accurately as she was able to distinguish between six different colours during the activity. Her success in sorting a variety of coloured items onto their corresponding coloured plates demonstrates that she understands and applies the concept of matching objects by one attribute, in this case, colour. Her independence in this activity without guidance from the teacher also indicates her confidence and mastery of the skill. By correctly placing each item on its matching plate, she exhibited the ability to classify and categorize objects based on a shared characteristic. This is a fundamental numeracy skill that helps develop logical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

title: Body Tracing and Collage
description: To expand the children's learning about "My Body," the teacher invited them to lie down on a large sheet of brown paper while she traced their body outlines. Afterward, the children were encouraged to create a collage on their outlines using colourful papers. Once Elroy’s body outline was traced, he began working on his collage by carefully pasting the colourful papers. He slowly covered the entire outline with the papers. When he finished his artwork, Elroy proudly exclaimed, "Elroy," and struck a pose next to his body outline.
interpretation: Elroy demonstrated his interest in art and ability to focus as he independently finished pasting the colourful papers onto his body outline. He also expressed pride and ownership over his collage when he exclaimed "Elroy" and struck a pose next to his artwork. Through this simple art activity, Elroy showcased his artistic skills and confidence in visually expressing himself.

title: Walking and Running
description: To help the children in enhancing their gross motor skills, they were encouraged to pick up a flag and bring it to the teacher's side by either walking or running. Elroy managed to successfully carry the flag to the other side by walking slowly along the path. During his second attempt, he opted to run and was able to cover the distance from one end to the other, independently. The teacher praised him, saying, "You did it!" to which Elroy replied, "I did it!".
interpretation:
Through this activity, Elroy has demonstrated his ability to independently walk and run from one point to another, showing his developing gross motor skills. 


In addition, Elroy also displays his physical abilities during outdoor walks and playground activities at school. He actively walks, runs, climbs, and is also able to kick and throw a ball, further developing his gross motor skills and physical strength.

title: Rainbow Sort and Choice
description: During a sorting activity, children were encouraged to sort a variety of coloured items on to the corresponding coloured plates. Shu Ya chose to sort blue and yellow items. She was able to swiftly pick out the correct coloured items from the mix of other colours such as red and green too. She decided to sort all of the blue items first before choosing all the yellow items. After she finished her task, the teacher pointed to a pale yellow pom pom ball and asked Shu Ya, "Oh is this yellow? It looks different from the other yellow things." Shu Ya then responded, "Yes, it is yellow. It is light yellow."
interpretation: Shu Ya accurately identified and sorted blue and yellow items, even when mixed with other colours like red and green. This shows she can distinguish and match objects based on the attribute of colour. When the teacher pointed out a pale yellow pom-pom, Shu Ya confidently identified it as light yellow, showing a more nuanced understanding of colour shades. This indicates an advanced ability to classify objects within a colour spectrum, which strengthens her categorization skills. Shu Ya’s ability to sort objects accurately by colour, recognize subtle differences in shades, and confidently express her understanding shows she has not only met but exceeded the learning outcome of matching objects by one attribute (colour). This reflects her growing classification and observational abilities, which are foundational for future mathematical learning.

title: Rainbow Sort and Choice
description: During a sorting activity, children were encouraged to sort a variety of coloured items on to the corresponding coloured plates. Sheldon chose to sort the red and green items. He was able to concurrently pick out both red and green items from an array of coloured items and placed them on their respective coloured plates. After he was seemingly done, the teacher asked him to double check the tray. Sheldon gave it a once over to check if he left any red or green items behind and then told the teacher. "No more red and green things already." The teacher then pointed to two green items- the marker and a magnet before commenting, "These two are not the same kind of green." Sheldon then replied, "The marker is light green and the magnet is dark green."
interpretation: Sheldon was able to simultaneously sort red and green items from a mix of other colours, placing them correctly on their respective plates- showcasing a strong ability to distinguish and match objects by colour with efficiency and accuracy. When the teacher highlighted the two different shades of green, Sheldon accurately identified the difference, saying, “The marker is light green and the magnet is dark green.” This shows a more deeper level understanding of colour shades, which goes beyond basic colour matching. Sheldon’s ability to sort items accurately by colour, self-check his work, and distinguish between different shades of the same colour shows he has fully achieved and exceeded the learning outcome of matching objects by one attribute (colour). His attention to detail and ability to idenitfy subtle colour differences enhance his classification and observational skills — all foundational for future mathematical learning.

title: Ribbon Parade
description: During a numeracy activity to explore ordering, the teacher prepared ribbons of different length for the class to explore. Maya was presented with three ribbons and prompted to pick the longest ribbon before arranging it on a black mat using velcro stickers. Maya was then asked to pick the longer ribbon out of the remaining two to place on the black mat. After arranging the three ribbons, Maya was given two more ribbons and tasked to sort the longer one first. During all her attempts, Maya was able to correctly identify the longest/ longer ribbons. Once she was done, the teacher encouraged Maya to identify the longest and shortest ribbon to which she was able to swiftly and accurately do so.
interpretation: Maya's consistent accuracy in identifying the longest and longer ribbons when presented with multiple options, showcases her ability to visually compare lengths and make accurate judgments. When the teacher added two more ribbons, Maya continued to sort them correctly, showing her capability to apply the same ordering logic even as the number of objects increased — which is a crucial step in solidifying the concept of ordering by length. Through this activity, Maya demonstrated a clear understanding of ordering objects by length. Maya's ability to successfully compare and arrange multiple objects, progressing from longest to shortest, while confidently identifying the longest and shortest ribbons out of five presented to her reflect her growing skills in more advanced numeracy concepts, such as measurement, patterning, and sequencing.

learning_goals.title: Put three or more things in an order according to size (e.g: small to big), length (e.g: short to long), or height (e.g: short to tall).

title: Storytelling: Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love
description: Christopher and his classmates listened to the story Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love read by the teacher. Throughout the reading, they were encouraged to ask questions and share their thoughts about the story. When Christopher heard the word "Abuela," he asked, "What's Abuela?" The teacher pointed to the picture of the grandmother in the book and explained that "Abuela" means grandmother in Spanish. After the story, the teacher encouraged the children to talk to each other and recap the story. Christopher began by saying, "I hear the word Abuela," and his friend responded with a question, "What's Abuela?" Christopher then flipped the book to the page with the grandmother and answered, "There," pointing to the picture. A friend pointed to the piñata in the book and shared an experience he had at a birthday party, where candies poured out of the piñata after they hit it. Christopher then added on and shared, "Oh, Caleb's party also have piñata. A lot a lot of candies drop out."
interpretation: This experience demonstrated how Christopher asked questions and sought answers by gathering information from different sources. When Christopher heard the word "Abuela," he asked, "What's Abuela?" seeking to understand the unfamiliar term. The teacher pointed to the picture of the grandmother in the book and explained that "Abuela" means grandmother in Spanish, providing an answer through the book’s illustrations and the teacher’s explanation. After the story, Christopher continued to seek understanding by sharing what he learned with his classmates. When a friend mentioned the piñata in the book and shared his personal experience, Christopher added his own experience, saying, "Oh, Caleb’s party also has a piñata. A lot a lot of candies drop out." By recalling a similar event from his own life, Christopher gathered information from his peer’s experience and used it to expand the conversation. This exchange showed how Christopher actively sought answers from a variety of sources.

learning_goals.title: Ask questions and seek answers by gathering infomration from different resources

title: Storytelling: Pablo's Tree
description: Darian and his classmates listened to the story Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love read by the teacher. Throughout the reading, they were encouraged to ask questions and share their thoughts about the story. The teacher shared about the tree and asked, "Who planted the tree there?" A friend answered, "Abuelito (grandfather) planted the tree." The teacher continued to share that "Abuelito" means grandfather in Spanish. When Darian saw the tree in Pablo’s Tree decorated with many colorful decorations, he asked, “Why did the grandpa put up the Christmas tree?" The teacher encouraged the children to talk to each other to find answers. One of Darian’s friends responded, "Because it’s the mother’s son’s (Pablo’s) birthday."
interpretation: This experience demonstrated how Darian asked questions and sought answers by gathering information from different sources. Darian learned that "Abuelito" means grandfather in Spanish when the teacher explained it after a classmate mentioned "Abuelito" in response to the question about who planted the tree. This allowed Darian to gather information from the teacher’s explanation and his peer’s understanding of the story. Through the illustrations in the book, Darian noticed the tree decorated with many colorful ornaments. From this, he inferred that the tree was likely a Christmas tree and asked, “Why did the grandpa put up the Christmas tree?” When Darian’s friend responded, "Because it’s the mother’s son’s (Pablo’s) birthday," Darian gathered more information from his friend’s perspective. By combining information from the book, the teacher’s explanation, and his classmates' insights, Darian was able to deepen his understanding of the story, demonstrating his ability to ask questions and gather answers from multiple sources.

learning_goals.title: Ask questions and seek answers by gathering infomration from different resources

title: Storytelling: Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love
description: Damien and his classmates listened to the story Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love read by the teacher. Throughout the reading, they were encouraged to ask questions and share their thoughts about the story. Damien and his classmates listened to the story Pablo’s Tree and With Lots of Love read by the teacher. During the reading, they were encouraged to ask questions and share their thoughts about the story. When Damien heard the word "Abuela," he smiled, looked at a friend, and repeated the word to him. Another friend then asked, “Why the words we cannot understand?” The teacher explained that these words were in Spanish. Damien, curious about the term, asked, “What’s Abuela?” The teacher responded that "Abuela" means grandmother in Spanish. After the reading, the teacher encouraged the children to recap the story. Damien shared, “The girl has a new house.” Another friend added, “Rocio had a new house and then she missed her grandfather.” The teacher asked whether it was the grandfather or the grandmother, and the friend insisted it was the grandfather. The teacher encouraged the children to look at the illustrations in the book to find the answer. As Damien and his friend looked through the illustrations, Damien pointed to the pictures and said, “No, grandmother.”
interpretation: This experience demonstrated Damien's ability to ask questions and seek answers by gathering information from various sources. When he didn’t understand the word "Abuela," he asked the teacher for clarification, receiving an explanation that "Abuela" means grandmother in Spanish. Later, during the story recap, Damien used the illustrations in the book to clarify whether the character missed her grandfather or grandmother, pointing out that it was the grandmother. While his friend contributed to the conversation about the character, Damien did not rely on peers for direct answers, but instead used their input as part of his process of discovery. This showed how Damien gathered information from his peers, the teacher, and the book’s illustrations to deepen his understanding of the story.

learning_goals.title: Ask questions and seek answers by gathering infomration from different resources

title: 三月份第二周：探索新触摸墙 （Update）
description: 老师抱着筠心来到新更换的触摸墙前，筠心兴奋地探索新事物。她拿起小槌子，这里敲敲，那里拍拍，玩得不亦乐乎。老师还放上自制的纸盒和响板，鼓励筠心用手触摸或敲击，感受不同的声音和触感。筠心专注地观察、聆听、探索，在游戏中享受发现的乐趣。

title: Family Hop
description: Inspired by traditional hopscotch, the hopscotch squares were labeled with family-related words such as "Mother," "Father," "Brother," "Sister," and more. As the children hopped through these family titles, they called out the words as they landed on each square. Shanice eagerly joined the game, starting by hopping on one foot. She laughed with excitement as she went through all the squares, wobbling slightly as she balanced on one foot. Even though she wobbled, Shanice kept hopping through the squares with determination, her laughter growing louder the more she wobbled. Even though these words were new and challenging for her, she was still eager to go again. By the time she reached the last square, she was filled with joy and asked eagerly if she could try again.
interpretation: This experience revealed Shanice’s willingness to try out something new and different in several ways. Despite the hopscotch game involving unfamiliar family-related words, instead of hesitating, she embraced it with enthusiasm. title: Ribbon Parade
description: During a numeracy activity focused on ordering by length, the teacher provided ribbons of various lengths for the children to explore. Jaylin was given three ribbons and asked to select the longest one to place on a black mat using velcro stickers. Next, she was prompted to choose the longer ribbon from the remaining two and arrange it on the mat. After successfully ordering the three ribbons, Jaylin received two additional ribbons from the teacher and was tasked with identifying and placing the longer one first. Throughout the activity, Jaylin consistently identified the longest and longer ribbons accurately. The teacher then asked her to point out the longest and shortest ribbons, Jaylin did so quickly and correctly. When asked if the ribbons she had arranged from the top to bottom were becoming longer or shorter, Jaylin answered, "They are getting shorter."
interpretation: Jaylin was able to consistently identify and select the longest and longer ribbons when comparing multiple options, showing her ability to visually assess and compare object lengths. Jaylin's careful arrangement of the ribbons step by step — placing the longest ribbon first, followed by the longer one, and continuing the sequence as more ribbons were added showcases her understanding of relative length and her growing ability to create an ordered sequence. Her response to the teacher's question also reflects her understanding of the overall pattern she created, which reinforces her ability to describe sequences. Through this activity, Jaylin demonstrated her capability to compare and sequence objects by length which will support her future learning in numeracy concepts such as measurement, ordering, and pattern recognition.

title: Building A Tower City
description: During a numeracy activity to explore ordering by height, the children were provided with stackable Jenga stones to build two towers of different heights first. The teacher prompted the children to build a tall tower first before the short one. Jing Wei was able to build two Jenga stones of differing heights and could identify which one was tall and which one was short. He then expressed to the teacher he wanted to build another tower, the 'middle tower' as he described. Jing Wei was able to build a third tower that was of a 'middle' height when placed in comparison to his first two tower. When prompted to count the number of stones he used to build his towers, Jing Wei was also able to count them for each of his tower accurately too.
interpretation: Jing Wei's capability to accurately built two towers of differing heights and correctly identified which was tall and which was short, demonstrates his ability to compare and differentiate objects by height. After building the tall and short towers, he independently decided to build a third "middle tower," showing that he understood the concept of a height continuum and could extend the sequence to include a third height. By intentionally building a medium-height tower and positioning it between the other two, Jing Wei displayed a deeper grasp of relative height relationships beyond just recognizing extremes. Through this activity, Jing Wei showcased his ability to compare and order objects by height while expanding the sequence to include a third, intermediate value. His growing skills would help build a strong foundation for future learning in numeracy concepts like measurement and sequencing.

title: Walking Through The Jungle
description:
Emma was encouraged to walk through a pathway in the jungle. Emma placed her right foot on the chair. Then, she placed her left foot onto the chair after shifting her weight to her right leg. After gaining balance, Emma alternated her legs to walk across the chairs. 

Emma wobbled a little but regained her equilibrium with her hands stretched. As she reached the last chair, she turned her body orientation to the right. Emma bent her knees, jumped from the chair and landed with them bent. She was delighted and decided to walk through the pathway again.
interpretation: Emma fostered gross motor development by walking on an elevated platform (the chairs) with no support. She developed a sense of balance by jumping from the chair and maintained her balance when she landed on the floor.

Develop a sense of balance (walk along a non-linear pathway/line/balance beam with little or no support, jump from a low platform and maintain balance) 发展平衡感，如：锻炼手部、腿部肌肉的力量及协调运动能力。

title: Working Together!
description:
Under the teacher's encouragement, Maeve and her friends thought about how they can work together to transport a pile of foam blocks across the classroom. After listening to the teacher's suggestion of using a blanket, Maeve set out to work by picking up a red foam block near her. She waited for her friends before placing the red foam block onto the blanket. 

After the foam blocks have been placed onto the blanket, Maeve told her friends, "I hold here okay!" She waited for her friends to be ready, before lifting the blanket with the teacher's prompt. Maeve walked slowly to ensure that she was in sync with her friends as they made their way across the classroom. She chanted, "Jiayou! Jiayou!" to encourage her friends. As they reached the finishing point, Maeve beamed and clapped happily.
interpretation: Maeve fostered a sense of belonging in a group by participating in transporting a pile of foam blocks with her friends. During this time, she fostered social skills by exchanging positive interactions with her friends such as smiling, waiting for her turn, and walking slowly. Throughout the experience, she fostered a sense of well-being.

Isaac walked slowly to ensure that he was in sync with his friends as they made their way across the classroom. He chanted, "Jiayou! Jiayou!" to encourage his friends. As they reached the finishing point, Isaac beamed and clapped happily.
interpretation: Isaac fostered a sense of belonging in a group by participating in transporting a pile of foam blocks with his friends. During this time, he fostered social skills by exchanging positive interactions with his friends such as smiling, waiting for his turn, and walking slowly. Throughout the experience, he fostered a sense of well-being.

title: 夹毛绒球

title: 《草莓长大了》
description: 上午活动时间，老师出示《草莓长大了》拼图游戏，鼓励雨芯和朋友轮流操作将大小不一的草莓按照模板的提示摆放在正确的地方。雨芯站在”草莓“模板面前，她右手从地板上捡起”大草莓“回头看着老师：“老师，Look  big one。”老师：“雨芯拿到一颗大大的草莓呀！大草莓放在哪里呢?”雨芯抬高小手指着”大草莓”模板：“Put here!”雨芯右手捏着“大草莓”将它粘贴在正确的模板里。雨芯：“大大  草莓put here。”老师：“哇！雨芯太厉害了，找到大草莓了，接下来呢？”雨芯从地板上捡起“小草莓“图片，直接将小草莓放回正确的模版中。老师：“雨芯刚才贴的是什么呀？”雨芯：“Small one。”老师：“对的，这个是小小的草莓 ，最小的草莓放好了，现在中间还有一个不大不小的草莓在哪里呢？”雨芯低头看看地板，她弯腰从地板上捡起“草莓”举高对着老师：“This one 。”雨芯说完将草莓放回模板中，完成拼图。她笑着看着老师！

description: Abby held a pipe cleaner in one hand and a short straw in the other. She examined the straw and then placed it near the pipe cleaner. The pipe cleaner passed through the straw, and Abby pulled it out from the other end. She continued by picking up another colored straw and repeated the same process.
interpretation:
Abby demonstrated interest and hand-eye coordination as she grasped and manipulated the pipe cleaner and straw. By positioning the straw and guiding the pipe cleaner through it, Abby practiced control and dexterity, key components of fine motor development.


Her repeated actions, such as picking up another colored straw and repeating the process, show her growing ability to focus on tasks and engage in purposeful, repetitive play. This activity also strengthens her pincer grip, finger strength, and coordination between both hands.

title: Let's Talk About My Painting!
description:
Emma was actively engaged in her cling wrap painting when she lifted her paint brush to show her teacher, "See, so many colours!" The teacher marveled at her painting and asked, “Yes, what colour did you use?” Emma looked at the brush and said, “I used blue, green, red.” 

Curious with her painting, the teacher asked what her painting was about. Emma replied, "I paint my leg, see like that!" while adding two strokes in her painting. The teacher commented, "Oh, you mean you painted two lines just like your legs?" Emma laughed and said, "yeah!"

After adding a few more strokes to her painting, the teacher furthered her question and asked, "Now, what is this?" Emma thought for a while and replied, "I drawing rainbow!" "Oh? Now it has become a rainbow?" the teacher asked. Emma replied, "yeah!" and laughed.
interpretation: Emma showed the ability to understand and comprehend the teacher's spoken language and questions. Then, she confidently expressed herself with four-five words in a sentence to communicate her painting to her teacher.

description: Lavinha was invited to climb onto the foam block in the obstacle course. At first, she was hesitant, but with encouragement from her teacher, her confidence grew. She used both hands to support her body weight and placed her right knee onto the platform first. Although she struggled to pull herself up, her teacher provided assistance, and she successfully climbed to the top. Filled with excitement, she raised her hands and cheered, "Hooray!" interpretation: Lavinha's gross motor skills are developing, but she still needs support with strength, coordination, and balance. However, her initial hesitation and struggle to pull herself up suggest that she is still building confidence and muscle control. With encouragement and assistance, she successfully completed the climb, demonstrating perseverance and growing confidence in her physical abilities.

description: Stephen grasped a pipe cleaner in one hand and a short straw in the other. title: 观察动物的牙齿
description:
幼儿正在参与”好奇乐“领域《动物的牙齿》教学活动，教师出示狮子、大象、老虎、猴子、鳄鱼等动物的牙齿图片，鼓励幼儿观察图片并说说他们看到了什么，什么动物的牙齿是尖尖的。
翊枫拿起图片，他用手指着图片对老师说：“我喜欢这个大象。”老师问：“那你看到大象的牙齿是什么样的啊？”翊枫又看了看大象的图片说：“大象的牙齿是长长的。”老师回应：“大象的牙齿是长长的，也是尖尖的。”他笑着复述说：“大象的牙齿是长长的，也是尖尖的。”老师说：“那你在看看其他的动物的牙齿是什么样子的？”他仔细看着其他的动物图片，他把小手指向狮子说：“老师，你看狮子的牙齿也是尖尖的。”老师：“对的！翊枫你真棒！”
interpretation: 在《动物的牙齿》活动中，翊枫能够通过探索观察图片了解动物牙齿的特征，并用自己的语言表达所观察到的结果，展现他对动物牙齿的好奇心和兴趣。

语言学习成果（说）- 交谈：尝试用华语与人交谈。
观察与讨论有生命和无生命的事物：运用多种感官，如：观察、触摸、聆听、实验等探索他们周围的事物。

title: 小蚂蚁搬家
description:
描述：
        教师向幼儿介绍已经搭建好的体能器材，排好的一排椅子，粘贴在地上的呼啦圈以及标志桶。邀请幼儿进行“小蚂蚁搬家”的活动，走过椅子，跳过呼啦圈，最后将标志桶堆叠在一起。
        Isaac走到椅子前，双手把着椅子背的上面，他的左脚踩上椅子，紧接着右脚也跟着踩上了椅子。然后他弯着腰将左脚向前迈出一小步，踩到另一把椅子上，移动双手，把着另一把椅子背的上面，右脚跟了过来，重复这样的动作直至最后一把椅子。Iassc走到最后一把椅子，把手从椅子上松开，从椅子上跳下来，教师对Iassc说：“你好勇敢哦。”他回应教师说：“是的。”他来到呼啦圈前面，双脚跳进呼啦圈里面，拿起标志桶，跳进第二个呼啦圈里面，将标志桶叠放另一个标志桶上，直至跳到最后一个呼啦圈，将所有的标志桶堆叠在一起，他主动对教师说：“张老师，你看我做好了。”教师回应Isaac：“你很有力气哦，将所有的标志桶都堆叠在一起了。”
interpretation:
诠释：

      在体能活动中，Isaac把着椅子背的上面走过椅子，展现出Isaac的抓握动作，以及良好的平衡能力。他也能够跳进呼啦圈里面拿起标志桶，再跳进呼啦圈将标志桶堆叠在一起，展现出他的身体各部位的协调和平衡能力。他能够说出简单的句子与教师进行沟通。

title: Making a class birthday cake
description:
After  listening to the story, “Bunny bakes”, Liam participated in a collaborative art project with his friend where they worked together to paint and decorate a giant birthday cake. This hands-on activity provided an opportunity for them to develop social skills and creativity in a fun and engaging way.
Throughout the process, Liam demonstrated teamwork and cooperation together with his friend as they shared the art supplies- paintbrushes, and paint pots. He practiced patience and turn-taking when using the colors which he wanted, showing his ability to request for the paintbrush which his friend was using. Liam went, “Jordan, may I have the blue please?” After his friend passed him the paintbrush, Liam thanked his friend.
interpretation: It was wonderful to see Liam communicating with his friend to negotiate choices, while expressing his creativity while contributing to a shared masterpiece. Beyond artistic expression, this activity helped to reinforce important developmental skills such as fine motor control, decision-making, and problem-solving. By working towards a common goal, Liam gained a sense of accomplishment and pride in his collective effort together with his friend. This activity not only nurtured his creativity but also strengthened his ability to speak up and collaborate—valuable skills that will continue to benefit him in both social and learning environments.

title: 《草莓长大了》
description: 上午活动时间，老师出示《草莓长大了》拼图游戏，鼓励昊霆和朋友轮流操作将大小不一的草莓按照模板的提示摆放在正确的地方。昊霆站在”草莓“模板面前，他右手从地板上捡起”小草莓“回头看着老师：“Small small one。”老师：“昊霆拿到一颗小小的草莓呀！小草莓放在哪里呢?”昊霆抬高小手指着”小草莓”模板：“ Here!”昊霆右手捏着“小草莓”将它粘贴在正确的模板里。昊霆：“小 小  Strawberry  here。”老师：“哇！昊霆太厉害了，找到小草莓了，接下来呢？”昊霆从地板上捡起“大草莓“图片，他回头看着老师笑，老师：“昊霆要把草莓放在哪里呀？”昊霆直接将小草莓放回正确的模版中。老师：“昊霆刚才贴的是什么呀？”昊霆：“Small one。”老师：“对的，这个是小小的草莓 ，最小的草莓放好了，现在中间还有一个不大不小的草莓在哪里呢？”昊霆低头看看地板，他弯腰从地板上捡起“草莓”举高对着老师：“This one 。”昊霆说完将草莓放回模板中，完成拼图后他笑着看着老师！
interpretation: 昊霆在《草莓长大了》活动中，能够根据老师的口头指令“小草莓放在哪里呢？”识别“小草莓”并且将“小草莓”正确放回模板中，他也能用自己的语言介绍不同大小的草莓：“Small small one、小 小  Strawberry  here。”同时昊霆还能根据模板的提示正确将三个不同大小的草莓拼贴完整，”向我们展现他对“大小”这一数学概念的初步认知。

title: Painting a class birthday cake
description:
After  listening to the story, “Bunny bakes”, Jordan participated in a collaborative art project with his friend where they worked together to paint and decorate a giant birthday cake. This hands-on activity provided an opportunity for them to develop social skills and creativity in a fun and engaging way. 
Throughout the process, Jordan demonstrated teamwork and cooperation together with his friend as they shared the art supplies- paintbrushes, and paint pots. He practiced patience and turn-taking when using the art supplies, showing his ability to share when his friend requested for the paintbrush which he was using. After Jordan passed his friend the paintbrush, he commented, “Later you give me, okay?” His friend replied, “Okay. Thank you.”  “See, Teacher Michelle, I give Liam the paintbrush.” Then he walked to the table to take another paintbrush from the paint pot.
interpretation: It was wonderful to see Jordan communicating with his friend to negotiate choices, while expressing his creativity while contributing to a shared masterpiece. Beyond artistic expression, this activity helped to reinforce important developmental skills such as fine motor control, decision-making, and problem-solving. By working towards a common goal, Jordan gained a sense of accomplishment and pride in his collective effort together with his friend. This activity not only nurtured his creativity but also strengthened his ability to speak up and collaborate—valuable skills that will continue to benefit him in both social and learning environments.

title: 夹毛绒球
description:
描述：
        教师向幼儿展示毛绒球，夹子和鸡蛋托，邀请幼儿进行夹毛绒球的活动。教师鼓励幼儿将盒子里面的毛绒球夹起来，放进鸡蛋托里面。
         若熙坐在桌子前，她用右手拿起桌子上的夹子，将夹子伸进装有毛绒球的盒子里面，她的拇指和其它的四指做夹的动作，将毛绒球从盒子里面夹出来放进鸡蛋托里面。教师对若熙说：“若熙你的小手很有力气哦，能够夹起毛绒球并放进托盘里。”若熙复述教师的话“有力气。”若熙用同样的方法再次夹毛绒球，直至将所有的毛绒球都夹到蛋托里面。她对教师说：“张老师，你看。”教师回应若熙说道：“你又成功了，很棒哦！”
interpretation:
诠释：

      若熙在活动中，能够用夹子将毛绒球放进托盘里，展现良好的抓握动作以及手部肌肉的力量，若熙也能够用简单的句子与教师进行互动，展现出良好的语言能力。

title: 观察动物的牙齿
description:
幼儿正在参与”好奇乐“领域《动物的牙齿》教学活动，教师出示狮子、大象、老虎、猴子、鳄鱼等动物的牙齿图片，鼓励幼儿观察图片并说说他们看到了什么，什么动物的牙齿是尖尖的，长长的。
雨蒽看着桌子上的图片，用小手指着图片说：“我害怕鳄鱼。”老师问她：“雨蒽那你看看鳄鱼的牙齿是什么样子的呢？”雨蒽看了看图片说：“鳄鱼的牙齿是尖尖的。”老师又问她：“那你再看看其他动物的牙齿还有尖尖的吗？”她又继续看着图片，用小手指向老化的图片说：“老师，老虎的牙齿是尖尖的。”老师对她说：“雨蒽你真棒！”

title: Painting a class birthday cake
description:
After  listening to the story, “Bunny bakes”, Eloise participated in a collaborative art project with her friend where they worked together to paint and decorate a giant birthday cake. This hands-on activity provided an opportunity for them to develop social skills and creativity in a fun and engaging way. 
Throughout the process, Eloise demonstrated teamwork and cooperation together with her friend as they shared the art supplies- paintbrushes, and paint pots. She practiced patience and turn-taking when using the art supplies, showing her ability to share when her friend requested for the paintbrush which she was using. After Eloise passed her friend the paintbrush, she commented to her teacher, “Give Caca brush.” Then she walked to the table to take another paintbrush from the paint pot. After some time when Eloise wanted the paintbrush which her friend was using, she pointed at the paintbrush and went, “Caca please.” So her teacher helped her repeat her request asking if he could share his paintbrush with her.
interpretation: It was wonderful to see Eloise beginning to communicate with her friend to negotiate choices, while expressing her creativity while contributing to a shared masterpiece. Beyond artistic expression, this activity helped to reinforce important developmental skills such as fine motor control, decision-making, and problem-solving. By working towards a common goal, Eloise gained a sense of accomplishment and pride in her collective effort together with her friend. This activity not only nurtured her creativity but also strengthened her ability to speak up and collaborate—valuable skills that will continue to benefit her in both social and learning environments.

title: 小水滴找朋友
description:
在本次活动中，老师化身“水精灵”，用趣味手偶和魔法口袋吸引幼儿兴趣，引导他们先触摸感知物品的“软软”和“硬硬”，再将材料轻轻放入水中观察“浮起来”或“沉下去”。孩子们通过直观的感官操作与对比，发现不同材质的特性（如木头浮水、石头下沉、海绵吸水），在玩水游戏中自然建立对材料属性的初步认知，同时激发观察与提问的科学探索兴趣，为后续学习奠定基础。

溪溪在活动中表现出极大的兴趣。她首先选择了一个塑料香蕉模型，将其放入水中，发现它沉到了水底。她显得有些惊讶，很快又拿起一个木块玩具放入水里，观察到木块浮在水面。她皱起眉头，疑惑地问：“为什么香蕉很小还是沉下去？”随后，她主动尝试更多材料进行测试，发现手指玩偶也能漂浮，而积木则有些沉下去。在教师的引导下，溪溪开始思考并提出新的问题：“是不是硬硬的会沉下去？”教师向幼儿介绍浮力和密度的概念，溪溪认真听讲，并尝试用自己的语言复述：“硬硬的玩具在下面，软软的会在上面。”她在实验过程中不断尝试不同材质的玩具在水中的状态，并与同伴分享自己的发现，表现出较强的探索精神和学习兴趣。
interpretation: 溪溪在活动中展现了良好的自主探索能力，可以选择不同的材料去尝试和观察。较少受到干扰，能投入持续的注意、精力旺盛并坚持不懈的完成。过程中表现出快乐、自信、好奇和积极的互动。主动提出问题，探索后会用自己的语言尝试解释：“香蕉硬硬在下面，玩偶软软在上面。”展现了初步的科学探究能力。

learning_goals.title: Develop an understanding of the physical properties of materials through exploration (e.g. water play to understand how water flows differently through funnels etc.) 通过探索活动，如：观察水流动等，发展幼儿对材料属性的认识。

domains.title: The Thinking and Communicating Self 思考与沟通

title: 哪一条最长
description:
幼儿在参与”数学脑“领域的”哪一条最长“的教学活动，教师引导幼儿画出的最长的一条线，可以象征兔妈妈对小兔子的爱是最长、最深的，就像故事《猜猜我有多爱你》里一样，爱是无法衡量的。并引导幼儿用语言描述，比如：“兔妈妈的爱就像这条最长的线一样。”这样能帮助幼儿用具体的形象表达抽象的情感概念。
在活动中，书雅使用铅笔在纸上画出了五条线。她画完后，仔细地用眼睛观察，并用手指一条条地数出来，边数边轻声念道：“一、二、三、四、五。” 确保自己数得正确后，她高兴地向老师展示自己的作品。老师问她： “书雅，你画了几条线呢？”书雅认真数着线条回答： “一、二、三、四、五！五条！”并伸出五根手指比划着。老师接着问： “那这几条线里面，哪一条最长？”书雅指着最长的一条说： “我喜欢这条，它最长！”老师说： “哇，那这条线可以代表什么呢？”书雅思考了一下说： “兔妈妈爱小兔子！很长很长！”老师微笑点头： “书雅真棒！最长的线像妈妈的爱一样，一直延续下去！”
interpretation: 书雅能清楚地感知数量概念，并正确数出五条线，说明她对数的稳定性已有较好掌握。她能主动关注线条长度，并能够区分“最长”这一特征，表明她对物体大小和比较的理解较为清晰。她能够完整表达自己画的内容，并运用手势辅助表达“5”的概念，体现了良好的语言表达能力。在交流过程中，她能用最长的线象征兔妈妈的爱，展现了抽象思维能力和想象力。

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（听）- 听指令：能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。
语言学习成果（说）- 交谈：尝试用华语与人交谈。
语言学习成果（写）- 写前准备：喜欢涂涂画画，能画出较直、横的线，基本能控制笔的方向。
一次计算一个物品，准确地累计到5个或以上。

title: This is Me
description:
The children were introduced to journal writing, and the question to reflect on was, "Can you draw your face and tell me what makes it special?" Engracia began making marks and drawing shapes. While drawing her hair, she said, “Teacher Chari, this is my Elsa hair.” I replied, “That is nice hair.” Engracia smiled and continued drawing her face. Once she was done, I asked, “Could you share with me what you drew?” Engracia shared, “This is my hair, Elsa hair. I like Elsa.” I asked her again, “Is that what makes you special?” She answered yes. Engracia continued sharing what she drew, saying things like, “My mouth is here,” “This is my face,” and “I like my hair.”

During the activity, Engracia showed great interest and enthusiasm in drawing her face portrait using lines and shapes and sharing her thoughts. While sharing, she could communicate her thoughts and feelings about her face portrait and how much she likes Elsa.

learning_goals.title: Use letter-like shapes, symbols and letters to convey meaning.

title: Toy Hunt
description:
The word "matching" was introduced to the children, and examples were given to help them understand the concept. A box with different toys was presented to the children, and they were invited to find the toy that matched the one they chose. Kyan chose the pink tube and began looking for its match. He walked around the class, focused on finding the other pink tube. I asked him, "What is the colour of your toy?" and Kyan replied, "Pink." I told Kyan to look for a pink toy to encourage him, and even his friends cheered for him, saying, "You can do it!" Kyan smiled and eagerly continued looking for the pink tube. He walked near the cubby, looked up, and found the other pink tube. Kyan said, "I found it." I asked Kyan if they matched, and he put the two pink tubes together, saying, "Yes."

Kyan successfully matched two pink tubes, demonstrating his ability to recognise and match identical objects. Kyan experienced feelings of focus and determination as he worked to find the matching toy. Additionally, the encouragement from his peers, as they cheered him on with phrases like "You can do it!" helped foster a sense of support and positive social interaction.

learning_goals.title: Match identical objects or pictures.

title: Toy Hunt
description:
The word "matching" was introduced to the children, and examples were given to help them understand the concept. A box with different toys was presented to the children, and they were invited to find the toy that matched the one they chose. Aydin chose the green bottle and began looking for its match. Aydin walked around the class, searching for the other green bottle in each corner. When Aydin couldn't find the bottle, I asked him if he needed help from his friends. Aydin replied, "No," and continued searching. Aydin was having a hard time finding the bottle, so I gave him a hint, saying, “Is it in the box?” referring to the wooden box. Aydin looked for the wooden box, and when he found it, he looked inside. With a smile, Aydin looked at me and said, “I found it!” I asked Aydin if the bottles matched or were the same, and he replied, “Yes.”

Aydin successfully matched two identical green bottles, demonstrating his ability to recognise and match identical objects showing an understanding of the concept of matching. Aydin effectively communicated his thoughts and feelings throughout the activity. He expressed his excitement and achievement by smiling and saying, “I found it!” Additionally, Aydin demonstrated persistence and independence by continuing to search for the matching bottle, even when he faced difficulty. His clear verbal communication and actions showed his ability to express his ideas and feelings effectively with others.

learning_goals.title: Match identical objects or pictures.

title: 胶带填色画
description:
艺术元素：颜色 

活动目标：
1.幼儿通过使用多种颜色搭配，感受色彩美，感知色彩的碰撞和搭配。
2.鼓励幼儿能够自己撕胶带，锻炼幼儿手指精细动作。 

活动过程：
教师事先准备好胶带纸，并引导幼儿将胶带贴在画纸上，设计出独特的图案或线条。随后，教师鼓励幼儿使用绘画滚筒或颜料刷，将自己喜欢的颜色均匀涂抹在画纸表面，包括覆盖胶带的部分。待颜料完全干透后，教师引导幼儿小心撕下胶带，欣赏作品中留下的空白图案，并与周围色彩形成的鲜明对比，感知色彩的碰撞，培养幼儿对艺术的兴趣。

learning_goals.title: Foster an interest in art (drawing, painting, modelling, collage work etc.) 通过美术活动，如：粗蜡笔涂鸦、水彩画、撕贴画、拼贴等，培养幼儿对艺术的兴趣。

title: 刷牙的先后顺序
description:
幼儿在参与“数学脑”领域的“刷牙的先后顺序”的教学活动，教师引导幼儿通过排序游戏的方式更进一步掌握刷牙顺序，幼儿按照自己的理解排列刷牙顺序，实际操作刷牙步骤排序游戏图卡，老师再进行讲解与调整。让幼儿在轻松的氛围中学习刷牙顺序，养成良好的刷牙习惯，同时提升幼儿的逻辑思维和表达能力。
在刷牙步骤排序活动中，老师问：“雨蒽，我们一起来看看刷牙的顺序吧！你能帮老师把这些卡片按顺序排好吗？” 在老师的引导下，雨蒽专注地观察卡片，依次放好：先是牙刷，接着是牙膏，再放上挤牙膏的图片，随后是刷牙，最后是漱口的图片。老师微笑着鼓励她：“我们一起说一遍，牙刷、牙膏、挤牙膏、刷牙、漱口。” 雨蒽看着排列好的顺序，跟着老师轻声重复。老师进一步问：“那你会不会认真刷牙呢？” 她开心地点点头，笑着说：“我要好好刷牙！”
interpretation: 雨蒽能够正确按照刷牙步骤进行排序，说明她对日常生活习惯有清晰的认知，并能理解先后顺序。她的排序清晰、合理，能够准确表达刷牙的先后顺序，展现了良好的认知能力。她能准确用简洁的语言描述刷牙的步骤，展现了条理清晰的表达能力。

learning_goals.title: 语言学习成果（听）- 听指令：能完全理解1个口头指示并完成任务。
语言学习成果（说）- 交谈：尝试用华语与人交谈。
把三个或更多东西排序：尺寸（如：从小到大）。

title: 阳光下的积木探险
description:
今天上午，教师带幼儿们组织了一次“阳光下的积木探险”户外活动，目的是通过让孩子们观察形状和颜色丰富的积木，激发他们对周围世界的好奇心，提升他们的观察力与语言表达能力。通过在阳光下观察，孩子们不仅能感知到不同颜色和形状的变化，还能学会从不同角度进行观察，发现更多细节。

在教师向小朋友们介绍不同的积木时，凯文不时向前走几步，试图靠近教师。当教师鼓励大家在阳光下自由探索自己喜欢的积木时，他高高的举起了自己的手，选取了一个半圆形的黄色透明积木。接着，他拿起积木放在眼前，眯起眼睛，一会儿透过积木看向天空，一会儿低头看向草地。过一会儿，他笑着跑到老师身边，举起积木指着说：“Yellow！”教师微笑着回应道：“凯文观察得真仔细，这是黄色。”他听后笑着说道：“黄色、黄色。”随后，凯文又主动挑选了不同形状和颜色的积木，继续透过阳光观察着周围的环境。
interpretation: 在“阳光下的积木探险”的活动中，凯文能够长时间投入到活动中，表现出强烈的好奇和积极互动能力，例如：他积极选择与探索不同的积木，通过积木观察天空和草地，并积极与教师分享等。

learning_goals.title: Foster interest and wonder in a well-planned environment通过周围环境和互动，培养好奇心和主动探索精神。

title: 小鱼绕线
description:
本次活动通过给小鱼缠线，发展幼儿的手眼协调能力和精细动作。教师提供小鱼模型和线，引导幼儿观察小鱼的形状，并提问：“小鱼少了什么呢？”随后，教师示范绕线的方法，鼓励幼儿尝试，并在遇到困难时主动调整或寻求帮助。

当教师展示小鱼模型时，她仔细观察后，兴奋地拿起绳子开始尝试绕线。她用一只手拿着小鱼模型，另一只手的食指和拇指捏起绳子一边开始往小鱼身上缠线。刚开始，她的手指动作不太灵活，线容易松开或打结，她皱眉，显得有些困惑。但她并没有放弃，而是耐心地尝试调整，并主动看向教师说：“帮我。”教师微笑道：“试着一只手固定线，另一只手慢慢绕。”在教师的引导下，語宸学会了一手固定绳子，一手慢慢绕线，使绳子贴合小鱼的形状。当她成功绕完一圈时，她露出自豪的笑容，并继续尝试将绳子绕得更均匀。教师问：“要再绕多一点吗？”她点头回答：“要。”她点头继续，最终举起小鱼自豪地说：“我做好了！”
interpretation: 語宸在活动中展现了良好的自主探索能力，她能够主动尝试绕线，并在遇到困难时寻找解决办法。过程中能投入持续的注意、精力旺盛并坚持不懈的完成。展现了快乐、活力、好奇和积极的互动。她通过不断调整和实践，提高了自己的绕线技巧，在过程中锻炼了手眼协调能力，能用拇指和食指抓线并调整绕法。她遇到困难时会主动尝试和求助，展现出专注力和耐心，并乐于完成挑战。

learning_goals.title: Develop eye-hand coordination  (roll a ball, pick up soft blocks and stack, self-feed, put simple things together and take them apart) 发展手眼协调能力，如：滚球，叠放软积木，喂食，把简单玩具连在一起再拆开等）。

title: Threading Straws
description: Vikranth held a pipe cleaner in one hand and a short straw in the other. He examined the straw before placing it near the pipe cleaner. The pipe cleaner passed through the straw, and Vikranth pulled it out from the other end. He then picked up another colored straw and repeated the same process. After a few tries, he pulled the straw but stopped just before it reached the end, leaving the straw threaded onto the pipe cleaner as he continued with the rest of the threading.
interpretation:
When Vikranth picks up the straw and aligns it with the pipe cleaner, he is practicing early hand-eye coordination, a crucial skill at this age. He also demonstrates an understanding of when to stop pulling the straw just before it reaches the end, leaving it threaded onto the pipe cleaner. This indicates growing control over his hand movements and a developing awareness of the task's requirements.


Additionally, this activity supports the development of his pincer grip, finger strength, and hand coordination. These skills are essential for more complex tasks and will continue to evolve as Vikranth engages in similar activities.

title: Threading Straws
description: Mikayla held a pipe cleaner in one hand and a short straw in the other. She carefully aligned the straw with the pipe cleaner and threaded it through. Afterward, Mikayla picked up another colored straw and threaded it onto the pipe cleaner, pushing the first straw inward as she did so. She continued this process, successfully threading more straws onto the pipe cleaner until it was completely filled.
interpretation:
Mikayla is practicing her hand-eye coordination, as she carefully aligns and threads the straws onto the pipe cleaner. She demonstrates hand-eye coordination as she grasped the pipe cleaner with one hand and threading the straw with the other. Additionally, the action of pushing the first straw inward while threading the second reflects increasing control over her hand movements and a growing understanding of spatial awareness.   


This task also supports the strengthening of her pincer grip and finger dexterity which are essential skills for more complex tasks in future.

title: Moving objects together
description: Abby worked with a friend to move the ball into the tire. She held the ball on the opposite side of where her friend was standing, and together they began walking toward the tire. Initially, they walked in the wrong direction, heading to the side instead of toward the tire. After adjusting their course, they found the right path and moved toward the tire as a team. At the end of the activity, Abby gave a high five to her partner, celebrating their teamwork and success.
interpretation: As Abby works with a partner to move the ball into the tire, she is practicing coordination, cooperation, and teamwork. By grasping the ball with both hands and adjusting her position to align with her partner, she is learning to move in sync and coordinate her actions. The process of adjusting their direction to reach the tire demonstrates early problem-solving skills and the ability to collaborate effectively. The high five at the end highlights her social and emotional development, as she engages with her peer and celebrates their shared success.

title: Painting a class birthday cake
description:
After  listening to the story, “Bunny bakes”, Louka participated in a collaborative art project with his friend where they worked together to paint and decorate a giant birthday cake. This hands-on activity provided an opportunity for them to develop social skills and creativity in a fun and engaging way.

Throughout the process, Louka demonstrated teamwork and cooperation together with his friend as they shared the art supplies- paintbrushes, and paint pots. He practiced patience and turn-taking when using the colors which he wanted, showing his ability to request for the paintbrush which his friend was using. Louka went, “Eloise, may I have the blue please?” After his friend passed him the paintbrush, Louka thanked his friend.
interpretation: It was wonderful to see Louka communicating with his friend to negotiate choices, while expressing his creativity while contributing to a shared masterpiece. Beyond artistic expression, this activity helped to reinforce important developmental skills such as fine motor control, decision-making, and problem-solving. By working towards a common goal, Louka gained a sense of accomplishment and pride in his collective effort together with his friend. This activity not only nurtured his creativity but also strengthened his ability to speak up and collaborate—valuable skills that will continue to benefit him in both social and learning environments.

learning_goals.title: Foster interactions, attachment and relationships with adults and children 通过与成人和同伴的互动，建立良好的关系。

title: This Is The Way We Wear Our Shoes
description: Lavinha was exploring the self-help skills area when she picked up an orange pair of sandals. Looking at the teacher, she said, "Wear shoe." The teacher acknowledged her and encouraged her to sit down to put them on. At first, she struggled to figure out where to place her feet. After a few moments, the teacher gently guided her feet onto the soles of the sandals, and she then pushed her feet further in.
interpretation: Lavinha’s physical well-being is developing well, as she is showing interest in self-help skills like wearing shoes. Her ability to recognise the task and attempt it independently is a positive sign of her growing autonomy. However, she still requires assistance with coordinating her movements and positioning her feet correctly in the sandals. With continued practice and guidance, she will gradually develop the confidence and motor skills needed to complete the task on her own.

learning_goals.title: Foster personal care skills，hygiene and safety, healthy eating habits (hand washing, cleaning up, dressing，toileting, personal safety, eating a variety of food, etc.) 培养个人自理能力、卫生和基本的安全意识、良好的饮食习惯，如：餐前洗手、脱衣服、如厕、食用多样化的食物等。

title: Dropping ball
description: The educator placed the Peek-a-Shoe octopus in front of Miya and showed her different colored balls. Once a ball was placed on its hand, it would roll down to the end, where the educator would lift the covers one by one to reveal where the ball had landed. After observing this, Miya took a turn, dropping the ball into the octopus's hand and watching it roll down. It took her some time to figure out how to lift the covers to find where the ball had landed. To help her, the educator assisted by lifting each cover and encourage Miya to find the ball.
interpretation:
Through this activity, Miya developed an understanding of object permanence. She observed how the ball rolled down after being dropped into one of the octopus's hand openings and then located it in a different spot. This helped her realize how actions can cause different outcomes, such as when dropping the ball into two different openings.

By dropping the ball and lifting the shoes one by one to find it, Miya engaged in problem-solving through trial and error, learning to identify the correct shoe to reveal the ball's location. She then began intentionally dropping toys, repeatedly watching where the ball went and tracking its movement.

learning_goals.title: Foster understanding of cause and effect through engagement with toys, materials and books 通过玩有回馈动作的玩具（如：按压一个会嘎嘎叫的玩具）、探索材料（如：吹泡泡）和阅读书籍等活动，初步发展婴幼儿对于因果关系的感知。

title: Hello friend.
description: Miya was very observant of her surroundings, so the educator took the opportunity to help her learn more about her friends' names. The educator invited Miya to the wall where all the children's photos were displayed. Since Miya was still learning how to stand, the educator carefully took down a few of her friends' pictures and handed them to her. Miya began flipping through the photos, as if browsing through them. The educator then pointed to her own picture and asked, "Who is this?" Miya would point to herself and continue flipping through the three photos she had. The educator then asked Miya to find the photo of the friend sitting next to her, Elijah. After flipping through the photos, Miya found Elijah's photo and passed it to him, showing that she recognized which photo belonged to which friend.
interpretation: Miya has shown that she is beginning to assert herself more confidently and is actively participating in activities with her friends. She is also becoming increasingly aware of herself as a separate individual when interacting with others. Miya demonstrates growing independence by completing tasks on her own, showing a sense of autonomy. Additionally, she expresses affection toward others beyond her primary caregiver, smiling and happily playing with her friends. This indicates that she is forming emotional connections and engaging in social behaviors with her friends, guided by the support of her educator.
